                                          staged job: a resume copy or the empty live file); never empty
  ```
  `key` is `sha256(kind \0 repo \0 ref)` truncated — a hash, not a path built from a branch.
  `PI_SESSIONS_DIR` has **no default**; unset means the feature is unavailable.
  **Since issue #643 the worker also reads the per-job copy while the job runs**, from its offset each poll, to
  publish the live transcript (`INT-LIVE-TRANSCRIPT-STREAM`); a non-resume job's copy is an empty live file with no
  key. That read writes nothing back, judges nothing for resuming and changes no edge of this contract: promotion
  still happens only on a completed exit, through the `lstat` checks below.
- **Read path**, host-side, fail-open at the first miss, every miss a named cold start: key resolves ->
  **the key's own name `lstat`s as a real directory** -> canonical file exists ->
  **`lstat` says regular file, not a symlink** -> size <= `PI_SESSION_MAX_BYTES`
  -> mtime within `PI_SESSIONS_TTL_DAYS` -> stamped `venue` matches the job's resolved backend -> stamped
  `pi-version` matches the job image's label ->
  `resume-chain` below `PI_SESSION_MAX_RESUME_CHAIN` -> stored `context` occupancy below
  `PI_SESSION_MAX_CONTEXT_PCT` -> first parsed line is a `{"type":"session"}` header
  -> that header's `timestamp` is within `PI_SESSION_MAX_AGE_DAYS` -> no compaction entry has an empty
  summary -> copy into the per-job dir. A cold start stages a **0-byte file** rather
  than nothing. The order is the contract, not an implementation detail, because the first miss is the one
  that names itself: the shape check stays AHEAD of the age bound so a damaged transcript reads as
  `unparseable` rather than as a lineage that aged out, and the age bound is the only arm that reads
  anything from the header beyond its `type`. The chain bound sits BEHIND `pi-version` and AHEAD of the
  header read, because it is a sidecar read like `pi-version` and because it is the one arm that asks
  about the lineage rather than the file, so refusing on it need not pull a transcript that may be
  megabytes. What that costs is stated rather than left to be found: a transcript both chain-exhausted and
  corrupt reports the chain, and the corruption is deferred by exactly one run, since that cold start's own
  promotion resets the counter. The venue arm (#277) sits BEHIND every arm a venue move cannot cause (a file
  that is absent, not a regular file, too large or past its TTL is all of those on every venue) and AHEAD of
  both `pi-version` arms, which a venue move CAN cause, since image preflight is dispatched per venue and
  another venue may report another pi or none. Before it existed a venue move named itself as a version
  change.
- **An empty compaction is never resumed** (issue #535). pi replaces the turns a compaction folds away with
  its summary, so a transcript holding a compaction with no summary would resume without those turns, and
  nothing in the run would say so. The read path cold-starts it with `compaction-summary-empty`. The arm is
  always on, since it is not an operator's bound but a transcript that is not what it claims to be. It is
  LAST, because it is the only arm that reads past the header, so a damaged or aged-out transcript names
  itself first. It judges EVERY `{"type":"compaction"}` line, not only the last: a later compaction is built
  on the earlier summary, so an empty one anywhere is lost from every summary after it. A line that does not
  parse is skipped, as pi's own reader skips it.
  **What counts as empty** is what pi 0.99.1 writes when the runner's brake refuses the summary call, which
  pi records rather than rejects (the hard stop is `stopReason: "aborted"`, and pi fails a compaction only on
  `"error"` or `"length"`). Measured at the pin, with the token cap and with the cost cap, the summary is
  `""` when the cut fell on a user message, and `<history>` + `"\n\n---\n\n**Turn Context (split turn):**\n\n"`
  + `""` when it split a turn, where `<history>` is `""` when that call was refused too and
  `"No prior history."` when there was none. When a split turn has no new history, `<history>` is the
  previous compaction's summary, its own file lists and any split-turn marker included. pi then appends
  the files the folded turns read and changed, as a `<read-files>` block and then a `<modified-files>`
  block, either one absent when empty. So the check strips pi's lists from the END ONLY. When the entry's
  `details` hold `readFiles` and `modifiedFiles` as lists of strings, as pi records them, it rebuilds pi's
  exact suffix from them and takes it off only if the summary ends with it. Otherwise it falls back to
  taking a list when the text ends in its closer, from that list's last opener, the modified list and then
  the read list, each at most once. Either way nothing before the lists is searched, so a list the model
  quoted, or one inside a reused previous summary, stays. It then splits on the LAST split-turn marker and
  calls the summary empty when any part is blank after trimming. A summary that is missing or not a string
  is empty. The strip is linear and uses no regular expression. One residual stays, on the fallback only: a
  file path the model chose that holds a list header can move where the fallback cuts, since pi copies a
  tool call's path verbatim. With `details` present, which is every compaction pi itself writes, the exact
  suffix is not fooled by it. A resumed session built on one sees a `compactionSummary` message
  wrapping that text, then only the turns the compaction kept.
  **Why a cold start and not a refused job**: every other arm here is a named cold start, and only a
  completed run replaces the canonical transcript, so failing the job would fail every later job on the key
  too. The cold start loses nothing a resume would have kept, since the summary is the only copy of those
  turns pi would have handed over. **What reaches this arm in practice**: a run whose brake refused the
  summary stops with `token_budget`, `cost-cap` or `model-not-allowed` (a policy exit) and is never
  promoted, so the measured cause cannot land in the store by itself. The arm is for the same shape from a
  run that completed: a provider that answered a summary with no text, an extension's compaction with an
  empty summary, or a transcript promoted before this arm existed. The transcript is agent-written, so this
  is a check on what pi produced, not a bound an agent cannot get around.
- **The venue stamp** (issue #277): one backend name beside the transcript, naming the venue whose container
  wrote it. **A sidecar, NOT key material**: `DES-SESSION-KEY-IS-DERIVED-NOT-INDEXED` keeps the key a function
  of `(kind, repo, ref)`, and a venue in the key would fork a trigger moved between venues into a second
  lineage nothing ever sweeps; as a sidecar it gates the one lineage, and a move costs one cold start. The
  job's venue is resolved exactly as the registry dispatches it (`resolveBackendName`: `run.backend`, else
  `PI_BACKENDS[0]`) and compared by exact string. **An ABSENT stamp is the literal `local`, never the
  deployment default**: every transcript written before the stamp ran on `local`, and the default is a
  setting that can move under it. Absence is decided by `lstat` and ENOENT alone, so a dangling symlink at
  the name is not absence. **A stamp that exists but cannot be read** (not a regular file, empty, oversized,
  unreadable) matches no venue, and a job whose venue cannot be resolved never resumes. **The write order
  is the contract**: removing a stamp does not invalidate it, since absence reads as `local`, so every
  promotion first writes `(pending)` -- parentheses are outside the backend-name charset -- through the
  link-safe temp-and-rename, FATALLY and BEFORE the transcript swap, then writes the real stamp immediately
  after the swap and before `pi-version`. A failed sentinel write swaps nothing and reports `promote-failed`;
  a failed post-swap stamp leaves the sentinel, which cold-starts everywhere rather than attributing a
  transcript to the wrong venue. **The resolve path re-checks the stamp after its copy**, because the read
  and the copy are not under the promotion lock: a stamp that no longer names the job's venue empties the
  staged copy and cold-starts; a fault while emptying it removes the staged directory, best effort, so a
  `null` resolve leaves nothing readable under the job dir unless that removal fails too. What
  `venue-changed` does not distinguish is stated rather than hidden: it also names a leftover sentinel from
  an interrupted promotion, an unreadable stamp, and a
  SAME-venue promotion whose sentinel is in place when another job reads or re-checks the stamp (that job
  cold-starts once), exactly as `pi-version-changed` already covers an unreadable version stamp.
  **The resolve path stages the transcript from ONE DESCRIPTOR, and re-checks the name after it** (issues
  #336 and #375). It opens the canonical transcript once, compares that descriptor's `dev:ino:size:mtime`
  with what the gates judged, streams the staged copy off the same descriptor bounded by the judged size,
  and then asks the name again: still a real directory, still this venue, still the judged transcript.
  NEITHER HALF SUBSUMES THE OTHER, and each was found by removing it. The descriptor answers a swap that
  lands during the copy, because bytes read from it cannot come from a file that replaced the name
  afterwards; that is what closes the A, B, A round trip this entry once stated as a residual the identity
  re-check could only shrink (measured against a live second process, 90 seconds each side of one harness: 23
  of 654 resumes staged an attacker's transcript before, 0 of 115 after). The by-path re-check answers a swap that lands BEFORE the open,
  since every gate above ran by path, so a link planted after the first of those lstats has the whole ladder
  judge the attacker's files and the descriptor then agrees with them; it is also what keeps the venue arm
  reachable, because a promotion that wrote its `(pending)` sentinel and has not yet swapped moves no
  identity at all. Inside that re-check the order is the one #277 set: the key's own SHAPE first, since a
  name that is no longer a directory is neither a venue move nor a swap; then the venue, because a
  cross-venue promotion trips both and `venue-changed` names WHY where `transcript-replaced` only says
  something moved; then the transcript's identity, which catches a same-venue promotion the stamp cannot
  see. A promotion renames a freshly created file into place, so the inode moves on every completed swap.
  **A process killed inside the promotion lock** leaks the lock, as any kill there always has, and until
  issue #336 later promotions then reported `locked` until the reaper swept the key, which for two shapes it
  never did. Killed between the sentinel and the real stamp,
  it also leaves the sentinel, and the key cold-starts on every venue meanwhile; killed after the stamp, the
  stamped venue keeps resuming. **A leaked lock is now recovered by the next promotion** (issue #336), not left for an
  operator: a lock older than `LOCK_STALE_MS` (one hour) is taken over once, with its age on its own
  `session_lock_stale_taken` line, logged only after the retake CREATE succeeded because a rival sweeper can
  win the recreate race. An hour is an assertion about storage rather than a derivation, since
  `PI_SESSION_MAX_BYTES=0` leaves no configured bound to derive from, and it is generous on purpose: too
  short steals a LIVE writer's lock, where too long only delays recovery on a key nobody is watching. The
  age is read with `lstat`, so a dangling link planted at that name is taken over rather than wedging the
  key for good, which it did under an exclusive create. **What a takeover costs when it is wrong is stated rather than
  softened**: two holders then run, BOTH report `promoted`, the last rename wins so one run's turns are
  silently discarded, and the chain counter is incremented twice for one conversation. Four residuals stay
  open. The release unlinks by PATH, so after a takeover the original holder's release deletes the new
  holder's lock. The staleness read is a check-then-act: the lock is lstat'ed, judged, and then unlinked by
  path without re-validating, so a lock created in that window is removed on the strength of its
  predecessor's mtime -- the same window `triggers-file.mjs` concedes. The lock's mtime is its CREATE time
  and is never refreshed, so the bound is on a promotion's total duration rather than on a holder's
  liveness, and `PI_SESSION_MAX_BYTES=0` leaves that duration unbounded. And a lock whose mtime is in the
  FUTURE, by clock skew or by a hand, is never stale, so under `PI_SESSIONS_TTL_DAYS=0`, where the reaper
  does not run either, such a key is wedged until someone removes the file. A takeover on a key two venues
  share can also leave one venue's transcript under the other's stamp. **Two
  triggers on one key that name different venues** replace each other's transcript and so cold-start on
  every alternation; that is the cost of keeping the venue out of the key, and it is the right way round,
  since the alternative resumes one venue's conversation in the other. Three residuals, one of them narrowed: two complete promotions from
  different venues inside one copy window (A, B, A) leave the STAMP matching again, and the venue re-check
  cannot see the round trip, but the identity re-check does, because each swap renames a fresh inode into
  place. What survives is narrower and is stated rather than claimed closed. **A SWAP is what this
  catches**, which is what a promotion performs; a rewrite IN PLACE that restores the file's size and mtime
  keeps every field of the identity and is not caught, measured. An inode NUMBER can also be reused, since
  the swapped-away inode is freed by its own rename, so two promotions inside one copy window whose second
  lands on a recycled number with the same size and mtime compare equal; that one is filesystem-dependent
  and was NOT reproducible on APFS, which hands out strictly increasing numbers, so it is a residual on
  filesystems that recycle rather than a general one. The sidecars are each read
  at their own instant and the identity covers the transcript only. **The reaper keys on the transcript's mtime, and falls back to the key DIRECTORY's own mtime
  when there is no transcript to key on** (issue #336), which is how a key whose first promotion died before
  the swap is swept at all rather than skipped on every pass forever. ENOENT alone takes that fallback: an
  EIO or an EACCES means the reaper could not ASK, and a reaper that treats "could not ask" as "old" deletes
  on a transient fault. **The reaper `lstat`s each entry FIRST** (issue #375), so nothing is
  judged THROUGH a link: an entry that is not a real directory is left where it stands and said, as
  `session_not_reaped {key, reason: "key-not-a-directory"}`. Until then a link whose target held a readable
  transcript was judged on that target's mtime and removed once it aged, which took the sweep's decision
  from a file outside the store entirely. It is a VERDICT event rather than `session_reaper_skipped`,
  which `OQ-007` reserves for what a pass could not establish. No link's TARGET was ever at risk either
  way: `rmSync` does not follow a symlink, measured, so it removes the link and leaves the target and its
  contents. `PI_SESSIONS_TTL_DAYS=0` is unchanged and still sweeps nothing at all, deliberately, because
  it is an explicit operator instruction and what makes a wedged key recoverable there is the stale-lock
  takeover rather than this. **Only a key-shaped name is judged** (issue #645): a name that is not 32 lower-case
  hex characters (`SESSION_KEY_PATTERN`, derived from `session-key.mjs`'s `KEY_LENGTH`) is never removed, whatever
  its age or type. A name starting with `.` is skipped silently, since that is where the store's own siblings live
  (the checkpoint store's default home is `<PI_SESSIONS_DIR>/.checkpoints`); any other non-key name is said once
  per pass as `session_not_reaped {key, reason: "not-a-key"}`. Before it, an aged non-key directory reached the
  directory-mtime fallback and was removed whole. A `PI_CHECKPOINTS_DIR` equal to the store, holding it, or below one of
  its key-shaped names is refused at load, since the two sweeps would then delete each other's folders.
  **What the fallback widens is stated**: a transcript-less key directory was
  previously never swept, so anything inside one now goes with it, including files an operator put there;
  and the lockless-sweep race below, which this contract used to state only for an EXPIRED key, now reaches
  any long-lived transcript-less key, where the cost is the whole key rather than a momentarily missing
  stamp. The reaper takes no lock and removes a key in one recursive walk, so a
  promotion landing on an EXPIRED key during its own sweep could, for a moment, leave that transcript
  without its stamp, which reads as `local`; and a worker older than #277 sharing a `PI_SESSIONS_DIR`
  neither reads nor writes the stamp, so every worker on a shared store must run a release carrying it
  before a second venue is blessed.
- **The chain counter**: an integer file beside the transcript, written immediately after the swap and
  under the same promotion lock, so it can never describe a transcript older than the one now in place.
  **It counts the HOST'S DELIVERIES**, incremented whenever the host handed this key's transcript to a
  container and reset to `0` when it did not. That is a correction, and the reason it matters is the whole
  security of this bound: it counted the CONTAINER's `resumed` first, on the reasoning that a transcript pi
  declined to continue extended nothing. The agent owns `/session`, so it chooses what pi makes of the
  file, and a transcript carrying a valid header with its payload on lines pi's parser DROPS is delivered
  every run while pi reports zero messages -- so the counter reset every run and the bound never fired.
  Measured against the pinned pi, not reasoned about. The host's own decision to hand the file over is the
  one fact in this exchange that nothing inside the container can influence, and it is what this counts.
  **Maintained whether or not a bound is set**, because a counter that starts when the knob does is a bound
  that does nothing for its first N runs, and an operator setting `3` against a lineage already forty deep
  would get no refusal at all. **A missing or unreadable counter is a chain of zero**, the opposite polarity
  to the age bound and deliberately: every key predating the file has none, and reading absence as
  exhaustion would cold-start an entire store the day the bound was set. **The reset needs a COMPLETED
  run**: only a completed exit promotes, so a lineage whose runs keep failing stays cold rather than
  resuming, which is the safe direction and the one an operator should expect.
- **The context sidecar**: `<tokens> <window> <provider>/<model>`, written under the same lock immediately
  after the swap, from the reading the container reported on its exit line
  (`INT-RUNNER-EXIT-CODE-PROTOCOL`). Both numbers rather than a precomputed percentage, so a refusal can be
  read against what it was judged by, and **the model stamped beside them because a key carries none**: a
  key is `(kind, repo, ref)`, two triggers on one issue may name different models, and the same token count
  is 78% of a 32k window and 2.5% of a 1M one. A reading stamped with a DIFFERENT model is not a reading
  about this one and is ignored; unknown on either side stays usable, so a deployment that names no model
  per trigger keeps the bound it had. **A run that RESUMED and measured nothing leaves the previous reading
  in place**, since the transcript it promoted is the old one extended and the last real measurement is the
  closest true statement available -- a zero would read as "the context emptied", which cannot have
  happened. **A COLD START CLEARS it**, and that is a correction: keeping it there turned one high reading
  into a key that refused itself forever, because the gate cold-started on a stale number and the cold
  start left the same number behind for the next run to read. Nothing released it either, since every
  promotion refreshes the transcript's mtime and neither the TTL gate nor the reaper can reach an actively
  used key. **Anything not readable as two positive integers is NO MEASUREMENT**, and the gate passes on no
  measurement rather than guessing. The rejected fallback is on the record: `bytes` against the model's
  `contextWindow` needs a bytes-to-tokens calibration this project does not have, and `bytes` is the whole
  branch INCLUDING what compaction folded away, so it over-reads exactly past the threshold the bound
  exists for -- it would fire hardest on the sessions that had just become safe. **The number is
  container-reported**, at the same trust level as `turns` and `tokens`; the residual is `OQ-003`.
- **Every read in a key directory is an `lstat` first, regular files only, and every sidecar write goes
  through a rename.** The transcript has been guarded this way since the feature shipped and the
  sidecars are held to it rather than being the exception, including `pi-version`, which predates them and
  was the last to inherit both halves (issue #336): its WRITE was plain until then, so it followed a link
  planted at that name, and a failure there after the swap reported `promote-failed` for a promotion that
  landed. Neither is true any more, and there is no longer an exception to state.
  **The key DIRECTORY is checked too, and that was the one shape the lstat-per-name rule could not see**
  (issue #375). A key directory that is itself a symlink is followed like any other path component, so every
  lstat above resolves through it and lands wherever it points: measured before the fix, a link planted at
  the derived path made a resolve return `resumed` from a transcript outside the store, and a promotion write
  `current.jsonl`, `pi-version`, `venue` and `resume-chain` through it. Both edges now `lstat` the key's own
  name and refuse anything that is not a real directory, with the token `key-not-a-directory`; the reaper
  does the same, so nothing is judged through a link either. THE FINAL COMPONENT ONLY: `PI_SESSIONS_DIR` and
  its ancestors may legitimately be symlinks (macOS's own temp root is one), so a `realpath` or an ancestor
  walk would refuse a supported layout. The entry is refused, never removed: this store creates key
  directories and nothing else, so whatever stands at that name belongs to an operator or to an attacker, and
  a refusal an operator can read beats a sweep that deletes either. The store is host-only and never mounted,
  so this is not a container reaching in; what makes it worth the lines is that the directory NAME is derived
  rather than random, so anyone who knows the repository and the branch can compute the path and pre-create
  it. **The READ path answers the swap with a descriptor rather than a re-check**, and that is what makes
  the refusal above worth stating: the gates ran by path, so a by-path copy after them could stage bytes no
  gate judged, and re-checking by path could not see it -- an attacker who is a symlink DURING the copy and
  the original directory again before the re-check matched every arm (measured against a plain second process
  on the first draft, in the review round's own harness: 195 of 757 successful resumes staged the attacker's transcript and reported `resumed`).
  `resolveSession` now opens the canonical transcript ONCE, judges that descriptor's identity against what the
  gates saw, and streams the staged copy off it, so the bytes a job resumes come off the inode that was
  judged and a later swap can only make it refuse. That closes the A, B, A round trip this contract used to
  state as a residual the identity re-check could merely shrink.
  **The WRITE path cannot be closed the same way**, because there is no descriptor for a directory Node can
  write through: `promoteSession` re-checks the key directory under the lock and again after the swap, which
  removes the check-to-lock window and makes a later swap REPORTABLE, but a swap after the last check still takes the transcript and the sidecars to wherever the name points. A swap STILL STANDING when the post-swap check runs reports `key-not-a-directory` instead of `promoted: true`; one REVERTED before it -- the A, B, A -- is caught by a second check that compares the inode `rename` preserved on the transcript against what the canonical name holds afterwards, and reports `transcript-diverted` (issue #390). Both are DETECTION, not prevention: the bytes are already wherever the name pointed and nothing host-side can recall them without `openat`/`renameat`. What they buy is that the RECORD stops claiming a promotion that landed outside the store, which is the difference between a loud refusal and the silent no-op the constitution's own logging rule forbids.
  Three residuals stay, all needing the same precondition (write access to the store). A real directory
  pre-created by another user passes, since no ownership check is made (a store shared across hosts or worker
  uids would otherwise cold-start every key, and Windows has no uid). The promote window from the last
  check to the final sidecar write is unbounded without `*at` syscalls, which Node does not expose -- its
  cost, stated rather than implied, is the SIDECARS written outside the store (the transcript itself is
  covered by the identity comparison above), plus a lock stranded in the real key until the staleness
  takeover, and it is detected rather than prevented. And a swap that is put back for the DURATION OF A CHECK
  and re-applied afterwards defeats any check that resolves the name again: an A, B, A, B around the two
  post-rename checks reports `promoted: true` with the transcript outside the store, and if that key already
  held one, the next job RESUMES the old transcript rather than cold-starting, so the lost turn is invisible
  on both edges. Every path-based check has this shape, and closing it needs `openat`/`renameat` rather than
  a further check; a 45 second unsynchronised live race over 215,372 promotions against 105,888 swap cycles
  hit it 0 times, so it is a deterministic-window finding rather than a frequent one.

  One assumption this comparison adds, named because it is the first in this file to rest on it: that a
  `rename` PRESERVES the inode. It does on every filesystem this project supports, and `identityOf` elsewhere
  only ever compares one path against itself. On a filesystem that derives inode numbers from the path
  (SMB/CIFS without `serverino`, some FUSE), every promotion would refuse `transcript-diverted` and resume
  would stop working with a token that reads as an attack. That is the same class as the `O_EXCL` semantics
  the lock already assumes.
  `readFileSync` follows a link, which would decide a gate on some other file's contents; `writeFileSync` and `copyFileSync` follow one at the
  destination, which would turn a promotion into a truncating write of any worker-writable file. Writing a
  temp and renaming over the name replaces a link with a regular file and never opens its target. Sidecar
  reads are **size-bounded** for the same reason the transcript is: `PI_SESSION_MAX_BYTES` does not cover
  them, and reading a huge one costs wall clock on the job's own path before any container starts.
- **Which transcript ownership this contract assumes.** Every file in a key directory -- the transcript, all
  four sidecars, the lock and the in-flight copy -- is created and written by the **worker** user; nothing in
  a container ever writes there, and the store is never mounted. So the lock, its staleness takeover and the
  reaper assume only that the worker owns `PI_SESSIONS_DIR`. The one file whose ownership the worker does NOT
  control is the per-job `/session/current.jsonl`, written by the job user inside the container: promotion
  only ever READS it (`lstat`, then `copyFileSync`), so the assumption is that the worker can read a file the
  container wrote. Under rootless Podman without `--userns=keep-id` that user maps to a subordinate uid on
  the host and the assumption may not hold. **This has not been measured** (`OQ-037`, issue #345). If it does
  not hold the symptom is bounded and loud rather than a corrupt store: the read is refused before the lock
  is taken, so it is a named promotion refusal on every completed run.
- **Write path**, after a `completed` exit **only**: the same `lstat` and size checks on the container's
  output, then an atomic rename under the per-key lock. **The transcript's in-flight copy is named per
  writer** (issue #336): a fixed name was self-cleaning while the lock guaranteed one writer, and a shared
  one voids the atomicity the swap exists for the moment there can be two, since one writer's unlink removes
  the other's in-flight copy and whichever renames second can place a half-written file at the canonical
  path. The SIDECAR temps keep a shared name deliberately, because a sidecar's worst case under a concurrent
  writer reads back as `null` and cold-starts, where the transcript's is a corrupt transcript. **That
  asymmetry holds for three of the four sidecars and not for the venue sentinel**, whose write is the one
  that is fatal: anything that makes its temp unwritable fails every promotion on the key. Every temp is
  therefore cleared by ONE rule that takes every shape, because choosing between the two calls was got wrong
  twice in opposite directions: `unlinkSync` first, which removes a file or a link INCLUDING a dangling one,
  and `rmSync` only for the directory it cannot take, which goes with its whole subtree. `rmSync` alone does
  not remove a dangling link (it resolves the path, finds nothing, and reports success while leaving it), so
  the next write follows the survivor, which is the write-through-a-link hole this contract exists to
  close. The venue sentinel is written under that lock
  immediately BEFORE the rename and is the one sidecar write that is fatal (above). The venue stamp,
  `pi-version`, the chain counter and the context reading are written under that lock immediately AFTER
  it, in that order, and are deliberately not described as part of it: the swap is one rename and cannot be
  widened. **A post-swap sidecar write that fails is logged, never fatal**, because it runs after the
  transcript is already promoted and throwing would report `promote-failed` for a promotion that
  demonstrably happened. **Only the venue stamp needs a sentinel**, and the reason `pi-version` needs none
  is that a failed version stamp is safe in both directions, which is not the same as always true. Where the
  job RESUMED, the surviving stamp already matched its own image's pi and a job runs one image, so it stays
  true of the new transcript. Where the job COLD-STARTED under a new pi, the surviving stamp is FALSE of the
  transcript beside it, and that is still safe, because the next job on that image reads a mismatch and cold
  starts rather than resuming it. With no prior stamp at all the next read cold-starts too. A promotion that knows no version writes an EMPTY stamp rather than
  skipping the write, which `readSidecar`'s size check refuses, so the key cold-starts; skipping would leave
  a previous version beside a transcript an unknown pi wrote. For the chain and context sidecars that
  would also tell an operator the next run will cold start when it will in fact resume. For the venue stamp
  the forecast runs the other way: a failed stamp leaves the sentinel, so the next run WILL cold-start, and
  the logged `session_sidecar_failed` line is what explains it.
  **`locked` means the lock was held and this job could not take it**: a lock younger than the staleness bound, or an older one whose takeover lost the recreate race. A read-only directory or a full disk also fails to create the
  lock, and reporting those as `locked` sends an operator looking for a stuck lock file that does not
  exist, so they fall through to `promote-failed`. A job that cannot take the lock discards rather
  than clobbers. Everything else the agent left in `/session` is deleted unread with the job dir.
- **Why**: This is the **second** agent-authored channel the host reads back, and `INT-OUTBOX-CONTRACT` is
  the precedent for how such a channel gets described — validated on the way in, never trusted because of
  where it came from.
  **The canonical store is never mounted**, and three properties fall out of that one decision rather than
  needing three mechanisms. `CONST-RETRY-INFRA-ONLY` survives, because a policy or infra exit discards the
  container's writes and attempt 2 starts from exactly what attempt 1 did. `CONST-ISOLATION-CONTAINER-PER-JOB`'s
  *"every one operator- or worker-supplied, none host-wide"* stays true verbatim, because `/session` is
  per-job exactly as `/job` is. And a container can name its own copy and nothing else — the mount is the
  capability, and the hash is not one.
  **`lstat`, regular files only, is security rather than hygiene.** The agent owns `/session`, so a
  symlink it plants resolves on the HOST when the worker reads it back; `stat` + `readFile` would hand the
  next job on that key any worker-readable file. `INT-CONTAINER-JOB-INPUTS` documents this attack in the
  other direction already, and the repo's own habit is the wrong one here: `makeLogReaper` uses `statSync`,
  which follows.
  **The 0-byte staging is what makes pi's own EEXIST race unreachable.** `setSessionFile` takes its
  empty-file branch, writes a header at our exact path and marks the manager flushed, so `_persist` never
  reaches `openSync(path, "wx")` — an exclusive create that would throw the moment two jobs shared a key.
  The host needs no knowledge of pi's file format to get that, and a test pins the header landing, because
  that branch is the one upstream change that would silently re-arm the race.
  **The pi-version gate exists because a transcript outlives the pi that wrote it.** pi's own docs record
  the consequence: an older session's stored tool-call arguments may no longer match the current tool
  schema. The repair hook is an extension-author API and this project does not own pi's built-in schemas,
  so the only available answer is to refuse the resume — which needs the version before the container
  starts, hence an image LABEL read on the preflight's existing `docker image inspect`. An image that
  declares none never resumes: `null` is the safe direction, never "assume it matches".
  **Nothing key-derived crosses the boundary.** The container always sees the constant
  `/session/current.jsonl`, so no repository name, no branch name and no host layout is legible from
  inside a job.
- **Traces to**: `REQ-RESUMABLE-SESSION`, `CONST-ISOLATION-CONTAINER-PER-JOB`, `CONST-RETRY-INFRA-ONLY`,
  `INT-CONTAINER-RUNTIME-CONTRACT`, `INT-CONTAINER-JOB-INPUTS`, `INT-RUN-HISTORY-FILE-CONTRACT`, `OQ-014`
- **Acceptance**: Given two jobs whose keys differ only in repository or only in branch, their `/session`
  host paths differ and neither is `PI_SESSIONS_DIR` nor a directory under it that the other can name.
  Given a symlink at either edge, it is refused and its target is never read; given a KEY DIRECTORY that is
  a symlink, a regular file or a dangling link when it is checked, both edges refuse it with
  `key-not-a-directory`, leave the entry where it stands, write nothing through it, and the reaper leaves it
  and says so; given a key directory swapped for one AFTER the read path has opened the transcript, the job
  resumes the transcript it judged and no byte of the replacement reaches the container; given one swapped after the write path's last check AND still in place when that check runs, the promotion reports `key-not-a-directory` rather than `promoted`; given one swapped in and reverted around the rename, it reports `transcript-diverted`;
  given the STORE itself behind a symlink, resolve and promote both work, because only the key's own name is
  checked.
  Given a transcript holding a compaction entry whose summary is empty, blank, missing, or only pi's
  split-turn and file-list text, the job cold-starts with `compaction-summary-empty`, whether that entry is
  the last compaction or an earlier one; given one whose summary has the model's text in every part, it
  resumes.
  Given a non-completed exit,
  the canonical file is byte-identical to before the run. Given a second writer holding the lock, the
  loser leaves the canonical transcript untouched. Given an image whose pi version differs from the
  stamped one, the job cold-starts. Given a transcript stamped with a venue other than the job's resolved
  backend, the job cold-starts with `venue-changed`, ahead of any pi-version verdict; given a key with no
  stamp, it resumes for a job resolving to `local` and cold-starts for any other venue, whatever the
  deployment default is; given a stamp that exists but is not a readable regular file, including a dangling
  symlink, the job cold-starts; given a promotion whose transcript rename fails, the stamp reads
  `(pending)` and both venues cold-start; given a completed promotion, the stamp names the venue of the
  session that promoted. Given a link planted at `pi-version`, a promotion neither writes through it nor
  reads through it and its target is byte-unchanged; given a `pi-version` write that fails after the swap,
  the promotion reports `promoted`, and the surviving stamp is stale-but-true where the job resumed under a
  matching stamp and wrong where it cold-started under a new pi, so the next job resumes in the first case
  and cold-starts in the second. Given a promotion by a job on the same
  venue landing between another job's gate read and its copy, that job cold-starts with
  `transcript-replaced` and its staged file is 0 bytes, while a transcript nothing touched still resumes.
  Given a promotion lock older than the staleness bound, the next promotion takes it over and lands, saying
  so once it holds it, including on a key with no transcript and on a store with `PI_SESSIONS_TTL_DAYS=0`;
  given one younger, the job records `locked` and leaves both the transcript and the lock alone. Given a
  key directory with no transcript whose own mtime has expired, the reaper sweeps it; given a fresh
  transcript in a long-untouched directory, it does not; given any error but ENOENT reading the transcript,
  it keeps the key and says so.

## INT-WORKSPACE-CHECKPOINT-STORE

**worker <-> host store. There is no container side: nothing mounts the store.**

- **Status**: **called by the recovery flow since issue #645 part 2** (`REQ-RUN-RECOVERY`). start.mjs builds one
  checkpointer per worker when `checkpointsDir` resolves (with a `snapshotTimeoutMs` of 20 s instead of the module's
  60 s, because a live snapshot is taken with a paid container frozen). A fresh `run.recover` job's processor calls
  `primeBase` before the container; the run checkpointer (`DES-RUN-CHECKPOINT-PAIRED`) calls `snapshot` for live
  (`frozen`), exit and salvage (`dead`) checkpoints and `readManifest` for the next `seq`; a recovery job calls
  `readManifest`, `baseSourceUrl` (the `file://` URL its clone fetches the base from) and `restore`; a run's final
  outcome calls `remove`; the retention tick calls `sweep()` (with no `active` list: the 7-day TTL is far past any run
  a host holds, the job timeout plus the six-hour recovery deadline). Doctor still warns at most. This entry is the
  contract that wiring keeps, written from the code as it stands.
- **Contract**:
  ```
  <root>                                   PI_CHECKPOINTS_DIR, else <PI_SESSIONS_DIR>/.checkpoints, else none; 0700
  <root>/<ck>/                             one per run; 0700; ck = first 32 hex of sha256("checkpoint\0" + runId)
  <root>/<ck>/repo.git/                    bare store, this run's only object database
  <root>/<ck>/home/                        empty; HOME and XDG_CONFIG_HOME of every store git
  <root>/<ck>/lock                         exclusive create, "<pid> <tag>\n"; absent when free; taken over when stale
  <root>/<ck>/base-too-large               marker "1\n": primeBase judged the base over maxBaseBytes
  <root>/<ck>/CURRENT                      "<seq>\n", the commit point; absent until the first checkpoint
  <root>/<ck>/cp-<seq>/manifest.json       0600; the schema below; at most two cp-<seq>/ kept (current, previous)
  <root>/<ck>/cp-<seq>/transcript.jsonl    0600; bytes [0, offset) of the job's transcript, offset <= maxTranscriptBytes
  <name>.<12 hex>.incoming                 an in-flight write beside any of the files above
  refs/pi-dispatch/base                    the base commit, fetched at depth 1 by primeBase
  refs/pi-dispatch/checkpoint              the newest imported checkpoint commit, moved by every import
  refs/pi-dispatch/cp/<seq>                one per imported checkpoint
  ```
  The module's surface is `primeBase`, `snapshot`, `writeTranscript`, `readManifest`, `restore`, `baseSourceUrl`,
  `remove`, `sweep` and `usage`. **None of them throws**: each returns a result, `{ skipped: reason }` for "could
  not, try later" and `{ refused: reason }` for "must not", because the caller has paused a paid container to call
  it and a throw unwinding through that pause handling loses a job for a checkpoint that was optional. Every
  filesystem call is `fs/promises` and every git an async spawn, because a synchronous walk of 200,000 files stalls
  the worker's heartbeat and lock renewals long enough for BullMQ to call the job stalled.
- **Location** (`checkpointsDirPath`, `worker/src/config.mjs`): `PI_CHECKPOINTS_DIR`, else
  `<PI_SESSIONS_DIR>/.checkpoints`, else `null`, resolved to an absolute path so doctor and the worker name the same
  directory. `null` means the feature has nowhere to write, and a caller says so rather than writing somewhere. The
  default sits inside the session store and only there, because a checkpoint holds a job's workspace and is as
  PII-bearing as a transcript, so it inherits the operator's choice of a private host-only directory rather than
  getting a default of its own on a path nobody chose. The DOT name keeps it out of the session reaper, which skips
  dot names silently (`INT-SESSION-STORE-CONTRACT`, the key-shaped-names rule). The checkpointer creates the root
  with mode 0700 and re-applies 0700 best effort. At `primeBase` the root, the run directory and `home/` must each
  `lstat` as a real directory, so a symlink or a file at any of those names fails it (`internal-error`); every later
  call `lstat`s the run directory too, and one that is not a real directory is `not-primed` to `snapshot`,
  `writeTranscript` and `restore` and `{ absent: true }` to `readManifest`. Only final components are judged, so
  the root's ancestors may be links. Both stores name their directories with 32 lower-case hex characters, so a
  layout where one store is, holds or sits below the other would have each sweeper judge the other's entries;
  `loadConfig` refuses that layout (`checkpointStoreCollision`, `INT-SESSION-STORE-CONTRACT`'s row of the same day).
- **The per-run folder name** is `checkpointKey(runId)`: the first 32 hex characters of
  `sha256("checkpoint\0" + runId)`. A HASH and not `sanitizeJobId(runId)`, because sanitising maps `..` to `..`
  (the dot is in its kept set), so a sanitised id is not a safe directory name; a hash cannot name `..`, a slash or
  another run's directory, has a fixed width, and keeps the store's listing free of anything a job id carries. The
  `checkpoint\0` prefix gives it its own hash domain beside the session store's keys.
- **The manifest** (`cp-<seq>/manifest.json`, one line of JSON, mode 0600). Every field is an integer, a boolean, an
  enum, hex, a host name or a short token, and none is ever a path or a file name; `readManifest` and `restore` both
  re-validate it with `manifestProblem`, so a manifest is never trusted because of where it sits.
  - `v`: integer, exactly `1`.
  - `runId`: string, `sanitizeJobId(runId)` cut to 200 characters, matching `[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,200}`. The run
    directory is found by the hash, never by this field; `restore` refuses a manifest whose `runId` is not its own
    argument sanitised the same way (`run-mismatch`), so one run's manifest is never applied in another's name.
  - `seq`: integer, 1 to 999,999,999, equal to `CURRENT`.
  - `attempt`: integer, 0 to 10,000, the caller's.
  - `host`: string, `[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}`: the injected or `os.hostname()` name, with every other character
    replaced by `_`, cut to 64, `unknown` when that leaves nothing.
  - `kind`: enum, `live`, `exit` or `salvage`.
  - `quiesced`: enum, `frozen` or `dead`. The CALLER's statement of how the workspace was held still; the module
    neither pauses a container nor can check the claim, and refuses any other value (`bad-args`).
  - `at`: integer, the injected clock's milliseconds.
  - `transcript`: exactly `{ bytes, sha256 }`, an integer and 64 lower-case hex.
  - `workspace.commit`, `workspace.baseSha`: hex of the store's object format (40 or 64).
  - `workspace.objectFormat`: enum, `sha1` or `sha256`.
  - `workspace.partial`, `workspace.ignoredDropped`: booleans. `partial` means something was unreadable and is
    missing from the checkpoint; `ignoredDropped` means the byte cap's ignore tier ran.
  - `workspace.counts`: integers `files`, `bytes`, `newBytes`, and `skipped`, exactly five integers `unreadable`,
    `special`, `dotgit`, `badName`, `tooLarge` (the walk's exclusions, below).
  - `workspace.git`: `state`, enum `parsed`, `unreadable` or `none`; `detached`, boolean; `branch`, null or a branch
    name (at most 200 characters, segments of `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` not starting with a dot, none ending `.lock` or
    holding `..`); `tip`, null or 40 or 64 hex. `branch` is only ever the CALLER's branch, recorded when the agent's
    `HEAD` is exactly `ref: refs/heads/<that branch>`; a name read from `HEAD` is compared, never recorded. `none` is
    no `.git` at all; `unreadable` is a `.git` that is not a real directory (a `gitdir:` file, a link) or a `HEAD`
    that is neither a sha nor a branch ref. The tip comes from the loose ref (each directory on the way `lstat`ed,
    the ref opened `O_NOFOLLOW`), else `packed-refs` (at most 1 MiB). It is RECORDED ONLY: the agent's commits are
    not in the store (every dotgit is excluded), so a restore reproduces the work tree and not its history.
  - `piVersion`, `imageDigest`, `venue`, `provider`, `model`: null or a token matching
    `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:@/+-]{0,127}$`. A malformed value is dropped to `null` and its field NAME logged
    (`checkpoint_meta_dropped`): fail open and say which.

  Every object is CLOSED, at every level: a missing or extra key is `field:keys` at the top, `field:transcript`,
  `field:workspace`, `field:counts` (for `counts` and `counts.skipped`) or `field:git`. An open nested object is
  where a path or a payload string would ride along unvalidated into everything that reads a manifest.
- **The commit point**, in `snapshot`'s order. Free refusals and caps first: arguments, the run directory and the
  store's `HEAD` exist (`not-primed`), no `base-too-large` marker, the lock, `seq` above `CURRENT` (`stale-seq`;
  an unreadable or malformed `CURRENT` does not refuse here and is replaced by a successful snapshot), the
  transcript `offset` against `maxTranscriptBytes` (`transcript-too-large`, judged on the offset because that is the
  number of bytes the copy would write: a sparse session file of 100 GB logical size reads as zeros), the store's
  object format and the base sha in it, free disk and the store's total size (both counting the transcript's
  `offset` bytes about to be copied), the walk (which refuses `over-file-cap`
  the moment its count passes `maxFiles`), the byte cap and its ignore tier, then every kept PATH matched against
  the job's secrets. Then the one expensive step: reading new bytes into `fast-import`, scanning them and every
  symlink target for job secrets.
  Then the stat cache is updated, the store repacked when `seq` is a multiple of `repackEvery`, and the commit point
  runs: `cp-<seq>/` is reserved (its leftover `.incoming` files removed), the transcript is copied (in 1 MiB
  chunks, the snapshot's deadline checked before each, so a slow or huge source ends as `timeout` with the temp copy
  removed and nothing committed), then the manifest is written, then `CURRENT`. Each is an exclusive-create temp, written, fsynced and renamed over its name; the
  manifest's directory and the run directory are fsynced after their renames (the first also covers the
  transcript's, which shares the directory). **The guarantee**: a failure or crash at any step before `CURRENT`'s
  rename leaves `CURRENT` naming the previous complete checkpoint, or absent; after it, the new one, complete. A
  `cp-<seq>/` or a `refs/pi-dispatch/cp/<seq>` that `CURRENT` does not name is an orphan: nothing reads it, and a
  later snapshot may reuse that `seq`. **Pruning**, after `CURRENT`'s rename and its directory's fsync and under the
  same lock: every `refs/pi-dispatch/cp/<seq>` (`for-each-ref`, then one `update-ref --stdin` of deletes) and every
  `cp-<seq>/` except the new checkpoint's and the one `CURRENT` named before it is removed, so a long run keeps two
  transcripts, not one per snapshot, and the next repack drops the pruned commits' objects. The previous one is
  kept as the fallback when the newest turns out to be the bad one. A crash or failure while pruning leaves
  `CURRENT` naming the complete new checkpoint (pruning never touches the two it keeps), is logged
  (`checkpoint_prune_failed {code}`) without failing the already committed snapshot, and the next snapshot prunes
  what was left. Pinned by injecting a failure at each of nine filesystem steps, and in the prune; the store's OBJECTS are written by git with git's own durability settings, which this module does not
  change.
- **The git environment and flags.** Every store git goes through one function (`startGit`), so every argv is
  `STORE_GIT_FLAGS` followed by the subcommand, and every environment is exactly `storeGitEnv`
  (`worker/src/git-hardening.mjs`), BUILT FROM NOTHING rather than spread from `process.env`: `PATH` (the
  worker's, with every empty and relative entry dropped, since both resolve against the cwd; `/usr/bin:/bin` when
  nothing absolute is left), `HOME` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` (both `<ck>/home`), `GIT_DIR` (`<ck>/repo.git`), `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`,
  `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null`, `GIT_ATTR_NOSYSTEM=1`, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`,
  `GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1`, `GIT_PROTOCOL_FROM_USER=0`, `LC_ALL=C`. `GIT_WORK_TREE` is added for ONE subcommand,
  `check-ignore`, and can reach no other; every git runs with the run directory as its cwd except `check-ignore`,
  which runs in `<ck>/home`. `STORE_GIT_FLAGS` is `GIT_SAFE_CONFIG` (`core.hooksPath=/dev/null`,
  `core.fsmonitor=false`) plus `protocol.ext.allow=never`, an empty `credential.helper`, `commit.gpgSign=false`,
  `tag.gpgSign=false`, `gc.auto=0`, `maintenance.auto=false`, `core.protectNTFS=true`, `core.protectHFS=true`,
  `transfer.fsckObjects=true`, `fetch.fsckObjects=true`, `core.untrackedCache=false`, then `--no-pager`. The
  store's own config gains `core.logAllRefUpdates=false`, `gc.auto=0` and `uploadpack.allowAnySHA1InWant=true` at
  init (the last so a restore's caller can fetch the base by sha; the store holds only this run's objects, so "any
  sha" is no wider than the repository). The subcommands are `init --bare --object-format=<fmt>`, `fetch`,
  `ls-tree`, `rev-parse`, `check-ignore --no-index --stdin -z`, `fast-import`, `repack -adq`, `for-each-ref`,
  `update-ref --stdin`, `diff-tree` and `cat-file --batch`. `primeBase`'s `file://` fetch passes `-c protocol.file.allow=always`, since
  `GIT_PROTOCOL_FROM_USER=0` turns the user-policy protocols off, and a restore caller fetching from
  `baseSourceUrl` needs the same. Each spawn
  carries a `gitTimeoutMs` deadline, combined with its operation's own, and dies by SIGKILL; its stderr is kept,
  bounded at 64 KiB, for tests only and never logged, because it can name agent paths. A test spies on every spawn
  of a full prime, snapshot (with the ignore tier and a repack) and restore and holds each to both. Doctor warns
  below git 2.32, the first that reads `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`.
  **Two git commands touch the workspace, and both are bounded.** `primeBase` fetches the base from
  `<workspace>/.git` BEFORE the container starts, when that repository is still the worker's own fresh clone (the
  caller's obligation). `check-ignore`, in the byte cap's tier, reads only ignore files: `--no-index`, `GIT_DIR`
  still the store, no attributes and no filters, and its cwd is `<ck>/home`, never the workspace: git resolves a work
  tree it is not inside from `GIT_WORK_TREE` alone and takes the paths relative to its top (measured on git 2.39).
  Exit 1 is "nothing ignored"; any other failure keeps nothing back, so the snapshot refuses `over-byte-cap` rather
  than storing everything it was asked to cut. The tier logs `checkpoint_ignore_tier` with `outcome` `failed`,
  `none-ignored` or `dropped`. A `.gitignore` that is a FIFO would hang it, so a walk that saw one skips the tier
  (`over-byte-cap`).
- **The fast-import stream**, one per snapshot, `git fast-import --quiet --done --force --date-format=raw`:
  ```
  feature done
  commit refs/pi-dispatch/checkpoint
  mark :1
  committer pi-dispatch <checkpoint@pi-dispatch.invalid> <unix seconds> +0000
  data <n>
  pi-dispatch checkpoint <seq>
  from <baseSha>
  deleteall
  M <100644 or 100755> <oid> "<path>"                a regular file served from the stat cache
  M <100644 or 100755> inline "<path>"               a regular file read now, then: data <n> LF <bytes> LF
  M 120000 inline "<path>"                           a symlink, then: data <n> LF <target> LF

  reset refs/pi-dispatch/cp/<seq>
  from :1

  done
  ```
  Every path is C-quoted, always, with every byte outside printable ASCII as an octal escape, so no name can end a
  command or change its meaning. A file is `100755` when any execute bit is set. Each checkpoint commit's parent is
  the BASE, never the previous checkpoint, and its tree is the whole walk (`deleteall`, then every kept path), so
  each checkpoint stands alone and its diff against the base is exactly a restore's change list. Empty directories
  are not recorded. A cached `M` names only an oid that exists in the store: `primeBase` caches a file's oid only
  when the BASE TREE holds it (a checkout that converted the file on its way out has a different on-disk id). A
  killed or failed import removes `objects/pack/tmp_*` and `fast_import_crash_*` (which quotes recent commands, so
  agent path names).
- **The walk and the stat cache.** The workspace is walked in Node: every stat is `lstat`, every open
  `O_NOFOLLOW | O_NONBLOCK`, names are read as bytes. Excluded and COUNTED, never silent: a dotgit segment at any
  depth under git's HFS and NTFS folding (`isDotGitSegment`: `.GIT`, `git~1`, ignorable code points, trailing dots
  and spaces, an NTFS stream suffix), so a nested repository's files are captured and its `.git` is not (`dotgit`);
  a name `validSegment` refuses (empty, `.`, `..`, a control byte, invalid UTF-8, over 255 bytes), a path over 4096
  bytes, or a directory too deep to descend (64 segments) (`badName`); a FIFO, socket or device (`special`); an
  EACCES or EPERM anywhere, which also sets `partial`, and no mode is ever changed (`unreadable`); a regular file
  over `maxFileBytes`, or a link target empty or over 4096 bytes (`tooLarge`). The deadline and the file cap are
  checked per ENTRY, so one directory of 200,000 names can neither run past the deadline nor grow the walk's list
  without bound. A file is read only after its descriptor's `fstat` shows a regular file with the walk's device and
  inode and exactly the walked size arrives; on a host with `/proc/self/fd` (Linux), the descriptor's link must also
  resolve inside the workspace's realpath followed by `/`, which catches a directory swapped for a link between the
  `lstat` and the open (`O_NOFOLLOW` guards only the last component). Anything else, or an ENOENT or ENOTDIR during
  the walk, abandons the whole snapshot (`tree-changed`) rather than recording a mix. Where `/proc/self/fd` does not
  exist (macOS) only the caller's pause and the device and inode check stand: an unpaused agent racing a directory
  swap there could have a host file read and stored, which is the residual the pause precondition covers. The stat cache is in memory, per run: a file whose device, inode, size, mtime and ctime (in
  nanoseconds) all match is not re-read. Losing it on a restart costs only re-reading.
- **The secret scan.** `snapshot` is handed the job's secret values; every non-empty one is matched, as bytes,
  against every kept PATH (a directory name is a substring of every path under it, so segments are covered), every
  regular file READ for the snapshot and every symlink target. A path match refuses before `fast-import` starts.
  One match refuses the whole snapshot
  (`job-secret-in-tree`): the import is killed and cleaned as above, `CURRENT` and the stat cache are unchanged, and
  no object holding those bytes is left in the store. NOT scanned, by construction: a file served from the stat
  cache (base content, or bytes an earlier snapshot of this run read and scanned; a write changes the ctime, so a
  secret written into one is re-read), and the transcript copy. The match is literal, so an encoded secret passes.
- **Caps and their defaults** (`DEFAULT_CHECKPOINT_LIMITS`, overridable only through the factory's `limits`; no
  environment variable sets them yet): `maxBaseBytes` 2 GiB (the walked base at prime; over it, the marker is
  written and every later snapshot reports `base-too-large`); `maxNewBytes` 512 MiB (bytes not served from the
  cache; over it, the ignore tier, then `over-byte-cap`); `maxFiles` 200,000 (files and links walked, judged as the
  walk counts them, before the ignore tier; exactly `maxFiles` passes, one more is `over-file-cap`); `maxFileBytes` 64 MiB per file (excluded and counted; also the largest blob a
  restore accepts); `maxTranscriptBytes` 256 MiB, the transcript copy's `offset` (`transcript-too-large`; far above a
  real pi session, whose JSONL is tens of MiB, half the byte cap, and with two checkpoints kept it bounds one run's
  transcripts to 512 MiB); `maxStoreBytes` 20 GiB for the whole root, every run together, plus the transcript about
  to be copied (`store-full`); free disk at least twice `maxNewBytes` plus that transcript AND at least 5% of the
  volume, from `statfs` (`disk-low`, also when `statfs` fails);
  `snapshotTimeoutMs` 60 s per prime, snapshot or restore; `gitTimeoutMs` 60 s per git spawn; `ttlMs` 7 days for the
  sweep; `lockStaleMs` 1 hour; `repackEvery` 20. Fixed: a link target of 1 to 4096 bytes, a path of at most 4096
  bytes and 64 segments, a segment of at most 255 bytes.
- **Skip and refuse reasons**, every one the code returns.
  `primeBase`: skipped `bad-args`, `locked`, `lock-failed`, `workspace-not-directory`, `tree-changed`, `timeout`,
  `over-file-cap`, `base-too-large`, `store-init-failed`, `base-fetch-failed`, `internal-error`.
  `snapshot`: skipped `bad-args`, `not-primed`, `base-too-large`, `locked`, `lock-failed`, `stale-seq`,
  `transcript-too-large`, `store-unreadable`, `disk-low`, `store-full`, `workspace-not-directory`, `tree-changed`,
  `timeout`, `over-file-cap`, `over-byte-cap`, `import-failed`, `internal-error`; refused `job-secret-in-tree`.
  `writeTranscript`: skipped `bad-args`, `not-primed`, `transcript-too-large`, `timeout`, `transcript-failed`.
  `readManifest`: `{ absent: true }` (no run directory, a run directory that is not a real directory, or no
  `CURRENT`), or `{ invalid: true, reason }` with
  `bad-args`, `current-unreadable`, `current-malformed`, `manifest-unreadable`, `manifest-json`, `seq-mismatch`,
  `transcript-mismatch` (the copy's length or sha256 differs from the manifest's, because a resume feeds it to a
  paid model), `internal-error`, or `field:<name>` where name is one of `not-object`, `keys`, `v`, `runId`, `seq`,
  `attempt`, `host`, `kind`, `quiesced`, `at`, `transcript`, `workspace`, `objectFormat`, `commit`, `baseSha`,
  `flags`, `counts`, `git`, `piVersion`, `imageDigest`, `venue`, `provider`, `model`.
  `restore`: skipped `bad-args`, `not-primed`, `workspace-not-directory`, `locked`, `lock-failed`,
  `store-unreadable`, `timeout`, `internal-error`; refused `bad-manifest`, `run-mismatch`, `base-mismatch`,
  `tampered`, `path-through-symlink`, `case-collision`, `path-conflict`.
  `remove`: skipped `bad-args`, `remove-failed`. `sweep`: skipped `sweep-failed`. `usage`: skipped `usage-failed`.
  Logs carry names, counts and codes, never a path or a value.
- **The lock** is exclusive create, as in `INT-SESSION-STORE-CONTRACT` (mirrored, not imported). `locked` means a
  lock is held and is younger than `lockStaleMs` by the injected clock, or changed while it was being judged; any
  other create failure is `lock-failed`. A stale lock is taken over by RENAMING it to a unique sibling
  (`lock.stale.<12 hex>`), which is atomic, so of two processes judging one stale lock exactly one moves it; the
  mover then checks that what it moved still holds the bytes it judged stale, and a lock a rival wrote in between is
  put back with `link` (which never overwrites) instead of removed; only then is the moved file unlinked and a new
  lock created with `wx`. A release moves the lock the same way (`lock.release.<12 hex>`) and unlinks it only when
  it holds the releaser's own tag, else puts it back, which closes the session store's release-by-path residual.
  Residuals: while a lock is moved aside it is absent, and a third process creating one in that instant wins, the
  put-back `link` then failing and the moved lock being dropped; and a lock with a future mtime is never stale.
- **Restore** writes the checkpoint `manifest` names into `intoWorkspace`, which must ALREADY hold a checkout of
  `manifest.workspace.baseSha` (the caller fetches it from `baseSourceUrl(runId)`, the store's `file://` URL). Before
  the lock it refuses a manifest of another run (`run-mismatch`) and a checkout whose commit is not `baseSha`
  (`base-mismatch`). That commit is parsed from FILES (`<intoWorkspace>/.git` a real directory, `HEAD` opened
  `O_NOFOLLOW` as a sha, or `ref: refs/heads/<name>` resolved through the loose ref or `packed-refs`), not by `git
  rev-parse`, although the target is a fresh host-made clone where rev-parse would be acceptable: every store git
  keeps `GIT_DIR` at the store, which the spawn bolt holds, and the parser already exists for the snapshot side.
  Under the lock it reads `diff-tree -r -z --raw --no-abbrev
  --no-renames <baseSha> <commit>` and the commit's full tree, and JUDGES THE WHOLE CHANGE LIST BEFORE TOUCHING THE
  DISK. Refused: a diff that does not parse, a path `validPath` rejects (the snapshot's own rule, from
  `checkpoint-paths.mjs`, so a dotgit path is tampering), a gitlink in the result, or a mode other than `100644`,
  `100755` or `120000` (`tampered`); a written path under a path the result makes a symlink
  (`path-through-symlink`); two paths, or ancestors, that collide under `foldCase` (`case-collision`). Then it
  applies the changes: deletions and type changes first (a gitlink on the base side is skipped, since the snapshot
  cannot record one; emptied parents are pruned), then regular files, then symlinks LAST, so no write of a restore
  traverses a link it created. Every existing ancestor must `lstat` as a real directory (a link refuses
  `path-through-symlink`, anything else `path-conflict`); missing ones are made one segment at a time, mode 0755. A
  target that is a directory refuses `path-conflict`. Blobs come from one `cat-file --batch`, whose header must name
  the requested oid as a blob of at most `maxFileBytes` (`tampered`); a link target must be 1 to 4096 bytes with no
  NUL (`tampered`). Files open `O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_TRUNC | O_NOFOLLOW` (`ELOOP` refuses `path-through-symlink`)
  and their mode is set explicitly to 0644 or 0755. The bytes written are the blob's bytes exactly; nothing runs a
  filter, an eol conversion or a checkout. **A refusal found on disk can come after writes**, so the caller
  discards a refused workspace and never resumes in it. `restore` treats `.pi/` and the root context files like any
  other path; the recovery resets them, and `.agents/`, to the base commit after the restore
  (`DES-RECOVERY-TRUST-PATHS-FROM-BASE`).
- **Sweep and remove.** `sweep({ active })` judges only names that are 32 lower-case hex and `lstat` as a real
  directory (a link with such a name is left, never followed); a run in `active` is kept. A run's age is its newest
  `cp-<seq>/manifest.json` mtime, else the directory's own, and one older than `ttlMs` by the injected clock is
  removed whole. It yields between entries. It takes no run lock, so a run missing from `active` can be removed
  mid-operation: the caller passes every run it holds. `remove(runId)` deletes one run's directory and its
  in-memory state; `usage()` is the root's total bytes.
- **Nothing mounts the store into a container.** No path under the root is ever handed to a container runtime, no
  key or run directory name crosses the boundary, and the checkpointer runs host-side only. What it reads from a job
  is the job's workspace from the host side, and the transcript at a path the caller passes.
- **Why**: this is the third agent-authored tree the host reads back, after `INT-OUTBOX-CONTRACT` and
  `INT-SESSION-STORE-CONTRACT`, and the largest: every byte, name and file TYPE in it is chosen by the agent, and it
  is read and later WRITTEN on the host, outside the container. So the store copies the session store's habits
  (`lstat` first, temp and rename, a derived name, never mounted) and adds the two this tree needs: no git command
  ever reads the agent's repository configuration, and a restore re-validates every path with the same functions
  the snapshot used, so a store tampered with on disk is refused rather than trusted. The design and its rejected
  alternatives are `DES-CHECKPOINT-WALKER-NOT-GIT-ADD`.
- **Traces to**: `REQ-RUN-RECOVERY`, `INT-RUN-CHECKPOINT-POINTER`,
  `DES-CHECKPOINT-WALKER-NOT-GIT-ADD`, `INT-SESSION-STORE-CONTRACT`, `CONST-ISOLATION-CONTAINER-PER-JOB`,
  `DES-CONTAINER-BACKEND-REGISTRY` (`pausable`).
- **Acceptance** (`worker/test/workspace-checkpoint.test.mjs`, `checkpoint-paths.test.mjs`, against real git):
  Given a snapshot restored into a fresh base clone, the tree matches byte for byte, links and execute bits
  included, in sha1 and in sha256 repositories, and under `.gitattributes` `ident`, `eol=crlf` and
  `working-tree-encoding`. Given a hostile `.git/config` (a clean filter, an fsmonitor, a gpg program, an include),
  none of it runs through snapshot, the ignore tier or restore; given a `gitdir:` redirect, `alternates` or a
  symlinked `objects/`, nothing of the target reaches the store. Given nested repositories, their files are
  captured and every `.git`, `.GIT` and `git~1` is excluded and counted; control-character names, a FIFO, an
  unreadable entry and an oversized file are each counted, the FIFO without hanging and the unreadable entry with
  `partial` and its mode unchanged. Given a job secret in any file read or any link target, the snapshot is refused,
  `CURRENT` still names the previous checkpoint, and no object, temp pack or crash report holds it. Given a failure
  at any of nine steps of the commit point, the call reports `internal-error`, `CURRENT` names a complete valid
  checkpoint, and the lock is released. Given a link and a file under it, a gitlink, a dotgit path, a case
  collision or a symlinked ancestor already on disk, the restore refuses and writes nothing through the link. Given
  a run directory or a link with a key's name, the sweep removes only stale real run directories outside `active`.
  Given any spawn, its argv starts with `STORE_GIT_FLAGS` and its env is exactly `storeGitEnv`, plus
  `GIT_WORK_TREE` for `check-ignore` alone; both are also pinned as LITERALS. Given a secret in a file name, a
  directory name or a link target, the snapshot is refused; `[""]` matches nothing. Given an open that lands on a
  link, a FIFO, another inode, a short read, or (with a proc directory) a path outside the workspace, the snapshot is
  `tree-changed`. Given a tree deeper than 64 segments or a path over 4096 bytes, the excess is counted, never
  stored. Given exactly `maxFiles` the snapshot passes and one more refuses; an unchanged big base is not new bytes;
  a failing `check-ignore` refuses `over-byte-cap`. Given a manifest of another run or a checkout off `baseSha`, a
  restore refuses; given a gitlink in the snapshot tree, the change judge refuses before anything is written, and a
  gitlink on the base side is skipped. Given a stale lock a rival retook, or a lock no longer the releaser's, it is
  put back rather than removed. Given a 30-day-old run directory with a day-old manifest, the sweep keeps it. Given a sparse
  transcript of 1 GiB logical size over a small `maxTranscriptBytes`, the snapshot is skipped with nothing reserved or
  written; given a slow transcript source, the copy stops at the deadline as `timeout`; given four checkpoints, two
  directories and two refs remain; given a failure in the prune, `CURRENT` names the new complete checkpoint.

## INT-RUN-CHECKPOINT-POINTER

**worker -> Valkey -> every worker of the deployment.** Where a durable run's latest checkpoint is (issue #645,
`REQ-RUN-RECOVERY`, `DES-RUN-CHECKPOINT-PAIRED`). Written by the worker whose host took the checkpoint, read by any
worker that must route the run's recovery (the host that noticed a stall can be any host), by the recovery job and by
the boot's orphan sweep. The constants are exported from `@edgehero/pi-dispatch/run-checkpoint`
(`CHECKPOINT_POINTER_PREFIX`, `CHECKPOINT_POINTER_TTL_MS`, `checkpointPointerKey`, `validPointer`,
`readCheckpointPointer`, `writeCheckpointPointer`, `removeCheckpointPointer`).

- **Key**: `run:checkpoint:<sanitized run id>`, the RUN id (`recoveryOf ?? job.id`) through `sanitizeJobId`, never a
  recovery job's own id, so a run has one pointer across its attempts and recoveries.
- **Value**: one JSON string, written whole by `SET <key> <json> PX <ttl>`:
  ```
  { "v": 1,
    "host":      "<host token>",       // [A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}: the host whose store holds the checkpoint
    "hostQueue": "<queue name>" | null, // that host's own queue (pi-jobs@<name>) when PI_WORKER_NAME is declared, else null
    "seq":       <int>,                 // 1 to 999,999,999: the checkpoint's sequence number in the store
    "attempt":   <int>,                 // 0 to 10,000: the run's container number that took it
    "at":        <int>,                 // ms since epoch, the worker's clock at the write
    "jobDir":    "job-<chars>" }        // the taking attempt's job folder BASENAME, ^job-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$, never a path
  ```
  A reader accepts a plain object with EXACTLY these seven keys, each typed as above, and treats anything else
  (malformed JSON, a value over 4 KiB, a missing or extra key) as no pointer. A pointer is peer-written data, and it
  decides where a recovery is queued and which folder a salvage looks at, so nothing loose rides along.
- **When it is written**: after every committed checkpoint (live, exit or salvage), never before: a reader that finds
  a pointer finds a checkpoint behind it. A failed write leaves the previous pointer (stale, never ahead) and is logged
  (`checkpoint_pointer_failed`).
- **TTL**: 7 days (`CHECKPOINT_POINTER_TTL_MS`, the store's own `ttlMs`), set again by every write.
- **Removed** at the run's final outcome (a completed or policy result of an armed run, and `recovery-failed`,
  `endDurableRun`), after the store entry, so "pointer and store both gone" is the superseded test's second half
  (`DES-RECOVERY-ROUTED-TO-CHECKPOINT-HOST`; its first is the base run's settled record).
  Not removed by a queued recovery, nor by `recovery-superseded`.
- **Failure**: every call is bounded (1 s by default, 2 s for the wiring's reads) and never throws: a read that fails
  or times out answers null, which is why a recovery never reads a lone null as superseded.
- **Readers**: the processor's infra-exit path and the failed listener (routing), the recovery job (superseded, the
  salvage), the run checkpointer (the next `seq`), the boot's orphan sweep (`pointedJobDirs`: a `SCAN` of
  `run:checkpoint:*`, bounded at 10,000 keys, refusing rather than answering partially, so a folder a recovery is about
  to salvage is never swept).
- **Acceptance**: `REQ-RUN-RECOVERY` (c) and (f); `worker/test/run-checkpoint.test.mjs` ("validPointer: exactly the
  pointer's keys, every value typed; anything loose is null", "the pointer round trip: written with its TTL, read back
  validated, removed").

## INT-RUN-BUDGET-LEDGER

**worker -> Valkey -> the worker's later attempts and recoveries.** The durable record of every dollar hold one
`run.recover` run has taken (issue #645, `DES-RUN-BUDGET-LEDGER`). Written and read by the processor alone, through
`makeRunBudgetLedger` (`@edgehero/pi-dispatch/run-budget-ledger`: `RUN_BUDGET_KEY_PREFIX`, `RUN_BUDGET_TTL_MS`,
`RUN_BUDGET_MAX_KEYS`, `RUN_BUDGET_STATES`, `runBudgetKeyFor`, `validHold`). A job that never armed `run.recover`
never touches it.

- **Key**: `run:budget:<sanitized run id>`, one hash per run.
- **Fields**:
  ```
  slot      "held"                                    set once, when the run's job-count slots are reserved
  seq       <int>                                     the last container number handed out (1, 2, 3, ...)
  h<seq>    {"amountMicros":<int>,"keys":[...],        the hold container <seq> ran under, as reserveDollars returned
             "ledgers":[{"keyPrefix":..,"keys":[..]}]}  it: at most 16 distinct budget:usd:* keys, ledgers optional
  s<seq>    held | settled | released | settled-crashed   that hold's state
  at        <ms>                                      the injected clock at the last write; for doctor, never a decision
  ```
- **States**: `held` is the only state a transition starts from; `settled` (the container's exit settled it),
  `released` (a never-started container's hold was given back) and `settled-crashed` (a later recovery wrote off a
  crashed container's hold at the floor, bookkeeping only) are terminal and never change again.
- **Scripts**, each one `EVAL`, each refreshing the TTL on a write:
  - `claimSlot`: `HSETNX slot held`; answers `new` (this call set it) or `carried`.
  - `nextSeq`: `HINCRBY seq 1`; the new container number.
  - `recordHold(seq, hold)`: writes `h<seq>` and `s<seq> = held` only when `s<seq>` is absent; answers `ok` or
    `exists`. The hold is validated first (`validHold`: a non-negative safe integer amount, the keys and the ledgers'
    flattened keys equal and under their prefixes).
  - `settle(seq)` and `release(seq)`: `held` to `settled` or `released`, only from `held`; answers `moved` or
    `not-held`. Only `moved` licenses the caller to adjust or refund a window key.
  - `settleCrashed(belowSeq)`: every `s<k> = held` with `k < belowSeq` to `settled-crashed` in one script, answering
    the seqs it moved; nothing written (and the TTL untouched) when none moved, so an expired ledger is not revived.
- **TTL**: 35 days (`RUN_BUDGET_TTL_MS`), past the longest dollar window a hold sits in, refreshed by every write.
  Deleted at the run's final outcome (`remove`).
- **Failure**: every method returns `{ error }` on a Valkey fault or a bad argument and never throws, and logs
  `run_budget_ledger_error` with the operation and the error code only (never a run id, a key or a value). The
  processor turns a failed `claimSlot`, `nextSeq` or `recordHold` into a never-started `InfraRetry` before tokens; a
  failed `settleCrashed` is logged and the run goes on with the holds at the floor.
- **Acceptance**: `REQ-RUN-RECOVERY` (e); `worker/test/run-budget-ledger.test.mjs`.

## INT-RECOVERY-JOB

**worker -> BullMQ -> the worker holding the checkpoint.** The job that continues a lost `run.recover` run, and the
two Valkey keys that keep it to one per recovery number and bound its wait (issue #645,
`DES-RECOVERY-ROUTED-TO-CHECKPOINT-HOST`). Exported from `@edgehero/pi-dispatch/recovery-queue` (`RECOVERY_CAP`,
`RECOVERY_TTL_MS`, `RECOVERY_CLAIM_TTL_MS`, `RECOVER_CLAIM_PREFIX`, `RECOVER_PENDING_KEY`, `recoveryJobId`,
`recoveryClaimKey`, `pendingMember`, `runIdOf`).

- **Job id**: `<runId>.r<n>`, n = 1 or 2. Refused before the claim (`job-id-refused`) when the id would hold a colon
  count other than none or exactly two, which BullMQ 5.80.4 refuses.
- **Queue**: `pi-jobs@<pointer.host>` when the pointer names a host queue, else the shared `pi-jobs`.
- **Data**: the lost job's data less `RECOVERY_STRIPPED_KEYS` (the per-attempt hold marks index.mjs writes with
  `updateData`: `podmanRestartHoldSinceMs`, `podmanRestartHoldLastMs`, `netnsKeeperHoldSinceMs`,
  `netnsKeeperHoldLastMs`, `netnsKeeperHoldStartedMs`, `netnsKeeperLoopSeen`, and `enqueueNonce`; `recoveryDataOf`),
  plus `recoveryOf` (the run id, a string), `recovery` (n, an integer) and `recoverBy` (ms since epoch, the first
  host-lost deadline). The name is the lost job's.
- **Options**: `attempts: 1`, no `deduplication`, `removeOnComplete` and `removeOnFail` 31 days (the forge jobs'
  retention).
- **Claim**: `run:recover:claim:<sanitized run id>:<n>`, `SET <key> <host> PX 7d NX` (`RECOVERY_CLAIM_TTL_MS`, the
  pointer's life). Deleted again only when this call's add failed.
- **Pending**: the sorted set `run:recover:pending`, member `{"q":"<queue>","id":"<job id>","host":"<checkpoint
  host>","at":<enqueue ms>}` (JSON; a member without a valid host or `at` is dropped as malformed), score the current
  deadline. Added by the claim's winner after the add; claimed by the host-lost sweep's `ZREM` once due; re-added with
  a later score when extended; put back with its score when handling it faulted.
- **Deadline**: first `recoverBy`, the enqueue time plus six hours (`RECOVERY_TTL_MS`); at a due deadline the sweep
  extends it by an hour (`RECOVERY_EXTEND_MS`) while the host is in the live host registry, the queue is paused or the
  registry is unreadable, never past the enqueue time plus seven days (`RECOVERY_MAX_WAIT_MS`). Lost: `host-absent` or
  `max-wait` in the log, `recovery-host-lost` in the record.
- **Acceptance**: `REQ-RUN-RECOVERY` (f); `worker/test/recovery-queue.test.mjs`.

## INT-CONFIG-OVERLAY-CONTRACT

**admin extension → worker.**

- **Contract**:
  ```
  settings.json  (PI_SETTINGS_FILE; absolute; unset -> <home>/.pi-dispatch/settings.json — the same durable state root as PI_LOGS_DIR, and the same no-home fallback)
  {
    "model":       "<optional, model id>",           // provider-native model id; the trigger's run.model shape (issue #673)
    "provider":    "<optional, provider id>",        // pi provider id; the trigger's run.provider shape (issue #673)
    "maxTurns":    <optional, int >= 1>,             // runner turn budget
