  (`INT-RUN-HISTORY-FILE-CONTRACT`'s door, which the hook does not read). The guard takes the record's token rule
  (above), so every reason the record keeps crosses as itself; the firing rules and the argv's other elements
  are UNCHANGED, checked. Tests: `worker/test/on-failure.test.mjs` ("a container's infrastructure exit and an unknown
  exit cross into argv as their tokens, where their messages read infra (#737)", "every reason the run record keeps
  crosses into argv as itself, up to its 64 characters; anything else reads infra (#737)").
- **Fires for the paid terminals only**: outcome `failed` at the TERMINAL failed event (`finishedOn`
  set -- BullMQ writes it on the non-retry branch alone, and the emit follows the move, so the guard
  reads the queue's own decision), and outcome `policy` with reason `worker-abort`, `runner-policy` or
  any member of the worker's `RUNNER_POLICY_REASONS` (`provider-auth-refused`, and since issues #501/#502
  `cost-cap`, `model-not-allowed`, `cost-cap-unenforceable` and `model-policy-unenforceable`, and the runner's six
  exit-`2` MCP refusals, `INT-RUNNER-EXIT-CODE-PROTOCOL`), or, since issue
  #596, `oom-killed` (a paid run killed for memory, which only the operator can fix by its size) at the
  completed event (policy RETURNS, so a failed-only mount would miss them).
  `provider-auth-refused` (issue #437) is a container exit `2` whose runner named a provider's refusal
  of the credential (a 401/403, or a Google or Bedrock refusal shape since issue #451): it would have
  paged as `runner-policy` anyway, and it gets its own token because a bad key needs the operator and
  fails every job until they act, which is the case this hook exists for. It fits the reason shape, so
  it crosses into argv as itself. The hook's set SPREADS the worker's `RUNNER_POLICY_REASONS` rather
  than listing its members, so every named runner reason pages as `runner-policy` did before it had a
  label. Never for completions, pre-spend refusals, retried attempts, or `operator-cancel`. A policy result
  pages unless it says `budgetReserved: false` (issue #502): `model-not-allowed` is both the runner's
  paid stop and the worker's free pre-spend refusal of a main model off the job's list, and the reason token
  alone cannot tell them apart; `mcp-config-invalid` is the same case, the runner's paid refusal and the
  pickup's free one. Every paid terminal carries `budgetReserved: true`.
- **At most once per job, best effort, and NOTHING flows back**: the hook cannot change an outcome
  (fired from listeners outside every deciding try, and `fire` never throws); its exit code and signal
  land in one `on_failure` log line -- pinned key set `{ jobId, code, detail }`, detail one of
  `exit|timeout|signal-*|spawn|unresolvable|argv-unusable` -- and are otherwise unread (`OQ-034`).
  Timeout `PI_ON_FAILURE_TIMEOUT_MS` (default 10s), then SIGTERM and SIGKILL after a 2s grace, every
  timer unref'd. The executable is resolved at FIRE time (realpath + the executable bit), so a script
  installed mid-day works and one deleted mid-day logs `unresolvable` rather than pretending.
- **Unset is absence**: no construction, no spawn, no log line, byte-identically -- the falsification
  test is a deployment diff with the variable unset, which must be empty.

**Code evidence**: worker/src/on-failure.mjs -> makeOnFailure; worker/src/start.mjs -> the
completed/failed listener bodies, HOOK_POLICY_REASONS; worker/src/config.mjs -> parseOnFailure,
onFailureTimeoutMs; worker/test/on-failure.test.mjs; worker/test/start-wiring.test.mjs.

## INT-CONSOLE-TOKENS-FILE-CONTRACT

- **AMENDED 2026-11-01 (#774)**: the CLI-only writer rule below gains two narrow
  uses of the same hardened expected-input writer under `INT-CONSOLE-SETUP-HOST`: host `up --console` may create
  an operator entry, and a granted operator browser may create/revoke a viewer entry. Browser input never names
  an operator/agent role. These paths discard durable plaintext, retain the existing hash-only shape and modes,
  audit their actual actor and preserve generation/revocation rules. Only the existing explicit `token add` and
  `token rotate` commands print durable tokens. A viewer revoke binds the exact created entry, refusing a rotated
  or replaced name. A failure minting a code after a write reports the retained entry and CLI recovery; an audit
  intent is not proof that the two files changed atomically. No existing tool gains token-write authority.

- **Upgrade order (#766)**: Upgrade both console and host `pi-dispatch` before minting an `agent` token. Older readers reject the whole file for its unknown role; older doctor/service installation fail and older up cannot establish operator readiness. The format version stays 1; roles form a closed vocabulary.

**`pi-dispatch-console token ...` → the console server and doctor.** Who may sign in to the operator console, by
name and role (`DES-OPERATOR-CONSOLE`, `REQ-CONSOLE-SECURITY`). The file holds hashes only: a copy of it signs no one
in.

- **Location**: `PI_CONSOLE_TOKENS_FILE`, default `console-tokens.json`, a relative value resolved against the
  deployment folder (`--deployment <dir>`, else the deployment pointer's `deploymentDir`, else the working
  directory). Read by the worker export `./console-tokens` (`tokensFilePath`), which the console and doctor share,
  so the two cannot disagree on where it is. The one-time login codes live beside it, in
  `<dirname(tokens file)>/console-login-codes/`.
- **Shape**:
  ```json
  { "version": 1, "generation": 0, "tokens": [
    { "name": "rob", "role": "operator", "sha256": "<64 lowercase hex>", "createdAt": "2026-10-14T09:00:00.000Z" }
  ] }
  ```
  - `version` (required): `1`. Any other value refuses the file, naming the version found, because a newer file may
    mean something this build cannot see.
  - `generation` (required): a whole number, 0 or more. `sessions end-all` raises it by one, and every session
    minted under an older generation ends on its next request.
  - `tokens[].name`: `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,31}$`, unique in the file. It is what the audit log names, so it should
    name a person.
  - `tokens[].role`: `operator` (reads and writes), `viewer` (reads), or `agent` (redacted viewer reads and only explicitly unattended transitions).
  - `tokens[].sha256`: the sha256 hex of the token, 64 lowercase hex characters, unique in the file.
  - `tokens[].createdAt`: an ISO instant, set when the token was added or last rotated.
  Any problem refuses the WHOLE file with a sentence naming the entry and the fix (invalid JSON, a missing list, a
  duplicate name or hash, a bad role, hash or date): a console that half-reads its own access list is not one an
  operator can reason about.
- **The token**: `pdc_` followed by base64url of 32 random bytes (256 bits). The prefix makes a leaked token
  greppable and recognisable to a secret scanner. It is printed ONCE, on one line, by `token add` and `token rotate`,
  and never stored, logged, audited or rendered anywhere. sha256 is the right hash for a 256-bit random secret: a KDF
  would slow the guessing of a low-entropy password and buys nothing here (`DES-OPERATOR-CONSOLE`, Rejected). A
  presented token is hashed and compared against EVERY entry with `timingSafeEqual`, with no early exit.
- **Modes and owner**: the file is a regular file (checked with `lstat`, so a symlink is refused, not followed),
  mode 0600 or tighter (`mode & 0o077` must be 0) and owned by the account that runs the console (the uid check is
  skipped where the platform has no uid). Anything else and `serve` refuses to start, and doctor names it: ssh's rule
  for a private key, for the same reason.
- **Refusal rules at start**: no file, a refused file, or a file with no `operator` entry refuses `serve`, with a
  sentence naming `pi-dispatch-console token add --name <n> --role operator`. A file inside
  any path a job container can see (a local trigger's `run.folder` or `run.skillsDir`, a `PI_DISPATCH_RUN_ROOTS` root, `PI_GLOBAL_PI_DIR`) is a doctor failure (a job that mounts the folder could read the names and roles).
- **Write protocol**: except for the narrowly scoped #774 setup writers above, only the CLI writes it
  (`token add`, `token revoke`, `token rotate`, `sessions end-all`). Each
  write reads the file, builds the new text, creates a temporary file in the same directory exclusively (`wx`) at
  0600, re-checks that the file did not change since it was read, and renames over it; a symlinked target is
  refused. `token add` creates the file at 0600 when it is absent and refuses a name that exists. `token rotate`
  gives a name a new secret (its sessions end, because their hash is gone); `token revoke` removes the entry (its
  sessions end the same way). Each change appends an audit row (`token-added`, `token-revoked`, `token-rotated`,
  `sessions-ended`) with the actor `{name: "shell", role: "shell", session: null}`. The pi extension's
  `guardedFiles()` holds the file, so the operator's pi session cannot write it with `write` or `edit`.
- **Read protocol**: the server reads it at start and on every request through the same reader, so a change
  takes effect on the next request without a restart. Two more readers since issue #708, both through the same
  reader and both read-only: `pi-dispatch service install --console` refuses when the file the SERVICE would read
  (`PI_CONSOLE_TOKENS_FILE` from the deployment `.env`, never this shell's export) is refused or holds no `operator`
  entry, the start refusal above made before a unit is written; and `pi-dispatch up` counts its `operator` entries
  in that same file (one helper, `consoleTokensPathFor`) to decide whether to name that install among its
  next steps. Neither prints a name, a hash or a count beyond "none".
- **Acceptance**: `REQ-CONSOLE-SECURITY` (a) and (i).

## INT-CONSOLE-AUDIT-LOG

- **Implemented (#774)**: setup preserves audit-before-apply and compensating failed rows.
  `INT-CONSOLE-SETUP-HOST` adds only safe operation/effect metadata through the existing row schema. Provider
  values, secret-derived input digests, raw child diagnostics, token/code bodies and private ticket payloads never
  enter a row. Confirm's intent is not an applied receipt or a cross-file transaction: partial/unknown effects
  must be reported from typed readback, never automatically retried. Existing actor/chain/mirror rules are
  UNCHANGED, checked. Setup action kinds and exhaustive schema tests accompany the implementation.

- **Agent receipts (#766)**: `actor.role` additionally accepts `agent`. HTTP uses the minted token name; pi tools use the scrubbed account login, even when a person confirmed. `action: "write"` remains the audit-before-write intent and compensating failed outcome. A successful agent write appends correlated `action: "write-applied"`, same ticket/kind/target, only after the side effect; bulk actions append one receipt per successful target. Receipt failure is reported as incomplete accounting and never retries a side effect. The overview counts verified local-console applied receipts since UTC midnight with bounded pagination, explicitly partial for an unresolved intent, retained prefix, scan bound, damaged/unavailable chain or newer rows beyond verification. Its link filters `role=agent&action=write-applied`; audit history has a broader time scope. No draft/question or standing text enters this log.

**Extension (#771).** Sandbox preparation, pin, End and Fleet mapping writes use the existing preview/confirm audit funnel. End names an exact session incarnation. No credential, command body, repository payload or terminal input is added to audit rows.

- **AMENDED 2026-10-30 (#750)**: The paid manual cron fire is kind `trigger-fire`, audited before enqueue and carrying only safe
  identity/outcome metadata. It uses the same confirmation and compensating failure-row rules as other paid actions.

**The console server, its CLI and (since issue #642) the pi extension → `audit verify`, doctor, and later a remote
console.** The record of who did what through the console, and since #642 through the `/dispatch` TUI and the
extension's tools too (`DES-OPERATOR-CONSOLE`, one audit chain; `REQ-CONSOLE-SECURITY` (h)).

- **Location**: `PI_LOGS_DIR/console-audit/YYYY-MM.jsonl`, the UTC month of the row's `at`, on the host whose
  console acted. The directory is created 0700 and each file 0600, appended with `O_APPEND`, one JSON object per
  line. The worker export `./console-audit` owns the format; the admin and doctor import it, never a copy. The
  single-instance lock `.console.lock` sits in the same directory (one `serve` per logs directory), and so does the
  short append lock `.append.lock`, held from the head read to the write so that `serve` and a CLI command appending
  at the same moment take turns instead of writing two rows with the same `seq` and `prev`. The lock holds its
  writer's pid and a random tag; it is taken over only when that pid is dead, never by age, and a writer removes it
  only while it still holds that writer's own tag (an age would compare the filesystem's
  clock with the process's); one still held after two seconds makes `append` throw.
- **Row**:
  ```json
  { "at": "2026-10-14T09:00:00.000Z", "seq": 42, "prev": "<sha256 hex of the previous raw line>",
    "actor": { "name": "rob", "role": "operator", "session": "<12 hex>" },
    "action": "write", "target": "pause-windows", "outcome": "ok",
    "beforeDigest": "<hex>", "afterDigest": "<hex>", "ticket": "<12 hex>" }
  { "at": "2026-10-15T09:00:00.000Z", "seq": 43, "prev": "<sha256 hex>",
    "actor": { "name": "rob", "role": "operator", "session": "<12 hex>" },
    "action": "write", "kind": "failed-retry-all", "target": "<job id>", "outcome": "ok",
    "count": 7, "ticket": "<12 hex>" }
  ```
  A write row's fields are in that reading order: who, the action and which write (`kind`), to what, how it went,
  why, what it holds (`reserve`) and how many (`count`), then the digests and the ticket.
  - `at`: ISO instant, stamped by the writer from its injected clock.
  - `seq`: a whole number that rises by one per row, across months.
  - `prev`: the sha256 hex of the previous row's raw line, without its newline; `null` only on the very first row
    ever written. The chain continues across month files.
  - `actor`: `{name, role, session}`. `session` is the first 12 hex characters of the sha256 of the session id,
    never the id; `null` for a CLI row, whose actor is `{name: "shell", role: "shell", session: null}`; a failed login
    names no token holder. Since issue #642 a write made from the `/dispatch` TUI, its commands and dialogs or the
    extension's tools is `{name: <the OS login, reduced to [A-Za-z0-9._@-] and 64 characters, "unknown" when there is
    none>, role: "panel", session: null}` (`panelActor`, `admin/src/audited-write.mjs`), appended to the deployment's
    `PI_LOGS_DIR`. The roles written are `operator`, `viewer`, `shell` and `panel`; `role` is an escaped string like
    `name`, not a closed set, so the verifier does not judge it.
  - `action`, exactly one of: `login`, `login-failed`, `login-code`, `logout`, `refused`, `write`, `token-added`,
    `token-revoked`, `token-rotated`, `sessions-ended`, `serve-started` (`CONSOLE_AUDIT_ACTIONS`). A `login-code` row
    comes from three writers: the console's sign-in with a code (the session's actor, or `anonymous` for a refused
    code, target `/login/code`), `pi-dispatch-console link` (actor role `shell`, target the token's name), and since
    issue #708 `/dispatch console --link`: actor role `panel`, target the token's name, outcome `ok`, appended BEFORE
    the code is made (no code without the row), and a second row with outcome `failed` and the mint's refusal as
    `reason` when the mint is then refused; both rows carry the same `ticket` (12 hex, `writeTicket`), so a reader
    takes the last row for the ticket as the outcome, as for every panel write. The row never holds the code. A
    `logout` row names a session the console ended; since #737 (PR 2) a sign-out ends every session its cookies name
    that the console holds, one `logout` row for each, and a sign-out with no session held (an unknown cookie, or
    none) is still answered and still a row, one, `anonymous`, target `/logout`, outcome `ok`, reason "no session was
    held, so only the cookie was cleared", rate limited like every other row without a session.
  - `outcome`, exactly one of: `ok`, `refused`, `failed` (`CONSOLE_AUDIT_OUTCOMES`).
  - `target`, `reason` (optional, absent when unset): short strings, control characters written out as `\u{XXXX}`,
    at most 200 characters. A refusal's `reason` starts with the guard (`host`, `origin`, `content-type`,
    `read-only`, `role`, `auth`, and since #737 (PR 2) `person`, a write from a page drawn for another person than the
    session's) followed by the console's own refusal sentence, which may name a refused Host
    hostname but never quotes a header value, a cookie or a body.
  - `beforeDigest`, `afterDigest` (optional): digests of the file before and after a write, so a row ties to a change
    without holding it. `ticket` (optional): the first 12 hex characters of the sha256 of the confirm ticket the
    write redeemed, never the ticket. A confirm appends its `ok` row BEFORE the write; when the write is then refused
    or throws, a second row with the same `ticket` and outcome `failed` follows, so the last row for a ticket is its
    outcome. A panel write has no console ticket; its rows share a fresh 12-hex correlation id in `ticket`
    (`writeTicket`), under the same ok-then-failed rule.
  - `kind` (optional, issue #642): which write a `write` row is, 1 to 40 of `a-z`, `0-9` and `-`
    (`CONSOLE_AUDIT_KIND_RE`), a closed charset rather than an escaped string, so a reader can group rows by it and
    no caller can carry text in it. `action` stays `write`; `kind` only names the write. The kinds written:
    the panel's and the console's shared configuration and control writes `trigger-add`, `trigger-edit`,
    `trigger-delete`, `setting-set`, `setting-unset`, `pause-window-add`, `pause-window-edit`, `pause-window-delete`,
    `limit-add`, `limit-edit`, `limit-delete`, `project-add`, `project-edit`, `project-delete`, `envelope-set`,
    `priorities-set`, `allocation-revert`, `secret-profile-add`, `secret-profile-remove`, `secret-bundle-add` and
    `secret-bundle-remove` (issue #704, AMENDED 2026-10-20), `cancel-active`,
    `cancel-held`, `fleet-pause`, `fleet-resume` and `run-enqueue`; and the console's own `queue-pause`,
    `queue-resume`, `failed-retry`, `failed-remove`, `failed-retry-all`, `failed-remove-all`, `held-cancel-all`,
    `run-rerun`, `trigger-fire`, `parked-answer`, (issue #646) `steer-withdraw` and (issue #737, PR 3a) `cancel-queued`, a job that
    never started taken out of its queue, `target` its job id; and `steer` (issue #646), which the console and
    the panel (the TUI's `t` and `T`) both write. The list is descriptive: the writer enforces the charset, not the list, and
    the console's configuration actions write the kind of their action's own name, plus `pause-windows-set` for the
    whole-list replace.
  - `reserve` (optional, issue #642): the micro-dollars a paid action (a re-run, an answer to a parked run) will
    hold, as the preview showed it (`estimateReserve`), a non-negative safe integer. Absent when the action is not
    paid, no dollar cap applies, or the action takes no new reserve (a `steer`, which spends from its run's own).
  - `count` (optional, issue #642): a bulk action's size, a positive safe integer. A bulk action writes one row per
    job, `target` that job's id, every row carrying the same `count` and `ticket`, so a reader groups a bulk action
    by its ticket and reads each job's outcome from its own last row. A resume (`fleet-resume`, `queue-resume`)
    writes `count` too, as the number of jobs waiting to start in the queues it resumes, as its preview counted them
    (none when none waits or the count could not be read), so a reader takes `count` by the row's `kind`. CORRECTED
    2026-10-24 (#737 PR 2): this bullet called every `count` a bulk action's size, which a resume's has not been since
    #642; the console's audit page says the two apart.
  - An answer to a parked run is recorded by the parked run's job id in `target` and the sha256 of the answer text
    in `afterDigest`; the text is never in a row.
  - A message into a running job (kind `steer`, issue #646) is recorded by `<job id>#<message id>` in `target`
    (`steerAuditTarget`; `#` is outside the job-id charset, so the split on the last `#` is exact, and a job id past
    166 characters is cut before it so the 32-hex message id always fits the 200-character cap) and the sha256 of the
    message text, as the run's inbox stores it after the scrub, in `afterDigest`; the text is never in a row. A
    `steer-withdraw` row has the same `target` and nothing else of the message.
  - An unknown action or outcome throws in the writer: the vocabulary is closed. A `kind`, `reserve` or `count` of
    the wrong shape throws too, and writes nothing. A row without them is a row from before them and verifies as it
    always did.
- **Rate-limited refusals**: a refusal of a request that carried no session (`actor.name` `anonymous`) is written
  one row each up to 60 a minute (burst 120). Past that, refusals are counted, and the count is written as one row,
  `action: "refused"`, `target: "(rate limited)"`, its `reason` starting with the number, just before the next
  allowed row. A refusal from a signed-in session is always its own row. Since #737 (PR 2) the anonymous `logout` row
  of a sign-out with no session held is limited and counted the same way, so the count is of rows, and the reason
  says so ("3 more rows without a session (refusals and sign-outs) went unwritten one by one (limit 60 a minute)").
- **Never in a row**: a token, a login code, a cookie value, a session id, a request body, or any payload text.
- **Head recovery**: the writer keeps no head in memory. Every append reads the newest month file's last line (a
  bounded 64 KiB tail read) under the append lock, so a restart, or a CLI command writing while `serve` runs,
  continues the one chain. A last line that does not parse makes every append throw until the file is moved aside;
  doctor and `audit verify` name it.
- **Failure**: `append` is synchronous and throws on any failure, and the caller refuses the write it was going to
  record. A write that cannot be audited does not happen.
- **Verification**: `pi-dispatch-console audit verify` and doctor walk every month file in order and check each `prev`
  and `seq`. The result is `{ok: true, rows, startsAt}` or `{ok: false, rows, broken: {file, line, reason}}`, naming
  the first broken link. A row whose `kind`, `reserve` or `count` is present and not of the shape above is a broken
  link too. The first row of the oldest SURVIVING file is not checked against a predecessor: when the
  retention reaper removed older months, verify reports where the chain starts (`startsAt`, the file and `seq`), and
  does not call it broken. A broken chain is a doctor warning. Since #737 (PR 2) a caller may ask `withLast: true`
  (the console's audit page does, cached 30 s), which adds three fields to either shape: `last: {file, line, seq}`, the
  place and `seq` of the last row the chain vouches for (null when none); `suspect: {file, line, seq}`, the row before
  a break whose line carries no `prev` that matches it, or null; and `files: [{file, seq, rows}]`, oldest first, each
  month file the walk passed a row in, the `seq` of its first row (its line 1) and how many rows the walk passed in
  it, so row `s` of an entry is at line `s - seq + 1` of its file. A row is vouched for only by the line after it,
  when that line's `prev` matches the row's hash: an edit to a row leaves its own line well formed and moves only its
  hash. So at a break whose line does not carry a matching `prev` (it does not parse, its `prev` is not a hash, or it
  is another hash, whatever else is wrong with the line: the `prev` is compared before the line's action, outcome and
  fields are judged), the row before is not vouched for either: it is `suspect`, and `last` is the row before it.
  Only a line whose `prev` matched and that fails another check (its seq, action, outcome or fields) is damaged
  alone, `last` then the row before it and `suspect` null. On an intact chain `last` is the newest row walked, which
  no line vouches for yet, since none follows it. Without `withLast` the result is exactly
  the one above, which doctor, the CLI and the tests compare whole. The row format, the files and the chain are
  unchanged.
- **Retention**: reaped on `PI_LOG_RETENTION_DAYS` by the worker (`makeConsoleAuditReaper`, at boot and on each
  retention sweep, beside the allocation log reaper), because the worker always runs and the console may not. Only
  names of the `YYYY-MM.jsonl` shape are touched, and the newest file is never reaped, since it holds the head.
- **The Valkey mirror**: each row `serve` writes is also pushed, after the file holds it and best effort, onto the
  list `console:audit` (`LPUSH` then `LTRIM` to 500 rows), the `alloc:log` precedent, so a console on another host
  can show recent rows later. The short-lived CLI commands do not connect to Valkey, so their rows are in the file
  only, and so are the panel's (`panelAudit` builds a writer without the mirror). A mirror failure never fails the
  append; the file is the record.
- **Failure, for the panel** (issue #642): a panel write whose `ok` row cannot be appended is refused in the shape its
  funnel already uses (`{invalid}`, `{refused}`, or an allocation `refused` outcome) with the sentence "the audit log
  could not be written, so nothing was changed; check PI_LOGS_DIR" (`AUDIT_REFUSAL`). A compensating `failed` row that
  cannot be appended is logged and swallowed, leaving an `ok` row for a write that did not land: the safe direction
  to be wrong in. The setup wizard's writes are not audited (`DES-ADMIN-VIA-PI-EXTENSION`).
- **Acceptance**: `REQ-CONSOLE-SECURITY` (f), (g) and (h), `REQ-OPERATOR-CONSOLE-ACTIONS` (j) and (k).

## INT-CONSOLE-SETUP-HOST

- **Status**: **IMPLEMENTED** (issue #774), after prerequisite specs PR #783. This is a local setup
  protocol and private action-state contract, not an additional listener, shell API or public snapshot format.
- **Authority**: the console process must be started with `serve --host-setup`, explicitly persisted only by
  `service install --console --host-setup` or the shown equivalent in `up --console`. Bind it to the canonical
  deployment directory, current uid, Linux user systemd/macOS LaunchAgent manager and verified durable worker
  package/entry. Resolve these on the host, never from action input. Existing services default off; reinstall
  without the flag and restart revokes the grant and terminates its children/private state. It cannot be
  activated by `.env`, deployment pointer, shared queue/host metadata or a model tool. Other hosts/accounts,
  Windows, Linux system scope, ambiguous entries and foreign units refuse with the supported terminal path.
- **Operation set**: version 1 permits install-and-start/start/stop/restart for the deployment's own worker or
  installed receiver user service, start-only of its missing/stopped egress proxy after runtime endpoint-locality
  verification, explicit non-live/non-fixing `setupReadOnly` doctor without probe containers, create-only provider API-key assignment, and viewer add/revoke
  through the hardened token writer.
  The implementation's registration/protocol/policy enumerations must be checked both ways. No arbitrary command,
  executable, argument vector, path, environment, forge credential or operator-token mutation comes from HTTP.
  Existing `up` performs bootstrap only on the host and is never a browser operation.
- **Plan and apply**: the shared planner supplies server-derived target identity, exact effect plan, expected
  file/unit/runtime identities and current exposure facts. Preview performs no mutation. Existing single-use
  session/action tickets bind the plan; confirm bodies cannot swap it. Refuse a missing host grant, wrong role,
  read-only console, changed sign-in, changed plan, unsafe ownership or stale file/unit before apply. Incomplete
  queue/cron exposure refuses operations that can start/restart a worker; key writes, viewer operations and
  doctor do not acquire an unrelated queue-scan prerequisite. A per-deployment lock serializes setup mutations
  across callers, including browser viewer writes and independent host children. A stale lock fails closed;
  host recovery inspects its PID/external effects before removal rather than racing an automatic reaper.
  Revalidate after taking it; no lock is represented as stopping ordinary job admission. Record
  audit intent before the first effect. Recheck the authorizing session/grant immediately before dispatch, monitor
  their loss and abort further dispatches. An already submitted service-manager action may finish after
  cancellation; bound its child lifetime and report observed partial/unknown effects without retrying it. Do not
  promise an in-memory parent session can atomically revoke an external manager action already submitted.
- **Version 1 wire shape**: `worker/src/setup-contract.mjs` is the derivable closed vocabulary. Requests carry
  `version`, 32-hex `id`, `phase` (`plan`, `apply`, `status`), `operation`, optional private 64-hex `expected`, and
  provider-only `input` (`provider`, `key`, `value`). Apply requires `expected`; only apply may carry a value.
  Results carry matching version/id/operation, closed `state`/`reason`, optional closed effects and a private plan:
  digest, component, user manager, local host/account, effects and optional canonical provider/key/workerName.
  The worker name is the validated effective `PI_WORKER_NAME`, so readiness binds the real heartbeat identity.
  Plan hashes can include secret-bearing source files and never enter HTTP, audit or shared state. CLI exit 2
  with a matching validated refused result remains a determinate refusal; other broken/nonzero replies are
  refused before mutation or unknown after apply dispatch. The parent revalidates entry ownership, ancestors,
  canonical path, package/version and captured CLI/metadata content identity before each dispatch.
- **Transport and bounds**: run the known worker entry with `shell:false` and fixed argv. The child receives one
  versioned JSON request on stdin (at most 64 KiB), with server-chosen operation id and validated operation
  fields; the key value, if any, never rides argv/environment. Unknown versions, keys and operations refuse.
  Output is at most 256 KiB of versioned typed result/progress; raw stdout/stderr, error text and uncontrolled
  strings are not console response content. Bound service/egress operations to 60 seconds and doctor to 120,
  terminate then kill after a 2-second grace, and clean up on shutdown. The child loads only its own validated
  deployment service environment. Console environment and bundle retain their secret/provider-SDK exclusions.
- **Result**: report a server-chosen operation id, closed operation/stage/reason tokens and validated effects.
  Distinguish unchanged, applied, partial, unknown and refused. A timeout or broken result after dispatch may mean
  partial/unknown, not "nothing changed". Never retry it automatically. "Unit written", "start accepted" and
  "waiting for heartbeat" are distinct from Ready. Worker starts wait at most 90 seconds for an actual fresh
  heartbeat; expiry leaves a named timeout/check state with recovery. Receiver manager readback is an applied
  operation, while forge/provider/egress readiness still comes from their separate published doctor evidence.
  Worker starts require a heartbeat whose observation and beat are at or after dispatch; a cached pre-start row,
  missing/future observation timestamp, stale row or degraded registry cannot become fresh as wall time passes.
  Audit intent or a zero exit cannot manufacture readiness. Bounded progress may reach operator live panels;
  observer projections include safe state only and no account/path, body, token or private result.
- **Service/exposure checks**: include actual multi-unit dependencies and configuration effects; refuse adoption,
  shared/foreign ownership or unpreviewable disruption. Show timestamped current queue/cron counts and existing
  paid-action reserve estimates. The scan explicitly bypasses the display waiting cache; duplicate job ids across
  queues refuse because the shared reserve reader keys by id. Unknown/partial exposure refuses start, never reads zero. No budget is reserved
  for the setup action. Worker admission and reservations remain per job. Stop/restart/Undo explicitly warn of
  interruption, including work arriving after preview, and never claim to undo spent money. Proxy mutation is
  start-only; destructive restart/removal/rules refresh retain terminal recovery and its active-job precautions.
- **Private key state**: only canonical API-key names selected by the server are writable; reject bearer/OAuth
  slots and providers without a supported key slot. Limit UTF-8 values to 4 KiB and private entries to 32 per
  process, at most one per session, with at most 60 seconds lifetime. Reject at capacity rather than silently
  evicting a preview the person is confirming. Keep value/expected inputs outside ordinary diff/flash/live/cache
  metadata. Private input comparison hashes never enter audit or public output. Expiry runs without new traffic;
  guarded Cancel, any redeem attempt, logout/revocation/role change and shutdown release the state. Best-effort
  buffer clearing is not a guarantee about JavaScript string copies. Reject controls/command references,
  duplicate/nonblank assignments, shadowed sources and managed-binding conflicts. The writer rechecks owner,
  mode, real target and bytes before exclusive temporary-file creation, then repeats the expected-input check
  immediately before atomic rename; unsafe or intervening inputs change nothing. Browser submission clears the
  field/transient value references and bypasses ordinary retained request bodies and Preview again replay; a
  refusal or expiry requires re-entry. The preview countdown uses this 60-second lifetime. A successful save
  never implicitly restarts a worker or claims its running environment reloaded.
- **Private viewer result**: the token role is fixed to viewer; the existing unique-name/expected-input writer
  supplies the entry and discards plaintext. Mint a one-use 60-second login code only after its audit/write
  succeeds. Bind the private code record to the exact created token hash/incarnation, viewer role and current
  tokens-file generation; redemption revalidates all three before making a session. Rotation, role change,
  revocation/recreation with the same name, or generation change invalidates it. Return a same-origin
  `/login/code#<code>&next=/setup` link only to the initiating operator's confirm response. A dedicated private
  success path displays/copies it rather than using the generic success reload. It is absent from SSR,
  shared flash, caches, state APIs, SSE/reconnect and logs. Never persist that DOM result to browser storage;
  remove it when its result expires or sign-in changes. Explain loopback/tunnel reachability and that a link
  grants a session, not a retained token. If minting fails, explicitly report the retained viewer entry and host
  recovery. Revoke is separately confirmed against that exact entry, never an independent same-name replacement.
- **Bootstrap link**: host `up --console` preserves or creates an operator entry without printing/retaining its
  durable plaintext, asks explicitly among multiple operators and prints the existing one-use 60-second link
  only after bounded console health succeeds. Failure after token/service mutation reports what remains and
  exact recovery. `token add`/`token rotate` retain their existing one-line durable-token output; no browser
  operator mint or new token-print exception is admitted.
- **Projection**: `/api/state`'s public shape is UNCHANGED, checked by this prerequisite. `/setup` reuses existing
  panel/SSE framing with role-separated caches. Setup action progress is bounded state, not authority; private
  tickets/keys/invitation links never enter the snapshot. `dispatch_setup` remains a read, never a setup executor.
- **Acceptance**: `REQ-BROWSER-FIRST-RUN-SETUP`; tests verify the real packaged child boundary,
  expected-input writer, session isolation, lifecycle limits, counterexamples and meaningful end-to-end effects.

## INT-CONSOLE-STATE-API

- **Agent projection and answer privacy (#766, #772)**: An `agent` session receives a separate allowlisted projection and cache/event group: no operator/job prose, private phase names/notes, raw failure text, resolver paths, variable names, draft bodies, citations, classifications, rules or standing answers. Catalog failure tokens and typed numeric facts remain. `/api/run` keeps its existing text-free shape; draft helpers are excluded when resolving a target URL or a newer workload. Private answer data is page-specific and operator-only, including live refresh, never added to shared `/api/state`. The operator Parked list may show verdict/source names and links, while viewer/agent rows carry only draft existence and answering identity/time. `/parked/rules` is operator-only and shows reviewed configuration; it is not a rule mutation API.

**Extension (#751):** `/config/secrets`, `/config/connections` and `/config/project?id=` are non-live viewer pages.
The project id follows PROJECT_ID_RE; readable absence is the no-project 404, unreadable projects remain
unavailable. Connections reads deployment source keys, allowlist, model-endpoint definitions and live slot leases
only for its page and its safe tool projection. Endpoint observations carry closed `counting` values: `fleet`,
`per-machine`, `worker-name-absent` or `unknown`. Only `fleet` can carry an observed integer `used`; other modes
carry null, with declared `slots` retained. An unavailable fleet lease read also has null `used`, distinct from
an observed zero. These are console/tool projections over existing worker gates, not new lease or host telemetry.
The page directs 401/404 diagnosis to forge history; receiver logs can help with 503/enqueue failures and do not
cover early request refusals or every 503. No such values enter `/api/state`; STATE_VERSION, its keys and
the event-stream protocol are UNCHANGED, checked. Resolver action response keys/tickets stay the same, while
all displayed diff lines, summary/Undo sentences and refusals shorten resolver/root paths to their last folder.
The ticket retains real operands server-side. Secret/bundle values and references never enter a response;
agent reads further omit variable names. Worker env, trigger, project, endpoint, lease, run-record and hook
file/process contracts are UNCHANGED, checked; the console reads their existing published facts.

**Extension (#750, trigger list):** `POST /api/trigger-check` is a hypothetical read, not an action. A viewer
session suffices, including on a read-only console. Host, same-Origin/fetch-site, JSON, body-size and
`x-console-as` person guards apply before its bounded event input is evaluated. It takes no query parameters.
Its closed input vocabulary and per-field limits come from `admin/src/trigger-check.mjs`, shared with the
form; the server's body ceiling applies too. The strict, bounded whole-file read must succeed before the
receiver's own filters judge precedence. Success returns `{ "html": "<escaped result region>" }`; invalid
event/configuration returns the same result shape with status 400. Missing infrastructure is a fixed 503;
body/auth/session refusals keep the existing JSON error contract. No response includes event text, private
trigger text or a constructed queue job. The request creates no ticket, job, reservation or audit row and
persists no input. The normal request log names the fixed route only. `GET /api/state`, its version and
payload remain UNCHANGED, checked; no list-specific history or checker text is added to shared state.


**Extension (#649):** `/api/run` and parked folds may carry optional validated id-only `approval` audit metadata under `INT-APPROVAL-STATE-CONTRACT`. The existing parked-answer action accepts optional approve/decline decisions, converted to command text before its shared planner; request binding and worker authority remain mandatory.

**The console → scripts and later integrations.** `GET /api/state`: the deployment's live snapshot as JSON, so a
script reads the console without scraping a page (issue #641, `DES-OPERATOR-CONSOLE`,
`REQ-OPERATOR-CONSOLE-SCREENS` (k)).

- **Request**: `GET /api/state`, no query. It needs a session (`pdc_session`, from `POST /login` with a token, or
  from a one-time link); without one it is answered `401` with a JSON error, never a redirect, as every `/api/*`
  route is. The viewer role is enough. It is a GET and has no side effect beyond the request moving its session's
  `lastSeen`, as every request does. **Since #737 (PR 2) the 401 body says why**, on every `/api/*` route and every
  write that needs a session: `{ "error": "sign in first", "ended": "<reason>" }`, `ended` one of `ENDED_REASONS`
  (`idle`, `max`, `revoked`, `role`, `all`, `elsewhere`, `restart`, `admin/src/console/session-ends.mjs`) when the
  cookie names a session that ended (`restart` only as a possibility: a well-formed id this process does not know,
  while it has been up for less than `PI_CONSOLE_MAX_HOURS` and has forgotten no ended session), and null otherwise
  (no cookie, or one with no reason to give). The list's eighth word, `switched`, is never this 401's: no session
  ends for it (below). The sign-in posts need no session and their own refusals are not this
  401: `POST /login`'s wrong token (`{"error": "that token is not valid for this console"}`) and `POST /login/code`'s
  refused link carry `error` alone. The 401 sends NO Set-Cookie, where before PR 2 it cleared the cookie: a script's
  next request still carries the cookie, so it can still read why, and a 401 never clears a newer cookie another
  tab's sign-in set meanwhile (a page's 303 to `/login` still clears it, and so does sign-out). `error` is the
  sentence it always was, so a script that read it reads the same. And while the console cannot use its tokens file,
  a request that carries a session cookie is answered `503` with `{ "error": "the console's tokens file cannot be used
  right now; the operator should run pi-dispatch doctor" }` (`TOKENS_UNUSABLE`), with no Set-Cookie and the session
  kept, on every route that needs a session (`REQ-CONSOLE-SECURITY` (i)): a script waits and asks again rather than
  signing in. `POST /logout` needs none: it ends every session its cookies name that the console holds, and answers
  `200` with the clearing Set-Cookie whatever the tokens file's state. **Since #737 (PR 2) a request may say whose page
  it comes from**, `<name>.<role>`, in the header `x-console-as` (`PERSON_HEADER`; the console's own page sends it
  on every preview and confirm, and an event stream says it in its query instead, `INT-CONSOLE-EVENT-STREAM`). When
  it names another person than the session the cookie names, the request is refused after auth and before the role,
  the body or the handler: `409` `{ "error": "this browser is now signed in as someone else, so nothing was changed;
  sign in again", "ended": "switched" }` (`PERSON_CHANGED`), a write's with `html` (the confirm bar's refusal, whose
  Look again the console's page sends to `/login?ended=switched`) and an audit row. A request that sends no such
  header is not checked: a script is held to the cookie alone, as before. A write's `503` `TOKENS_UNUSABLE` carries
  `html` too, the confirm bar's refusal: since #737 PR 3a in the setup state ("This console cannot take this
  action"), its sentence `TOKENS_UNUSABLE`'s words with `pi-dispatch doctor` in the code face, and Close, since
  nothing on the page can fix the file and a reload would meet the same 503 (it offered Look again); the `error`
  beside it is the sentence as it always was.
- **Response**: `200`, `Content-Type: application/json`, with the security headers of every console response
  (`Cache-Control: no-store` among them). The body is ONE fleet reader snapshot (`createFleetReader`, the reader the
  pages and the `/dispatch` panel read), projected by `stateOf` (`admin/src/console/live.mjs`) to these keys and no
  others (a test pins the key list):
  ```json
  { "version": 1, "at": 1760432400000, "role": "operator",
    "paused": { "state": false, "partial": false },
    "counts": { "waiting": 0, "active": 1, "paused": 0, "delayed": 0, "failed": 0 },
    "queues": [ { "queue": "pi-jobs", "paused": false, "counts": {} } ],
    "workers": 2, "fleetDegraded": false,
    "hosts": [ { "name": "mac", "lastBeatAgeMs": 1200, "capacity": { "memMiB": 8192, "cpuCenti": 400, "concurrency": 3 }, "running": 1 } ],
    "budget": { "day": 3, "week": 10, "month": 40, "tokensToday": 120000 },
    "dollars": { "unreachable": false, "windows": [ { "ledger": "global", "scope": null, "window": "day", "capMicros": 5000000, "counterMicros": 1200000, "full": false } ] },
    "parked": [ { "target": "acme/web#12", "kind": "github", "jobId": "gh-...", "ageMs": 60000, "chainCount": null } ],
    "parkedUnknown": false,
    "failures24h": 0, "failures24hFloor": false,
    "refusals24h": { "count": 3, "top": [ { "reason": "scope-cap", "count": 2 }, { "reason": "over-budget", "count": 1 } ] },
    "active": [ { "jobId": "gh-...", "queue": "pi-jobs", "startedAt": 1760432400000, "host": "mac" } ],
    "schedulers": [ { "name": "nightly", "next": 1760432400000, "overdue": false, "overdueMs": 0, "stalls": 0 } ],
    "schedulerStallMax": 3,
    "failed": { "unreachable": false, "rows": [ { "jobId": "...", "queue": "pi-jobs", "attemptsMade": 3, "endedAt": 1760432400000, "failedReason": "..." } ], "more": 0 } }
  ```
  `parkedUnknown` true means the parked list could not be read, so an empty `parked` is not "nobody waiting". A
  folder-scoped dollar window's `scope` is null rather than a host path. **Since issue #644 each `active` row gains
  `progress`** (`INT-RUN-PROGRESS-KEY`), integers and the running call's checked tool name only, never a phase name or
  a note, and null when the job has no readable progress key; within `version: 1`, an added key (`STATE_VERSION`
  unchanged): `{ "turn", "steps", "failed", "running": { "tool", "since" } | null, "phase": { "index", "count",
  "done", "total" } | null, "ended", "updatedAt" }` (`activeProgressOf`), `running` the newest open call, `count` the
  length of the phase list, and `updatedAt` the key's last write, so a script can apply the stale rule
  (`INT-RUN-PROGRESS-KEY`: not ended and older than 180 s). **Since issue #646 each `active` row also gains `steer`
  and `inbox`** (`INT-STEER-INBOX-CONTRACT`), added keys within `version: 1`: `steer` is true for a job whose data
  arms `run.steer` and false otherwise; `inbox` is that job's messages WITHOUT TEXT, `[ { "id", "mode", "source",
  "state", "at", "bytes" } ]` (`inboxOf`), each field rebuilt against the inbox's own vocabularies (`id` 32 lowercase
  hex, `mode` `steer` or `followUp`, `source` `forge`, `console`, `cli` or `panel`, `state` `queued`, `written`,
  `delivered`, `withdrawn` or `late`, `at` milliseconds, `bytes` the text's UTF-8 size), a field that fails being null
  (`bytes` 0). `inbox` is null for a job that is not steer-armed, for one whose inbox could not be read that tick, and
  past the first 16 steer-armed active jobs a snapshot reads (`STEER_INBOX_ROWS_MAX`), so `[]` always means no
  message. Both roles get the same. **Since issue #647 each `parked` row gains `jobId`**, an added key within
  `version: 1`: the parked run's job id in the run-id charset, else null, for both roles, so a script or the terminal
  chat can open the run or answer it through the `parked-answer` action without a second lookup. The fleet reader's
  snapshot also marks each parked row `answering` (the job taking its answer, false, or null when unknown; review round
  1 of #647), which the `/parked` page and the overview draw; `/api/state`'s parked projection does NOT carry it (the
  keys above are the whole row), and a script asks `/api/run`'s `pendingRunOnTarget` for one run instead. **Since
  issue #710 the document gains `refusals24h`**, an added key within `version: 1`, beside `failures24h` and from the same
  window: `{ "count", "top": [ { "reason", "count" } ] }`, the runs of the last 24 hours whose outcome the console calls
  "refused" (`refusalsIn`: a `policy` record, but NOT one with `operator-cancel`, which the console calls "cancelled"),
  and the five most frequent reasons by count, then token, each `reason` the record's token charset
  (`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$`) or the row is left out; null where `failures24h` is null (the runs could not be read)
  and for a snapshot without the field. `failures24hFloor` marks both counts as floors. The same for both roles.
  AMENDED 2026-10-26 (#737, PR 4a), no key added or renamed: `failures24h` counts the runs of the window whose outcome
  the console calls "failed" (`outcomeWord(...).word`), as `refusals24h` counts those it calls "refused", where it
  counted `outcome === "failed"`; the console's words now call the three recovery ends the worker records as `policy`
  (`recovery-cap`, `recovery-checkpoint-absent`, `recovery-unsafe-extensions`) failed, so they move from
  `refusals24h` (count and top reasons) to `failures24h`. Each key still means what it says, the day's failed and
  refused runs in the console's words, so `version` stays 1; a script that compared `failures24h` with its own count of
  `outcome: "failed"` records reads it larger by the recovery ends. Test: `admin/test/read-model-pages.test.mjs` ("the
  parked rows carry the record's project, a project id only; failures24h counts a recovery end as the failure it reads
  as (#737)"). The snapshot's parked rows gain `project` (the record's, a project id only, else null), which the
  `/parked` page draws and `/api/state`'s parked projection does NOT carry. Whether
  a worker is online is not a key of its own: it is a host whose last beat is at most 60000 ms old, the overview's
  rule, and the overview says none is only when `workers` (BullMQ's connected workers on the shared queue, free of any
  host clock; null, read as 0, when unknown) is not above zero either, and judges neither way while `fleetDegraded` is
  true. AMENDED 2026-10-25 (#737 PR 3b), words only, no key changed: `hosts[].lastBeatAgeMs` is the beat's age as the
  overview takes it, Valkey's measure of the row's last refresh where the reader had it (`ttlAgeMs`, `beatAgeOf`,
  `INT-HOST-REGISTRY-CONTRACT`), else the console's clock against the host's beat time (`staleMs`), so a script that
  applies the rule to it judges a host whose clock runs behind as the overview does; `schedulers[].name` is the
  scheduler's key, the cron trigger's id (null when the reader refused it), never BullMQ's job name.
- **What it never holds**: a token, a cookie, a session id, a host path beyond what the panel shows, a secret's value
  or resolver reference (secret profiles appear by name only), a job's `.data`, log or transcript text, or a steer
  message's text or sender. A record's
  `jobId`, `target` and `parentJobId` are JSON strings, encoded by `JSON.stringify` and never interpreted; a script
  that puts one in HTML escapes it itself.
- **The role difference**: for a viewer, every failed job's `failedReason` key is absent (not null), the one free text the snapshot carries. The operator gets it scrubbed (control bytes replaced, 120
  characters at most, `DES-ADMIN-VIA-PI-EXTENSION`'s FAILED surface). Nothing else differs between the roles.
- **Unreachable parts**: a part the reader could not read says so with a boolean (`failed.unreachable`,
  `dollars.unreachable`, `fleetDegraded`, `parkedUnknown`), never with the error's text, which can name hosts and
  addresses and stays in the console's own log; read beside it, an empty list or a zero is "unknown", not "nothing
  there". `failures24hFloor: true` means `failures24h` is a floor. When the fleet cannot be read at all (Valkey
  down), the answer is `503` with `{ "version": 1, "error": "<a fixed sentence>" }` instead of a partial body.
- **Stability**: within `version: 1`, keys are only ever added. A key removed or renamed, or a value whose meaning
  changes, raises `version`; a script should check `version` and ignore keys it does not know. The keys of the
  nested projections follow the read model's snapshot and are held by the same tests.
- **One run: `GET /api/run`** (issue #647, `REQ-TERMINAL-CHAT`, `admin/src/console/run-api.mjs`). One run and the
  chat it can have now; the terminal chat asks it which mode to open and polls it every 5 s for its status line.
  - **Request**: `GET /api/run?id=<job id>` or `GET /api/run?url=<issue, pull request or merge request link>`, with a
    session; the viewer role is enough. Exactly one of the two, given once, and no other key; `id` in the run-id
    charset; `url` at most 2048 characters. `?url=` resolves through `forgeTargetOf` (the inverse of `forgeLinkOf`,
    on github.com and the deployment's own `GITLAB_URL`, `FORGEJO_URL` and `AZURE_ORG_URL`, also reading GitHub's
    `/pull/<n>` and Forgejo's `/pulls/<n>`) and then the run history: one runs page whose `limit` (`TARGET_RUNS_MAX`
    100) counts runs matching the target exactly (`readRunsPage`'s `match` predicate, `targetKeyOf`: the repository
    path case-insensitive, the number's leading zeros dropped), over a scan of at most `RUNS_PAGE_EXAMINE_MAX` (2000)
    records examined, never the filter's substring `q`; the newest run on that target is the run.
  - **Response**: `200` JSON, every field rebuilt by its shape, null when it fails:
    ```json
    { "version": 1,
      "run": { "id": "gh-...", "jobId": "gh-...", "kind": "github", "repo": "acme/web", "target": "acme/web#12",
               "triggerType": "label", "triggerIndex": 0, "flow": "fix", "outcome": "completed", "reason": null,
               "startedAt": "2026-10-18T09:00:00.000Z", "finishedAt": "2026-10-18T09:12:00.000Z",
               "provider": "anthropic", "model": "...", "host": "mac", "backend": "docker", "project": null,
               "attempt": 1, "exitCode": 0, "turns": 14, "parentJobId": null, "recoveryOf": null,
               "session": { "kept": true, "resumed": false } },
      "state": "finished", "mode": "fork", "says": null, "activeJobId": null,
      "steer": { "armed": false, "open": false },
      "transcript": { "exists": true, "ended": true, "outcome": "completed" },
      "progress": { "live": false, "turns": 14, "steps": 30, "failed": 0, "interrupted": 0,
                    "phase": null, "ended": true, "updatedAt": null },
      "forgeLink": "https://github.com/acme/web/issues/12",
      "newerRunOnTarget": null,
      "pendingRunOnTarget": null }
    ```
    `run.id` is the id asked about; the other `run` fields come from its record and are null while the job has no
    record (a running job's is written at its end). `state` is one of `active`, `queued`, `parked`, `answered`,
    `finished`, `unknown` (`RUN_STATES`); `mode` is `live`, `reply`, `fork` or null, from `chatModeOf`, and `says` is
    null or one of its fixed refusal sentences (`CHAT_REFUSALS`). `activeJobId` is the job itself when active, else
    the #645 recovery job its run goes on as, else null; `steer` and `transcript` are that active job's (else the
    run's own): `steer.armed` whether its data arms `run.steer`, `steer.open` true, false, or null when the open key
    could not be read, and both null when the inbox could not be read at all (never a guessed false); `transcript.outcome` one of the live stream's outcomes or `unknown` once ended. `progress` is
    the live key's integers while the key is the run's own, else the record's (`live: false`), else null.
    `newerRunOnTarget` is the job id of a later run on the same kind and target, or null when there is none or the
    history could not be searched (also when a truncated scan stopped before the record's own instant); the fork uses
    it to warn that the session holds that run's turns too. `pendingRunOnTarget` is the job id queued or running on a
    parked run's target that takes its answer (it has no record yet; found by the bounded queue scan
    `readPendingOnTargets`, `DES-TERMINAL-CHAT`), else null; with it the run is `answered` and refused
    (`CHAT_REFUSALS.answering`), and a scan that cannot tell makes it `unknown` (`CHAT_REFUSALS.parkedTooMany` when
    the queues hold more jobs than the scan's budget, else `parkedUnknown`). A run whose #645 recovery job is
    waiting, delayed or prioritized is `queued` (`CHAT_REFUSALS.recoveryQueued`), never `finished`.
    `session` is two booleans, never the key. `run.model` is the record's bare model id checked by the runs filter's
    own `RUN_MODEL_RE` (one optional leading `@` or `~`, then a letter or digit, then letters, digits and
    `. _ : / @ + -`, at most 128 characters; issue #668), so a priced `@cf/...` or `~...` id is kept, not null.
  - **Errors** (each `{ "error": "<sentence>" }`, the sentence never echoing the value): `400` for a query refusal or
    a URL that names no target on a forge this deployment knows; `404` for a run that this host's history, the run mirror
    or the queue knows, and for a target with no run (the sentence says a running job's record is written at its end,
    so give its run id, and after a truncated scan that it searched the newest 2000 runs); AMENDED 2026-10-26 (#737, PR
    4a): for a run id, by one rule the run page's status follows too (`runPlaces`), `404` only when no place a run is
    kept shows one and every place was read and said it holds none (`runAbsent`, the run page's run-not-found rule:
    this host's record file and the fleet's run mirror both read with no record, every queue the kill switch flips
    asked, over a keyspace scan started after the question, with no such job and no active or queued recovery of its
    run, the live transcript and the progress key read and absent), and `503` with `runNotTold`'s sentence ("whether a
    run with that id exists could not be told: this console could not read <places>; try again", each place said in
    its `RUN_PLACES` words, `admin/src/read-model.mjs`, joined "a, b and c", and no cause) when no place shows a run
    while one of them could not be read (its record, a queue lookup that failed or ran over a set that was not whole,
    the transcript or the progress key), which it answered `404` before (a queue lookup that failed, the fixed queue
    sentence below); a run some place shows is answered as before, a base run whose job the queue no longer holds
    while its recovery runs or waits included; `409` for
    an Azure work item whose runs are in several repositories of its project, with `"candidates": [ { "target", "jobId"
    } ]` (the newest run per repository, at most 10); `503` for a run some place shows whose queue state could not be
    read (`RUN_UNREADABLE`, a fixed sentence: a mode judged on half the facts is worse than none; since #737 PR 4a it
    names no cause, and a run no place shows is told by `runNotTold` instead), a history that could not be searched for
    a URL (also one whose logs or run mirror could not be read: a partial history is not a known absence), or a console
    with no fleet reader; `401`
    without a session, with `ended` beside its `error` as for `/api/state` (since #737 PR 2), and `503`
    `TOKENS_UNUSABLE` while the tokens file cannot be used.
  - **What it never holds**: a record's free text (`why`, a failure reason), a Job's `.data`, transcript text, or a
    session key (it names a directory of unredacted transcript; a host-local fork re-derives it,
    `sessionKeyOfRecord`). That is why a viewer may read it (`REQ-CONSOLE-SECURITY` (l)).
  - **Stability**: `version` is `RUN_API_VERSION` (1); keys are only ever added within it.
- **Acceptance**: `REQ-OPERATOR-CONSOLE-SCREENS` (k), `REQ-CONSOLE-SECURITY` (l), and for `/api/run`
  `REQ-TERMINAL-CHAT` (f) (`admin/test/console-run-api.test.mjs`).

## INT-CONSOLE-EVENT-STREAM

**Extension (#771).** The Sandboxes page and its five panels require the operator role before data is read or a stream is registered. Viewer events never contain shell leases, commands, opener links or preparation results. Stream admission, lifetime, limits and person/session binding are UNCHANGED, checked.

An initial Sandboxes subscription without `Last-Event-ID` holds the panels its HTTP response rendered until a fresh
bounded load succeeds. It never replays a previously cached empty view over newer cleanup warnings. Initial reads
coalesce by data key on the queued tick and bypass that page's ordinary five-second data reuse window. A failed read
marks the held panels stale and cannot fall back to an older cached snapshot. Reconnects with a cursor, other pages,
wire fields, event framing, admission and role/session guards remain unchanged.

**The console → its own pages.** `GET /api/events?page=<name>&<that page's query>`: the Server-Sent Events stream
that keeps an open page live (issue #641, `DES-OPERATOR-CONSOLE`, the live hub and the stream lifecycle). The served
script is its only intended client; it is documented so that what a stream may carry, and when it ends, is pinned.

- **Request**: a GET with the session cookie. `page` names a page in `PAGES` whose `live` is true; the rest of the
  query is that page's own (`parsePageQuery`, every value bounded and charset-checked, refused by field name). A
  page the session's role may not open is refused as the page itself would be. `Last-Event-ID` (the header the
  browser sends on a reconnect) is optional. An unknown page, a page whose `live` flag in `PAGES` is false
  (the non-live set is derived from that flag, never maintained as a second page list), or a refused query is answered 400 JSON; a page above the session's role is 403.
  **Since #737 (PR 2)** the query may also carry `as=<name>.<role>` (`PERSON_PARAM`), the person the page was drawn
  for, which the console's page always sends: it is taken off before the page's own query is parsed (no page's query
  takes the name), and when it names another person than the cookie's session the stream is refused `401`
  `{"error": PERSON_CHANGED_STREAM, "ended": "switched"}` ("this browser is now signed in as someone else, so this
  page's live updates were refused") after auth and before any slot is taken (an EventSource cannot read the body;
  the page learns why from its probe, below). A stream with no `as` is not checked, and on a route that is not an
  event stream `as` is not read as a person.
- **Admission**: at most `PI_CONSOLE_MAX_STREAMS` (default 4, 1 to 32) open streams per token across all its
  sessions, and at most 32 in the process, of which 8 are kept for the operator role; a stream over any of these is
  answered `429` with `Retry-After` and opens nothing. `HEAD` is answered `405`. The slot is taken before the response
  starts and released on the response's `close`, however it ends. 32 is half of the server's 64 connections, so
  streams can never hold every connection.
- **Response**: `200` with the security headers of every console response, plus `Content-Type: text/event-stream`,
  `Cache-Control: no-store` and `X-Accel-Buffering: no`. The body is a sequence of events:
  ```
  id: 3f9c2a-17
  event: panel
  data: {"id":"p-queues","html":"<table>...</table>"}

  : ping

  event: stale
  data: {"since":1760432400000,"what":"data"}

  event: fresh
  data: {}

  event: end
  data: {"ended":"revoked"}
  ```
  - `panel`: `data` is one line of JSON, `{id, html}`. `id` is a panel region of the page (`p-<panel>`, the `id` of a
    `<section data-panel>` the page rendered); `html` is that region's complete new content, rendered on the server by
    the same renderer as the page and escaped by the same template. The client replaces the content of the element
    with that `id` only when the element carries `data-panel`, and never runs anything from it (the CSP forbids
    inline script in any case). `html` may be the EMPTY string (since #710: the run page's record panels with no
    record, and its Progress and Chat panels for a run refused before it started): the client writes it like any
    other, which empties the section, and the stylesheet's `section[data-panel]:empty` hides it until a later event
    fills it. **Since #737 (PR 1) an `id` may also name the shell's panel**, `p-nav-parked`: the
    `<span id="p-nav-parked" data-panel>` inside the navigation's Parked pill, drawn on every live page and sent after
    that page's own panels (`panelIds`, `pagePanels`), by the same digest rule. Its `html` is the count of unanswered
    parked runs (a `<span class="count tone-parked">`), or EMPTY when nothing is waiting or the count is not known, and
    the stylesheet hides an empty one (`.pillnav [data-panel]:empty`). No other element outside the page's sections
    is ever a panel, and the client's `data-panel` guard is unchanged. **AMENDED 2026-10-25 (#737 PR 3b): a page's
    headline is the shell's second panel**, `p-headline`: the `<span id="p-headline" data-panel>` inside the title
    bar's `p.titlebar__sub`, drawn only on a page that has a headline (the overview alone) and sent after
    `p-nav-parked` (`SHELL_PANEL_IDS`' order, `panelIds`, `pagePanels`), by the same digest rule. Its `html` is the
    headline's sentence. The overview's page sections may also be EMPTY: its first run's three while the deployment
    runs, and its other eight while the first run's checklist stands in for them, so a stream moves the page from one
    to the other by `panel` events alone. These two spans are the only panels outside a page's sections, and the
    client's `data-panel` guard is unchanged.
  - The event `id` is the hub's sequence for that page, query, role and name (each is drawn for its own reader, so
    a viewer never receives an operator's panels), prefixed by a random per-process epoch: it rises whenever any of its panels changes, and
    every `panel` event written in one tick carries the same value. Ids carry a per-process prefix, so an id from
    before a restart never matches.
  - `: ping`, a comment line, every 15 seconds, so an idle stream is not closed by a tunnel or a proxy. Clients ignore
    it.
  - `end`: the session is over (logout, revoke, rotate, a role change, `sessions end-all`, the idle or the absolute
    limit). The server closes the stream after it; the page goes to `/login` instead of reconnecting.
    Its data is `{}`, because a browser fires no event that carries none. **AMENDED 2026-10-24 (#737 PR 2): the data
    says why.** It is `{"ended": <word>}`, never empty, the word one of `STREAM_ENDS` (`admin/src/console/session-ends.mjs`)
    or null: `idle`, `max`, `revoked`, `role`, `all` (`sessions end-all`) and `elsewhere` (this session signed out,
    which ends its streams at once, or the browser signed in again over its cookie, which ends them once the sign-in's
    answer, with the new cookie, has gone out) are the session's own end, and `shutdown` is the console stopping, which is NOT a sign-out: a client keeps what it shows
    and connects again once the console answers. `restart` is never sent (this process opened every stream it ends),
    and null means ended for no reason the console can give. A client treats a word it does not know as an end with no
    reason. The
    browser page goes to `/login?ended=<word>` only for a member of `ENDED_REASONS`; on `shutdown` and on `elsewhere`
    it waits 2 seconds (the browser may be storing a newer cookie) and asks `/api/whoami`, a 401 then meaning the
    console no longer knows the session, and a 200 reloading the page only when it names the person the page was
    drawn for (the top bar's name and role), else going to `/login?ended=switched` (the page's own word: no stream
    ends with it). The terminal chat treats `shutdown` as a cut connection: it backs off and reconnects with the same
    cookie, and the 401 of a restarted console signs it in again inside its retry loop. Its once-a-minute limit on
    signing in again does not count a 401 that says `restart` or the first 401 after a `shutdown`, so a second
    restart inside a minute does not end the chat; a real end still counts, and so does an `end` whatever its word
    (only a 401 is a restart), and the free sign-in is had at most once per stream that opened since the last one, so
    a console that answers every stream 401 `restart` ends the chat after one counted sign-in.
  - `stale` and `fresh` (since #737 PR 2): a page stream's state, and its FIRST message, before any panel: `fresh`
    (data `{}`) once its page's load and render succeeded, `stale` once they failed and its browser holds panels (a
    load or a render that throws, and a tokens file the console cannot read, send `stale` to every stream they were
    for, whatever it holds), each sent once and again only when it changes. `stale` says the console could not read this page's data (the load or
    the render threw, or the load's primary read failed) or could not read its tokens file this tick, so it keeps the
    panels it last sent rather than draw unreadable ones over them. Its data is `{"since": <ms or null>, "what":
    "tokens" or "data"}`: `since` the hub's clock at that view's last good render, null when the hub holds none (a
    view goes with its last stream, so a lone tab that reconnects is told null), and `what` which failed, the
    console's tokens file or the page's data, so a client never blames the deployment's data for a tokens file. A
    browser holds panels once a good render was sent to its stream, when its stream came with a `Last-Event-ID` (a
    reconnect holds the panels it was drawn with), and once its stream was told `stale`: a read-failed load sends such
    a stream `stale` and no panel, while a first stream that holds none is sent the degraded panels the load makes,
    with no state before them (they say what the page already says). What a stream is sent after a failure is always
    measured against the last good render: a degraded draw is never kept as what another stream of the same view
    holds, so the next good render sends each stream that holds panels every panel that changed, and a reconnect with
    a `Last-Event-ID` during the failure is sent the last good render. A reconnect is a new stream: told `stale` first while its page still fails,
    `fresh` first once it recovered. At subscribe only the page's data and render are judged, never the tokens file
    (the stream's own request has just read it). A client takes its stale state back on `fresh` alone, never when a
    stream opens, and a page already marked keeps the time it was told when a `stale` comes with `since` null. Page
    streams only: a
    transcript stream never gets either.
- **The first events**: a new stream gets its state (`fresh` or `stale`, above), then every panel of its page, as of
  the latest tick, unless its `Last-Event-ID` equals the current sequence for that page, query, role and name, in
  which case it missed nothing and gets no panel until the next change. Any other `Last-Event-ID`, a stale one or
  garbage, gets every panel: the hub keeps no history to replay, so a full set is the only correct answer to "I missed
  something".
- **Only what changed**: after the first events, a panel is sent only when its rendered content differs from what
  the stream was last sent for it (a digest per panel). One poll of the fleet reader a second, in the console
  process, serves every stream, and only while at least one is open. (Since #737 PR 3b the overview's query, `rows`,
  `zoom` and `project`, is the page's own like any other, and its streams share one load whatever its value; which
  load a stream shares is the hub's (`DES-OPERATOR-CONSOLE`), and nothing a stream is sent depends on it.)
- **When it ends**: on `end` (above); within a tick, about a second, of the session failing any check, which is
  re-judged every tick without moving its `lastSeen`, so an open stream never keeps a session alive; at once on
  logout; when the client's unsent buffer passes 2 MiB, without an `end` (the browser reconnects and, its
  `Last-Event-ID` being stale by then, gets every panel again); and when the console stops (`end` with `shutdown`,
  since #737 PR 2). `requestTimeout` and `headersTimeout` do not end it. **Since #737 PR 2 a tokens file the console
  cannot read ends nothing**: for each tick it cannot be read no stream is ended and none is written a `panel` or an
  `entry`, each page stream is sent `stale`, and the `: ping` goes on; the first tick that reads it again judges every
  session, so one that ended meanwhile gets its `end` then. A request to open a stream with a session cookie while
  the file cannot be used is `503` (`INT-CONSOLE-STATE-API`), and one without a session is `401` with `ended`.
- **The transcript stream** (issue #643, `REQ-LIVE-TRANSCRIPT`, `DES-OPERATOR-CONSOLE`): `GET /api/transcript?id=<jobId>`,
  a second kind of event stream, opened by the run page's live transcript section, and since issue #647
  (`REQ-TERMINAL-CHAT`) by the terminal chat with `&format=json`.
  - **Request**: a GET with the session cookie, operator role only: a viewer is answered 403 before any slot is
    taken. `id` is a run id in the run-id charset, else 400. `format` (issue #647) is optional, at most once, `html`
    (the default) or `json`; any other value, or a second one, is 400 with a sentence that names the rule and never
    echoes the value, and so is any other key but `as`, the page's person, taken off and held to the session as for
    the hub's stream (since #737 PR 2; the run page sends it, the terminal chat does not). `Last-Event-ID`, when
    present, must match `TRANSCRIPT_ID_RE` (`^\d{1,16}-\d{1,10}$`, a Valkey stream id, a different shape from the hub's
    `<epoch>-<n>`); the stream then resumes after that entry. A malformed one, the hub's panel shape included, is ignored, and the
    stream is read from its start. `HEAD` is answered `405`.
  - **Admission and lifecycle**: the same slots as the hub's streams (per token, global, the operator reserve), the
    same per-tick session re-judging with `peek` (`event: end` when the session ends), the same 2 MiB cut, the same
    headers and `: ping`.
  - **Events**:
    ```
    id: 1760600000123-0
    event: entry
    data: {"html":"<article>...</article>"}

    event: done
    data: {"outcome":"completed"}
    ```
    `entry`: one stream entry. Its `id:` is the entry's stream id, so a browser's reconnect resumes after the last
    entry it received; `html` is that entry rendered on the server by the one escaping template (a header with the
    kind, the tool, an error marker and the time in UTC, then the text in an escaped `<pre>`, tool-call arguments and
    tool results in `<details>`, no markdown, no inline style). The client appends it to the `[data-transcript]`
    element and runs nothing from it. `done`: the reader has read the stream's `end` entry; `data` carries the
    outcome (`INT-LIVE-TRANSCRIPT-STREAM`), and the server closes the stream after it, so the browser does not
    reconnect. `end`: the session is over, exactly as for the hub. `entry` data is `{html}`: an `<article class="t-entry t-<kind>">`
    holding a `<header>` (kind, tool, an error marker, a `<time datetime>` in UTC, a truncated marker) and the text in
    an escaped `<pre>`, tool-call arguments and tool results inside `<details>`; `done` data is `{outcome}` and nothing
    else. **With `format=json`** (issue #647) an `entry`'s data is instead the structured entry, rebuilt by name from
    the reader's entry (`transcriptEntryJson`) so no other field rides along:
    `{ "id", "kind", "ts", "text", "tool", "error", "truncated", "outcome" }`, `id` the stream id (`TRANSCRIPT_ID_RE`)
    or null, `kind` one of the stream's kinds (an unknown one `note`), `ts` milliseconds or null, `text` the worker's
    redacted text with controls already escaped, as a JSON string, or null, `tool` the `LIVE_TOOL_RE`-checked name,
    `?` for one that fails, or null, `error` and `truncated` booleans, `outcome` the live outcome (else `unknown`) on
    an `end` entry and null otherwise. `done`, `end`, `: ping`, the ids and the resume are the same in both formats.
  - **What it reads**: each tick, `transcriptSince` from the stream's own cursor on the fleet reader's client, at most
    200 entries a read, non-blocking, ONCE per job however many streams follow it and in whichever formats; each entry
    is rendered once per format a stream asked for. It never carries the `.log`, and transcript text appears in no `panel` event.
- **Acceptance**: `REQ-CONSOLE-SECURITY` (k) and (l), `REQ-OPERATOR-CONSOLE-SCREENS` (j), `REQ-LIVE-TRANSCRIPT` (f),
  and for `format=json` `REQ-TERMINAL-CHAT` (f).

- **AMENDED 2026-10-28 (#747), run-page multiplexing.** For `page=run`, `panel` events have no SSE `id:` line,
  on full, changed and degraded renders alike. Reconnect always resends the run panels whole. An operator's stream
  may additionally carry `entry` events (`id: <transcript ms-seq>`, data `{html}`) after a successful page load reports
  transcript existence; a viewer's stream never carries them. `Last-Event-ID` for this page is the validated
  transcript cursor, never a panel sequence. The headline region `p-headline` is a block `div` inside the title
  bar's sub line, allowing the active run's Cancel form without invalid inline markup; it keeps `data-panel` and
  the same swap guard. `tdone` data `{outcome}` marks the transcript ended without closing the
  connection; its outcome word and the entry end line use the record's reason-aware word when available. The
  transcript box stays outside panel swaps, within the page grid. Its key follows the query run id and the existing
  worker run-id mapping across retries/recovery, never a new cursor space invented by the page. A terminal event
  received before the final run record is available can be corrected to the record's word on a later page load. Internal attachment takes no second stream slot;
  all actual connections still count. Other pages retain their sequence ids and reconnect rule; `/api/transcript`
  retains its `done` and closure. Session expiry, fresh/stale signals, backpressure cuts and keep-alives are
  UNCHANGED, checked. Tests: `admin/test/console-live.test.mjs`, `admin/test/console-transcript.test.mjs`,
  `admin/test/console-server.test.mjs`.

## INT-LIVE-TRANSCRIPT-STREAM

**worker → Valkey → the read model (the `/dispatch` panel and the console).** One Valkey stream per running job,
holding a redacted, compact copy of its pi transcript (issue #643, `DES-LIVE-TRANSCRIPT-STREAM`,
`REQ-LIVE-TRANSCRIPT`). The worker is its only writer; the read model is its only reader. The constants are the
worker's, exported from `@edgehero/pi-dispatch/live-transcript` (`liveKeyFor`, `LIVE_KEY_PREFIX`,
`LIVE_MAX_ENTRIES`, `LIVE_TTL_LIVE_MS`, `LIVE_TTL_ENDED_MS`, `LIVE_KINDS`, `LIVE_OUTCOMES`, `LIVE_TEXT_MAX`,
`LIVE_ASSISTANT_TEXT_MAX`, `LIVE_LINE_MAX_BYTES`, `LIVE_TOOL_RE`, `UNPARSEABLE_NOTE`), so the reader and the
