publisher cannot drift.

- **Key**: `run:live:<sanitized job id>`, the queue's job id through `sanitizeJobId`, the sanitizer the run mirror
  uses for `runs:rec:`. Since issue #645 the id is the RUN id (`runIdOf`), so a recovery job `<runId>.r<n>` writes its
  run's stream, its first write replacing the lost attempt's entries as a retry's does. Absent when the job never published, when `PI_LIVE_TRANSCRIPTS=0`, or after it expired; a
  reader cannot tell those apart and a surface says so rather than picking one.
- **Entries**: Valkey's own ids (`<ms>-<seq>`), written by `XADD <key> MAXLEN ~ 2000 * <fields>`. Every entry is a
  flat field list and every value a string:
  ```
  kind       user | assistant | tool-call | tool-result | steer | compaction | note | reset | skipped | end
  ts         ms since epoch, decimal: the pi entry's own timestamp when present, else the publish time
  text       redacted, escaped, cut; absent on reset, skipped and end
  tool       on tool-call and tool-result only: [A-Za-z0-9_.:-]{1,64}, else "?"
  error      "1" on a tool-result pi marked isError; absent otherwise
  truncated  "1" when text was cut; absent otherwise
  outcome    on end only: completed | policy | failed | unknown; never free text
  ```
- **Kinds**: `user`, `assistant`, `tool-call`, `tool-result`, `compaction` and `note` are the transcript. One
  assistant message is one `assistant` entry for its text (omitted when blank) and one `tool-call` per call, whose
  `text` is the arguments, JSON-stringified. A `tool-result`'s `text` is its text parts joined by newlines, each image
  as `[image]`. A `note` is a line the worker composes (the session header as "session started", a model or thinking
  level change, a context edit, a branch summary, a message of a role pi does not define as "a <role> message", a
  turn that ended `error` or `aborted`, or the fixed `UNPARSEABLE_NOTE` for a line that is not JSON), except a custom
  message's note, which carries the extension's own content, redacted, escaped and capped like any `text`. **Never in the stream**: thinking, the header's `cwd`, pi's
  `usage`, `custom`, `session_info` and `label` entries, a provider's error message, and the bytes of a line that did
  not parse.
- **A steering message in the stream** (issue #646, `INT-STEER-INBOX-CONTRACT`). A message the runner handed to pi is
  persisted as a `custom_message` entry of type `pi-dispatch-inbox`, so it appears as one `steer` whose `text` is
  `pi-dispatch-inbox: ` followed by the framed text the worker wrote (the heading, the attribution, the no-authority
  sentences and the fenced message), redacted, escaped and capped at `LIVE_TEXT_MAX` like any `text`. The entry's
  `details` (the id, the mode, the source and the ack MAC) never reach the stream. Only the exact inbox custom type gets the `steer` kind; other custom messages keep the note rule above. The entry appears only once pi persisted the message (its `message_end`),
  so a message still queued, written, withdrawn or late is not in the stream. With `PI_LIVE_TRANSCRIPTS=0` nothing is
  published, although a steer-armed attempt's transcript file is still tailed for its acks (`stream: false`).
- **`reset`**: the source file shrank, was replaced or had its first line rewritten; the entries after it start the
  transcript over (a reader may clear what it shows or mark the break). **`skipped`**: one line over 1 MiB was left
  out unread.
- **The source on a copying venue (AMENDED 2026-10-19, issue #686 part 1).** On `openshell` the lines do not come from
  a file the worker tails but from the runner's signed records on the exec's stderr (`INT-RUNNER-EXIT-CODE-PROTOCOL`,
  "The transcript records"); every line then takes the same path into the same stream, with the runner's baseline
  standing in for the tail's `lstat` at spawn (a resumed session's staged lines are `prior`), so the key, the entries, the
  kinds, the redaction, the caps, the TTLs, the `end` and the retries above are UNCHANGED, checked, and so is every
  reader. Two words gain a second cause there: `reset` is also the runner's reset record (its file rewritten), and
  `skipped` also a gap in the records' `seq` (a line the runner did not send, or a record that did not verify). The
  timing is the records' cadence (the runner reads every 250 ms) plus the publisher's 500 ms flush.
- **Text**: redacted first (`DES-LIVE-TRANSCRIPT-STREAM`, the redactor: `[redacted]` in place of each match), then
  every control and bidi or invisible character written as `\u{XXXX}`, except real newlines (`\r\n` and lone `\r`
  normalised to `\n`) and tabs, which stay real; then cut to `LIVE_TEXT_MAX` (4,096) code points, `LIVE_ASSISTANT_TEXT_MAX`
  (8,192) for `assistant`, never inside an escape, with `truncated: "1"`. **It is agent-written text even so**: a
  surface still scrubs and escapes it for its own medium and interprets none of it.
- **Caps and TTLs**: `MAXLEN ~ 2000` (approximate, so the bound is a floor and the oldest entries go first); a
  `PEXPIRE` of 7 days (`LIVE_TTL_LIVE_MS`) at an attempt's first write, and of 24 hours (`LIVE_TTL_ENDED_MS`) in the
  same transaction as the `end` entry. A stream whose worker died mid-run has no `end` and lives out its 7 days.
- **The end**: the last entry of a finished attempt is `end`, written after the worker's final read of the file
  and before the job directory is removed. Its `outcome` is read from the container's exit (0 `completed`, 1
  `failed`, 2 or a worker abort `policy`, any other code `unknown`, a container that never started `failed`). It can
  differ from the run record's `outcome`, which the processor classifies afterwards with more facts; the record
  (`INT-RUN-HISTORY-FILE-CONTRACT`) is the authority. A stream can lack its `end` when the abort grace ran out
  before the worker's final read (`DES-LIVE-TRANSCRIPT-STREAM`, residuals).
- **Retries**: a retry reuses the job id and so the key. An attempt's first write deletes the key in the same
  `MULTI` as its first entries, so a stream holds one attempt and its `end` is that attempt's.
- **Timing**: the key appears about one poll (500 ms) after the container starts, and entries trail the file by
  at most a poll. Writes are best effort and bounded at 1 s each (3 s for the final read and `end`): entries
  written while Valkey is unreachable are lost and counted, never buffered past 2,000.
- **Reading** (`admin/src/read-model.mjs`): `readTranscriptSince(redis, jobId, after, { count, timeoutMs })` returns
  `{ entries: [{ id, kind, ts, text, tool, error, truncated, outcome }], next, ended, outcome }`, `{ invalid }` or
  `{ unreachable }`; `readTranscriptMeta(redis, jobId)` returns `{ exists, ended, outcome, length, firstId, lastId }`,
  `{ invalid }` or `{ unreachable }`. The job id must match the run-id charset (`[A-Za-z0-9._:-]{1,200}`) and a cursor
  `TRANSCRIPT_ID_RE` (`^\d{1,16}-\d{1,10}$`), both checked before a key is built. A read is non-blocking (`XRANGE`
  after an exclusive cursor, `XREVRANGE COUNT 1`, `XLEN`), at most `TRANSCRIPT_PAGE_MAX` (200) entries, and never a
  blocking `XREAD`. `ended` is true once the cursor is at or past the stream's `end` entry, also on an empty page. A
  reader takes only the fields above, each once and only as a string; an unknown `kind` reads as `note`, an
  unknown `outcome` as `unknown`, a `tool` outside the charset as `?`, and a `text` past 65,536 UTF-16 units is cut
  and marked truncated. The fleet reader's `transcriptSince` and `transcriptMeta` run these on its own client,
  bounded at 2 s.
- **Acceptance**: `REQ-LIVE-TRANSCRIPT` (b) to (e).

- **AMENDED 2026-10-28 (#747), `steer`.** `LIVE_KINDS` includes `steer` for a delivered custom message whose
  `customType` is exactly `pi-dispatch-inbox`; its text remains the redacted delivered message with attribution.
  The ack details never leave the publisher. Consumers that do not recognize `steer` render it as a note, just as
  any unknown kind. No key, field, cap, TTL or outcome vocabulary changes. Tests:
  `worker/test/live-transcript.test.mjs`, `admin/test/console-transcript.test.mjs`.

## INT-RUN-PROGRESS-KEY

**worker → Valkey → the read model (the console, the `/dispatch` panel) and the worker's next attempt.** One Valkey
string per running job holding where the run is, as one JSON snapshot (issue #644, `DES-RUN-PROGRESS`,
`REQ-RUN-PROGRESS`). The worker is its only writer (`makeProgressWriter`, `worker/src/run-progress.mjs`). The
constants are the worker's, exported from `@edgehero/pi-dispatch/run-progress` (`PROGRESS_KEY_PREFIX`,
`progressKeyFor`, `PROGRESS_MAX_BYTES`, `PROGRESS_RUNNING_MAX`, `PROGRESS_RECENT_MAX`, `PROGRESS_PHASES_MAX`,
`PROGRESS_PHASE_MAX`, `PROGRESS_NOTE_MAX`, `PROGRESS_COUNT_MAX`, `PROGRESS_OPEN_MAX`, `PROGRESS_ID_MAX`,
`PROGRESS_HEARTBEAT_MS`, `COMMENT_ID_RE`, `REPORT_PROGRESS_TOOL`), with the TTLs and the outcome enum taken from `@edgehero/pi-dispatch/live-transcript`
(`LIVE_TTL_LIVE_MS`, `LIVE_TTL_ENDED_MS`, `LIVE_OUTCOMES`, `LIVE_TOOL_RE`), so the reader and the writer cannot drift.

- **Key**: `run:progress:<sanitized job id>`, the queue's job id through `sanitizeJobId`, as `run:live:` is. Absent when
  the job never wrote one, when `PI_RUN_PROGRESS=0`, or after it expired; a reader cannot tell those apart. **Since
  issue #645 the id is the RUN id** (`runIdOf`): a recovery job `<runId>.r<n>` writes its run's key, so it reads the
  `commentId` the run's first attempt stored and edits the same status comment, as a retry does.
- **Value**: one string, the snapshot serialized as JSON, written whole by `SET <key> <json> PX <ttl>`. Every write
  carries the whole state, so a lost write is repaired by the next one. The shape (`v: 1`):
  ```
  { "v": 1,
    "turn": <int>,                    // assistant messages this attempt (after the resume baseline), not "error" ones
    "steps": <int>,                   // tool results that closed a call
    "failed": <int>,                  // of those, results pi marked isError
    "interrupted": <int>,             // calls still open at the end; set in the final snapshot only
    "running": [ { "tool": "<name>", "since": <ms> } ],              // open calls, newest last, at most 8; [] once ended
    "recent":  [ { "tool": "<name>", "status": "ok" | "error" | "interrupted",
                   "durationMs": <int> | null, "at": <ms> } ],       // the last 20 closed steps, newest last
    "phase":   { "index": <int>, "done": <int> | null, "total": <int> | null } | null,   // 0-based index into phases
    "phases":  [ "<phase name>" ],                                   // first-seen order, at most 32: MODEL TEXT
    "note":    "<the latest report's note>" | null,                  // MODEL TEXT
    "prior":   { "turns": <int>, "steps": <int> } | null,            // counted from lines before the resume baseline
    "startedAt": <ms>, "updatedAt": <ms>,                           // updatedAt: the time of the write that carried it
    "ended": <bool>,
    "outcome": "completed" | "policy" | "failed" | "unknown" | null, // on the final write only
    "commentId": "<forge status comment id>" | null,                 // COMMENT_ID_RE, INT-FORGE-STATUS-COMMENT-EDIT
    "replayed"?: <int> }              // issue #645: calls a recovered run's runner re-ran; present only when above zero
  ```
  Every integer is a safe non-negative integer; `done` and `total` are at most 1,000,000 with `done <= total` and
  `total >= 1`. `since` is the assistant entry's time and `at` the result's (the pi entry's own timestamp when it lies
  between 0 and a day ahead, else the read time, `DES-LIVE-TRANSCRIPT-STREAM`'s rule); `durationMs` is the result's own
  `durationMs`, null when pi wrote none (a call refused before it ran), never a timestamp difference. An assistant
  message whose `stopReason` is `"error"` or `"aborted"` opens no step (pi runs none of its calls); an `"error"` one is
  no turn and an `"aborted"` one is, as the runner counts turns. A call or result whose id is longer than
  `PROGRESS_ID_MAX` (128 UTF-16 units) is ignored, so a forged id cannot pin memory while its step is open.
- **Tool names** (`running[].tool`, `recent[].tool`) are model-chosen and checked: the live stream's charset
  (`LIVE_TOOL_RE`, `[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]{1,64}`), else `?`, and `?` too when the job's redactor would change the name.
- **Model text**: `phases[]` and `note` come from the agent's `report_progress` calls, only on a job armed with
  `run.progress` and only once the call's result arrived with `isError: false` (the runner validated it). Each is
  redacted with the job's redactor (`DES-LIVE-TRANSCRIPT-STREAM`'s), then has its control and bidi characters written
  as `\u{XXXX}` (`escapeControls`), then is cut to 64 code points (a phase) or 200 (a note). **It is agent-written
  text even so**: a reader shows it to the operator role alone, escaped for its own medium, and interprets none of it.
  Neither ever reaches the run record (`INT-RUN-HISTORY-FILE-CONTRACT`'s `progress` holds counts) or the forge
  comment (`INT-FORGE-STATUS-COMMENT-EDIT` holds integers).
- **Size**: the serialized value is at most `PROGRESS_MAX_BYTES` (16 KiB of UTF-8). Past it the writer drops `recent`
  oldest first, then `phases` from the tail, then the note, until it fits. **`phase.index` is not adjusted by that
  cut**, so it can point past `phases`: a reader bounds it.
- **When it is written**: the first write when the container starts, once the writer has read the key an earlier
  attempt left (below), carrying the empty snapshot (turn 0), so a retry's key replaces the previous attempt's final
  snapshot at once; then on every change, at most once a second, with a trailing write for the latest state; while the
  attempt has not ended, again every 30 s (`PROGRESS_HEARTBEAT_MS`) when nothing changed, a heartbeat whose only new
  value is `updatedAt`; and a final write when the container ends, after the live transcript's own final read, with
  `ended: true`, `running: []`, every call still open counted in `interrupted` and listed in `recent` as
  `interrupted`, and `outcome` the exit's own reading (`liveOutcomeOf`, the stream's `end` rule: it can differ from the
  run record's classification, and the record is the authority). Before the final write the sink waits at most 2 s for
  a status comment post still in flight, so its id rides the final write and a retry edits that comment. Nothing is
  written after the final write.
- **Staleness**: a key that has not ended and whose `updatedAt` is older than 180 s (`PROGRESS_STALE_MS`,
  `progressStaleFor` in `admin/src/read-model.mjs`, six missed heartbeats) belongs to a worker that stopped writing (a
  crash, a kill, a lost Valkey), not to a quiet run. Readers say so and stop the running ages they would otherwise keep
  counting; an ended key is never stale.
- **TTLs**: 7 days (`LIVE_TTL_LIVE_MS`) from this attempt's first successful write, each later write setting what is
  left of it so no write extends it; 24 hours (`LIVE_TTL_ENDED_MS`) from the final write. A key whose worker died
  mid-run has no final write and lives out its 7 days, read as stale (above) after 180 s. Seven days after the writer
  started, every write but the final one stops for good, the heartbeat with it (`run_progress_expired`), so no write
  sets a TTL under 1 s. When the processor gives up on a container whose stop did not take, it makes the final write
  itself, with outcome `unknown` (`onLive`, `DES-RUN-PROGRESS`).
- **Retries**: a retry reuses the job id and so the key. An attempt's first write first READS the key (a bounded
  `GET`) and keeps its `commentId` when it matches `COMMENT_ID_RE`, so the attempt edits the comment the first one
  posted; the key is then replaced whole by this attempt's state (the earlier attempt's counts are not carried). An
  unreadable or unreachable key is read as none.
- **Failure**: every call is bounded (1 s for a write and the read, 2 s for the final write, 5 s for the sink's whole
  finish, the wait for a comment post and the final write together) and best effort: a client that is not ready, refuses or hangs costs that
  write, counted, and is logged once per job (`run_progress_write_failed`, the job id only); nothing here throws into,
  fails or slows the job.
- **Reading** (`admin/src/read-model.mjs`): `parseProgress(raw)` validates strictly (`v` 1, every named key with its
  type and cap, a tool name outside `LIVE_TOOL_RE` read as `?`, `phase.index` bounded): a field it does not name makes
  the WHOLE key `{ invalid }`, so adding a field to the snapshot means raising `v`. **`replayed` (issue #645) is the
  one exception, and a stated one**: it was added at `v: 1` as an OPTIONAL key, written only when a recovered run
  replayed a call, so every other key is unchanged; a reader from before #645 refuses such a key whole (that run shows
  no progress on an older console or panel), and the current reader accepts it as an optional count. `commentId` is validated and then
  dropped, so no reader hands a forge id on. `readProgress(redis, jobId, { timeoutMs })` returns that snapshot, `{
  absent }`, `{ invalid }` (also for a run id outside the run-id charset, refused before any read) or `{ unreachable
  }`; `readProgressMany(redis, jobIds)` reads at most `PROGRESS_BATCH_MAX` (50) distinct ids in ONE `MGET`, ids
  outside the charset left out. The fleet reader exposes both on its held client, bounded like its other reads
  (`progress(jobId)`, `progressFor(jobIds)`), and its snapshot's `active` rows carry `activeProgressOf`'s projection:
  integers (`updatedAt` among them, for the stale rule) and the running call's checked tool name only, never a phase
  name or the note, so `/api/state` and the
  lists stay free of model text (`INT-CONSOLE-STATE-API`). The full snapshot, phase names included, is read for an
  operator's surface alone (the run page, the panel's ACTIVE row).
- **Acceptance**: `REQ-RUN-PROGRESS` (a) to (c) and (g).

## INT-FORGE-STATUS-COMMENT-EDIT

**worker → forge.** The one forge comment the worker posts and then EDITS (issue #644, `REQ-RUN-PROGRESS`,
`REQ-JOB-STATUS-COMMENTS`): a job whose trigger set `run.statusComment: true` gets one status comment on its issue or
pull request when its container starts, edited as the run goes and a last time with the run record's outcome
(`worker/src/status-comment.mjs`, the host methods below, wired in `worker/src/start.mjs`).

- **Post**: each forge host's `postStatusComment(ref, target, text, token)` now RETURNS `{ id }`, read after the 2xx
  (callers that ignored its result are unchanged): GitHub and Forgejo the issue comment's id, GitLab the note's id, each
  as a decimal string; Azure DevOps `<threadId>:<commentId>` for a pull request (the create answers the thread with its
  first comment) and `wi:<commentId>` for a work item comment. A 2xx whose body has no usable id answers `{ id: null }`
  and never throws, since the comment exists and a retry would post a second one.
- **Edit**: a new `editStatusComment(ref, target, id, text, token)` on each host:
  ```
  github   PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/comments/{id}                       { body }    (issues and pull requests alike)
  gitlab   PUT   /projects/{id}/issues/{iid}/notes/{note}                         { body }    (target.type issue)
           PUT   /projects/{id}/merge_requests/{iid}/notes/{note}                 { body }    (target.type pull_request)
  forgejo  PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/comments/{id}                       { body }
  azure    PATCH /{project}/_apis/git/repositories/{repo}/pullRequests/{pr}/threads/{t}/comments/{c}?api-version=7.1   { content }
           PATCH /{project}/_apis/wit/workItems/{w}/comments/{c}?api-version=7.1-preview.4                           { text }
  ```
  The id is checked before it reaches a URL: `STATUS_COMMENT_ID_RE` (`^[A-Za-z0-9:_-]{1,200}$`) and numeric on GitHub,
  GitLab and Forgejo; on Azure its form must agree with `target.type` (a `<t>:<c>` id for a pull request, `wi:<c>` for
  a work item), since the number comes from the target and the wrong pairing would address another object. A
  malformed id is a config error with no request. An HTTP failure throws with `status` set (octokit's own error on
  GitHub, `InfraRetry` with `status` elsewhere).
- **Identity**: both calls go through the `comment` adapter's path in `start.mjs` (`forgeFor`, the auth re-resolve,
  a token minted per call), so the status comment is posted and edited by the same forge identity as every other
  comment the worker posts, and needs no permission the terminal comments did not already use beyond editing that
  identity's own comment.
- **The wrappers never throw**: `statusPost` answers `{ id }` or null; `statusEdit` answers `{ ok: true }`,
  `{ stop: "http-403" | "http-404" | "http-429" }` (the comment is gone, the token may not edit it, or the forge is rate
  limiting: editing on would repeat the refusal), or `{ ok: false }` for any other failure, which the next edit tries
  again. A host without `editStatusComment`, a job with no forge host or no target, gets no commenter at all, so no
  comment is posted that could never be updated.
- **The text** (`renderStatusText`): fixed words, the sanitized job id (cut to 128 characters) in backticks, and
  integers. Running: ``pi-dispatch job `<id>`: running. Turn 7, 12 steps (1 failed). Phase 2 of 4 (3/10).``; finished:
  ``... `<id>`: finished: completed. ...`` with the outcome from `LIVE_OUTCOMES` (anything else written `unknown`); an
  attempt that ended and will be retried: ``... `<id>`: attempt ended, retrying. ...`` (`STATUS_RETRYING`).
  `(N failed)` and `N interrupted` appear only when above 0; the phase part only when a phase was reported, its `of
  <n>` from the LENGTH of `phases` (only when it exceeds the index) and its `(<done>/<total>)` or `(<done> done)` from
  the integers. **No phase name, note or tool name is ever written**: a public comment must not carry model text that
  could mention a user or hold a link, and a counter that is not a safe non-negative integer is written as 0.
- **Cadence** (`makeStatusCommenter`): one post when the container starts (after the progress key's read, below); an
  edit only when the rendered text changed and no sooner than 30 s after the last forge call, the trailing edit
  carrying the latest snapshot; at most 120 edits a job, the last kept for the final edit, so the outcome is written
  whenever the run got that far; on `{ stop }` no further progress edit, the last text left in place. Forge calls run
  one at a time. The final edit cancels a pending one and is bounded at 4 s: a stuck forge costs a stale comment, never
  a slower job. It is made even after an earlier `http-429` stop (a rate limit asks for a pause, and a comment left
  saying "running" after the run is wrong for good), and tried once more after 1 s, inside the same 4 s, when the forge
  answers a 429 or any other failure (`{ ok: false }`); an `http-403` or `http-404` stop still ends it. A run that ends
  before its commenter started posts one comment carrying the outcome; one whose post found no id posts nothing more,
  since the first may have landed.
- **The final outcome** (`makeStatusCommentRegistry`, start.mjs): the exit code is a weaker reading than the run
  record's classification (an OOM kill exits 137 and is recorded `policy`; an infrastructure exit is retried under the
  same job id), so the final edit is made from the record. Each commenter is registered by job id; the progress sink
  hands it the final snapshot when the container ends, and `recordRun` settles it with the record's `outcome`, or with
  `STATUS_RETRYING` when the error is an `InfraRetry` and the record's `attempt` is below the job's `attempts`. An
  attempt that leaves no record (a hold, a record path that threw) is finished `STATUS_FALLBACK_MS` (5 minutes) after
  the container ended with the exit's outcome. **A late settle**: a commenter the fallback finished is kept for
  `STATUS_LATE_SETTLE_MS` (10 minutes; at most `STATUS_LATE_SETTLE_MAX`, 256, the oldest dropped first), and a record
  that settles in that time makes one corrective final edit (`correct`, allowed one edit past the 120) when its text
  differs from the fallback's. A later attempt's commenter replaces the entry, and any kept one, without a final
  edit. **An attempt with no commenter** (refused before its container, so nothing registered): when the job set
  `statusComment`, `recordRun` reads the progress key (one bounded `GET`, never throwing) and, when it holds a valid
  `commentId` (an earlier attempt's post), makes one edit bounded at 4 s with the record's outcome and the key's
  snapshot; a phrase collision skips it before the read, and a key with no id edits nothing. An operator's cancel of a
  delayed retry writes no record, so it reaches none of this, and the comment keeps its retrying text.
- **Retries and recovery**: the posted id is stored in the progress key's `commentId` (`INT-RUN-PROGRESS-KEY`); a later
  attempt of the same job reads it at its first write and edits that comment instead of posting a second one. A post
  still in flight when the container ends is waited for (at most 2 s) before the key's final write, so its id is not
  lost. An invalid stored id is not trusted, and the attempt posts a fresh comment.
- **Loops**: every edit is a comment event on the forge. The receiver drops it twice: the bot-loop guard (the editor
  is the harness's own identity), and on GitHub, GitLab and Forgejo the comment route, which routes only a CREATED
  comment (GitHub's and Forgejo's `edited` action and a GitLab note update route as nothing), so a maintainer who edits
  the status comment to hold the trigger phrase starts nothing either. On Azure DevOps the receiver reads one pull request
  comment event type and splits it by no action, so there the bot's own event is dropped by the self guard
  alone, as are its work item update and comment events, and a member's work item update that changes no tag routes
  as nothing. Pinned through the whole receiver on all four forges by
  `receiver/test/status-comment-edits.test.mjs`, each with a positive control. **Belt and braces at the source**:
  before it builds a commenter, the worker renders every word form the text can take (each count singular and plural,
  each failure part, each phase form, running, every outcome and the retry) for this job id and refuses the comment when the
  phrase the job was started with (`trigger.matched.phrase`, set on the comment route only) could occur in it, digit
  runs compared as one (`statusTextMayMatch`); the job then runs without a comment and logs `status_comment_skipped`
  with reason `phrase-collision`.
- **Logs** carry the job id and a reason or an HTTP status, never the text: `status_comment_failed` (`op` post or
  edit, `status`), `status_comment_stopped` (`reason`), `status_comment_capped` (`edits`),
  `status_comment_final_timeout`, `status_comment_error` (an error's name) and `status_comment_skipped` (`reason`:
  `progress-off` for a trigger that asked for a comment on a deployment with `PI_RUN_PROGRESS=0`, `no-transcript` when
  the job had no transcript file or job id to read progress from, `no-forge-target` for a job with no forge host that can post and edit or
  no target, `phrase-collision` above).
- **Acceptance**: `REQ-RUN-PROGRESS` (e).

## INT-DOCTOR-RESULTS-KEY

- **Model proposal exception (#773)**: a check explicitly identified as a model proposal may retain a redacted bounded label at level `ok` as well as warn/fail. Its optional typed proposal data is rebuilt from an allowlist of kind, scope/role and validated current/candidate model references. The builder and reader both validate this data; an arbitrary label prefix or unknown extra field grants no publication authority. Generic `ok` checks still carry no label. Existing version-1 records remain readable; absence of typed proposal evidence is not a claim that the host has no proposals. Count, detailed-text and redaction bounds remain authoritative.

**`pi-dispatch doctor` → Valkey → the read model (the console's Fleet page and its configuration sentences, the
`/dispatch` panel's HOSTS view).** One Valkey string per host holding that host's last doctor run, as one JSON record
(issue #712, `DES-DOCTOR-RESULTS-PUBLISHED`). Doctor is its only writer (`publishResults` in `worker/src/doctor.mjs`,
through `publishDoctorRecord`); the worker runs doctor for it (`doctor-spawner.mjs`). The constants and the reader are
the worker's, exported from `@edgehero/pi-dispatch/doctor-results`, so the reader and the writer cannot drift.

```
  doctor:hosts      SET of host names that published: an index the READER prunes, never a source of truth
  doctor:h:<name>   STRING, one JSON record, written whole by SET <key> <json> PX 604800000 (7 days)
```

- **The name**: the host's worker name (`PI_WORKER_NAME`, else the sanitized hostname, as the registry names the row),
  held to `WORKER_NAME_RE`, so it is a key segment unescaped; any other name is refused before a write.
- **Value** (`v: 1`):
  ```
  { "v": 1,
    "at": <epoch ms>,                       // when the run published
    "version": "<worker package version>",  // [0-9A-Za-z.+-]{1,32}, else ""
    "openshell": <bool>,                    // whether the openshell venue was judged on this run
    "every": <int> | null,                  // the worker's own interval when its spawn ran this (--by-worker=<h>), else
                                            // PI_DOCTOR_INTERVAL_HOURS as this run resolves it; null when it does not parse
    "by": { "uid": <int> | null, "worker": <bool> },   // the effective uid, and whether the worker's spawn ran it
    "workerRun"?: { "uid": <int> | null, "at": <ms> },  // a run by hand under ANOTHER uid over the worker's: that run's uid and time
    "counts": { "ok": <int>, "warn": <int>, "fail": <int> },   // over EVERY check, listed or not
    "checks": [ { "id": "<id>", "level": "ok" | "warn" | "fail",
                  "label"?: "<redacted>", "fix"?: "<redacted>",
                  "proposal"?: { "kind": "<closed kind>", "scope"?: "<scope>", "role"?: "<role>",
                                 "model"?: "<provider/model>", "candidate"?: "<provider/model>",
                                 "provider"?: "<provider>" } } ], // label/fix on warn/fail and typed proposals
    "more": <int> }                         // checks past DOCTOR_CHECKS_MAX, counted and not listed
  ```
- **Ids** (`CHECK_ID_RE`, `<section>.<name>`): a NAMED id where the check carries one (`NAMED_CHECK_IDS`:
  `triggers.file`, `triggers.file-missing`, `settings.overlay`, `settings.overlay-dollars`, and for each boot file
  `<scaffold name>.file`, the service's verdict on the file it reads, and `<scaffold name>.file-shell`, this shell's);
  else `<section>.<n>`, the check's place in its section on that run (`DOCTOR_SECTIONS`, `--live` read-backs in
  `live`). A repeat gets `-2`, `-3`. A reader matches on named ids only: a derived id is stable for one host's
  configuration, not across hosts. Both lists are pinned against `doctor.mjs` by a test. AMENDED 2026-10-25 (#737,
  PR 3a): two more named ids. `egress.proxy` says whether the egress proxy runs, on each venue that has one: docker's
  proxy line carries it, and so does the line doctor prints in its place for a running proxy that is not this
  deployment's (or is out of date), which takes the id from the proxy's check (`proxyCheck.id`); rootless Podman's
  proxy line carries it too, so a host on both venues publishes `egress.proxy` and `egress.proxy-2`, and a reader
  of the proxy takes both and judges the worse. `provider.key` says whether the provider's key is found where the
  worker looks (the provider key line, not drawn for a malformed `PI_PROVIDER`, whose shape row is the one line).
  Every named id is written at ONE site of `doctor.mjs`, except those in `REPEATED_CHECK_IDS`
  (`{ "egress.proxy": 2 }`: the proxy is a different container on each venue, each judged by its own line, and the
  question a reader asks of either is the same), and the test counts the literal sites against it. No id names a
  forge's credentials, because no one check holds them: the `github` section alone prints about twenty lines across
  its three auth sources, and the other forges print theirs under `forges`; a reader judges those by the section part
  of their derived ids, which `DOCTOR_SECTIONS` pins. AMENDED 2026-10-25 (#737, PR 3b): the console's first run is
  that reader (`firstRunState`, `admin/src/doctor-view.mjs`): over every host's readable record it takes the worst
  level of `egress.proxy` and its repeats, the worst of `provider.key` and its repeats, and, for a deployment with a
  forge trigger, the worst of every check whose id's section is `github` or `forges`; a record with a `provider`
  derived id (`provider.<n>`) and no `provider.key` is a doctor older than the named id, and is said so. It reads no
  derived id's number.
- **Content rule** (`redactText`, applied by the writer), in this order: invisible characters (zero-width, joiners,
  marks, the soft hyphen, the byte-order mark) are deleted, and control, bidi, line and paragraph separator characters
  are spaces; every value of a secret-named variable in doctor's resolution (and the `.env` values
  it did not take) and every known token shape (`redact-secrets.mjs`'s, plus a JWT, a Google API key, `hf_` and `npm_`
  tokens) is `[redacted]`, as is a credential-named query or fragment parameter's value, a `password=`, `password:`,
  `--password` or `--token` value, a `Basic` credential, a `*-api-key:` header value and the userinfo of a scheme-less
  `user:password@host` (a numeric or switch value of a secret-sounding knob is not taken as a secret); the input JSON.parse QUOTES in its message (`Unexpected token 'x', "..." is not valid JSON`) is
  `<content>` (its position forms quote nothing and stay); a URL keeps `scheme://host[:port]` only; an absolute POSIX,
  home (`~/`), drive or UNC path is `<path>`, wherever the character before it is not part of a word, a ratio or a URL
  (so after `:`, `|`, `*` or a dash too), to its closing quote when it opens after one, and over a space into a next
  word that holds a separator; whitespace is folded; each is cut to `DOCTOR_LABEL_MAX` (300) characters LAST, so a cut
  never leaves the prefix of something a rule would take. **What is guaranteed is these rules, not "no value"**: a
  secret under a name that does not look like one, with no known shape, written outside a URL, is not recognised, and
  the last word of an unquoted path with a space and no separator after it (`/a/My Projects`) is kept. An ok check carries no label unless it carries validated model proposal metadata (#773). At most `DOCTOR_CHECKS_MAX` (400)
  entries, of which at most `DOCTOR_DETAILED_MAX` (80) carry words.
- **When it is written**: at the end of every `pi-dispatch doctor` run unless `--no-publish` (after `--fix`'s re-check
  and `--live`'s read-backs, before the closing line), every `pi-dispatch up`, and every run the worker starts (a minute
  after boot, then every `PI_DOCTOR_INTERVAL_HOURS`). Only to the Valkey doctor talked to on that run, at the address
  the worker pins (`judgeValkeyListeners`); a run that talked to none writes nothing.
- **TTL**: 7 days (`DOCTOR_RESULTS_TTL_MS`), set afresh by every publish: a record's expiry IS "no result in a week".
  The index has none; a reader that may write removes a member whose record is gone.
- **Who ran it**: `by.worker` is set by the worker's own spawn (`doctor --publish --by-worker=<hours>`, 1 to 168 or exit 2, an internal
  flag); every other run is "by hand". A run by hand under a uid other than the one that last ran as the worker
  publishes as any run does, and carries `workerRun` (that run's uid and time, read with one `GET` before the write and
  kept while hand runs follow), so a reader says whose view of the host it shows. A declared `PI_WORKER_NAME` the
  worker refuses at boot (`workerName`, config.mjs) is never a key: the run says so on stderr and writes nothing.
- **Failure**: every command is bounded (2 s) and the write is best effort: a fault is one stderr line starting
  `doctor: results not published (`, naming no URL, path or value, and the exit code and stdout are unchanged.
- **Pruning by the writer**: after its write, a publish looks at up to 256 other index members in one `MGET` and
  removes those whose record has expired, so an index read only by the console (which never prunes) cannot grow.
- **Reading** (`readDoctorResults(redis, { names, prune, now, timeoutMs })`): the live hosts a caller names FIRST, then
  the index's other members, worker names only, each list sorted, at most `DOCTOR_HOSTS_MAX` (64), in ONE `MGET`, so
  expired index members can never push a live host out of the read; each value through
  `parseDoctorRecord`, an allowlist (another `v`, or JSON that does not parse, is `{ name, unreadable: true }`); each row
  gains `ageMs` from the reader's clock (0 when the record is ahead). `{ unreachable }` is not `{ hosts: [] }`. The fleet
  reader reads it at most every 15 s and the console's reader never prunes. Not on `/api/state`
  (`INT-CONSOLE-STATE-API` UNCHANGED, checked: its body is built field by field and names no doctor field).
- **Deleting it changes nothing**: no decision reads `doctor:*`; a reader that finds nothing says no result was
  published, never that a host is healthy.
- **Acceptance**: worker/test/doctor-results.test.mjs (ids, sections and named ids pinned, redaction, the record, the
  write's one `SET ... PX` and the refreshed TTL, the read's allowlist, prune and bounds), worker/test/doctor.test.mjs
  ("doctor publishes one record per run", "publishing is best effort"), worker/test/doctor-spawner.test.mjs,
  admin/test/doctor-view.test.mjs, admin/test/console-pages.test.mjs (the Fleet fixtures).

## INT-DEFER-REASON-KEY

- **Canary exclusion (#717)**: ordinary worker pickup checks `dispatch:canary:exclusive` before paid gates and defers with reason `canary`. The experiment takes its compare-owned renewable lease before proving shared/host queue active lists empty. Lost ownership aborts the experiment. All consuming workers must run this implementation before experiments begin, and legacy consumers must not be started during an experiment: older code does not honor the lease. This closes the standalone command concurrency bypass; queue pause still refuses canaries.

**The worker → Valkey → the admin console's waiting reader.** Why the worker put a job that has not started back on
the delayed set, in the worker's own words, written at the moment it defers (issue #737, PR 3a,
`DES-WAITING-REASONS`). The key, the closed vocabulary and every field's rule are ONE leaf,
`worker/src/defer-reasons.mjs`, exported as `@edgehero/pi-dispatch/defer-reasons` (`./defer-reasons` in the worker's
exports map). It imports nothing, so the console imports it without the worker's dependencies, and the writer and the
reader cannot drift on the key, a field, a reason or a bucket. The writer is `worker/src/defer-write.mjs`
(`makeDeferTo`, worker only, never loaded by the admin); the readers are the admin's `readWaiting` and
`readWaitingRow` (`admin/src/read-model.mjs`); besides the writer itself, the one deleter is `removeQueuedJob`
(`INT-CANCEL-CHANNEL-CONTRACT`).

```
  defer:job:<jobId>   HASH, one per job id, with its own TTL; the fields in DEFER_FIELDS order, the readers' HMGET
    why         the reason, a key of DEFER_WHYS (below)
    at          epoch ms on the deferring worker's clock: when it wrote the record (a retry's: the reading its delay is from)
    until       epoch ms: the instant it moved the job to, the very value it hands `moveToDelayed`
    project     the job's project id, as this pickup resolved it, when it has one
    host        the deferring worker's name, as the registry names its row
    holder      a job id the wait is on: the chained parent, the run a recovery continues, or the holder of the target
    endpoint    the model endpoint's id (`endpoint`)
    budgetWhy   the host budget's verdict word: `memory`, `cpu`, `count`, `share`, `running-here` or `unseeded`;
                legacy `budget` remains readable during rolling upgrades (`host-budget`)
    trigger     the job's matched trigger index, `job.data.trigger.matched.index`, 0-based
    attempt     the attempt a retry will be (`retry`)
    attempts    the job's total attempts, `opts.attempts` (`retry`), so a reader need not read `opts`
    n           the writer's nonce, 16 hex characters; never returned by a reader
```

- **Who writes it.** Every gate of `makeProcessor` that puts a job back on the delayed set goes through ONE function,
  `deferTo(job, token, untilMs, why, extra)`: it writes the record, then calls `job.moveToDelayed(untilMs, token)`,
  then throws BullMQ's `DelayedError`, the move and the throw the gates always made (the class is handed in by the
  processor, which imports bullmq, so the processor's own `instanceof` still tells a deferral apart). No module in
  `worker/src` moves a job to the delayed set except `defer-write.mjs`, which a source-shape test holds. Before each of
  the four `InfraRetry` throws (the netns keeper loop's three and the processor's own retryable failure),
  `noteRetry(job, { project })` writes the `retry` record, because BullMQ delays that job itself after the throw, where
  no gate can say why: only when `retryDelayOf(job)` knows the delay, which mirrors the pinned BullMQ 5.80.4's retry
  decision and builtin backoffs (`attemptsMade + 1 < opts.attempts` and not discarded; a number or `fixed` waits
  `delay`, `exponential` waits `round(2^attemptsMade * delay)`), and is null, so nothing is written, for a jittered or
  custom backoff and a delay at or below zero. Its `until` is the worker's `now()` plus that delay, `attempt` is
  `attemptsMade + 2` and `attempts` is `opts.attempts`.
- **The reasons** (`DEFER_WHYS`, closed: each its bucket and the sentence a console shows, whose `{placeholders}` the
  console fills from the record's own fields, escaped, times drawn as `<time>`):

  | Reason | Bucket | The gate |
  |---|---|---|
  | `pause-window` | pause | a scoped pause window |
  | `size-never-fits` | slot | a job size that never fits this host, on a fleet's shared queue, which another host may take |
  | `canary` | run | the operator model experiment holds the exclusive admission lease |
  | `host-slot` | slot | this host's job slots across its queues, on a host without a host budget |
  | `scope-folder`, `scope-repo` | slot | a folder's or a repository's concurrent limit, in process or the fleet lease |
  | `chained` | run | the same slot, for a job with a `parentJobId`; `holder` is that parent |
  | `scope-project` | slot | a project row's concurrent limit |
  | `endpoint` | slot | every slot of a model endpoint; `endpoint` is its id |
  | `model-cooldown` | check | no candidate is available and the first transient blocker is a cooldown; asks again at `until` |
  | `model-window` | check | no candidate is available and the first transient blocker is a full model window; asks again at `until` |
  | `subscription-quota` | check | a connection/application bucket is exhausted; waits for newer evidence, an observed reset or one person's trial, with `until` only a recheck time when reset is unknown |
  | `subscription-owner` | ready | this host does not own the selected connection; waits for its owning host |
  | `subscription-auth` | check | the credential cannot be renewed yet; waits until its measured earliest refresh instant without consuming an attempt |
  | `host-budget` | slot | the host budget; `budgetWhy` is its verdict |
  | `bundle-profile` | slot | a host that serves the job's secret bundle profile |
  | `recovery-wait` | run | a recovery whose run's attempt still runs; `holder` is that run |
  | `wait-after` | check | an `after` hold |
  | `wait-hold` | check | a wait check that said not yet, or could not tell |
  | `wait-throttled` | check | the check lease denied, on this host's or the fleet's |
  | `wait-supersede` | check | the supersede probe could not answer; `holder` is the delivery holding the target |
  | `wait-aborted` | check | a wait check a restart or a cancel stopped |
  | `wait-unclear` | check | a wait check that answered what the gate cannot read |
  | `podman-restart` | ready | rootful Podman's service, restarting |
  | `netns-keeper` | ready | the rootless network keeper, too young |
  | `retry` | retry | an infrastructure retry's backoff (`noteRetry`) |

  The buckets are `DEFER_BUCKETS`, in the order a console shows them: `slot`, `run`, `check`, `retry`, `pause`,
  `ready`, `paused`, `due`, `unknown` and `none`, each with a title and a short form (`DEFER_BUCKET_WORDS`). No reason
  is `paused`, `due`, `unknown` or `none`: a reader gives these four itself. `due` comes first: a delayed job more
  than `WAITING_DUE_GRACE_MS` (10 s, the admin's `read-model.mjs`) past its due instant, the delayed set's score read
  against the read's own clock, is `due` whatever its record says, and its line is the leaf's `DEFER_DUE_SENTENCE`,
  "Due since {due}; no worker has taken it", which no worker records, since the job is overdue exactly because no
  worker has looked at it since. Then `paused`, a job in the paused list or in a paused queue's wait list or
  prioritized set (the queue's meta hash has a `paused` field at all, whatever it holds, as BullMQ 5.80.4 reads it).
  Then `unknown` ("A reason this console does not know", short "Unknown reason"), a delayed job whose record names a
  reason within the reason charset (`DEFER_WHY_RE`) that the table does not hold, most often a newer worker's, whose
  line names that reason's word with "no explanation yet"; and `none` ("No reason was recorded"), a delayed job with
  no record it can use (none at all, an earlier episode's, or one whose reason fails the charset) that is not held on
  `run.waitFor` (a held one with none is `check`). Each title is true of every job in its bucket, which is why a
  reason a console cannot explain has a bucket of its own rather than `none`'s "No reason was recorded". A
  source-shape test holds every reason to a site that writes it, and every site to a reason of the table.
- **Field rules**, judged on the way in by `deferHsetArgs` (a field that fails its rule is left out and the record is
  still written; a reason outside the table throws `RangeError`, a defect at the call site, and nothing is written)
  and on the way out by `parseDefer`: `at` and `until` decimal integers with no leading zero from 0 to
  253402300799999 (`DEFER_TIME_MAX_MS`, 9999-12-31T23:59:59.999Z, the last instant a UTC date-time can be written
  with a four-digit year, so a console that draws an instant's first sixteen characters as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM` can
  always draw one; it is not the latest instant a JavaScript Date holds, 8.64e15 in the year 275760, whose ISO form
  writes the year as six digits with a sign, which those sixteen characters would draw as another date); `project`
  `DEFER_PROJECT_RE` (a copy of `project-id.mjs`'s `PROJECT_ID_RE`); `host` `DEFER_HOST_RE` (a copy of
  `worker-name.mjs`'s `WORKER_NAME_RE`); `holder` `DEFER_ID_RE`, `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]{1,200}` (the admin reader's
  `RUN_ID_RE`); `endpoint` `DEFER_ENDPOINT_RE` (a copy of `model-endpoints.mjs`'s `MODEL_ENDPOINT_ID_RE`);
  `budgetWhy` `DEFER_WHY_RE`, `[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,31}`; `trigger` 0 to 9999; `attempt` and `attempts` 1 to 1000; `n`
  `DEFER_N_RE`, 16 lowercase hex characters. The leaf carries the four copies because it imports nothing, and
  `worker/test/defer-reasons.test.mjs` imports the sources and holds each copy to its source byte for byte. So every
  value is an id, a name, a closed word or an integer: never a path, a repository name or payload text
  (`INT-HOST-REGISTRY-CONTRACT`'s content rule).
- **The write, then the move.** `writeReason` sends ONE `MULTI` of `DEL`, `HSET` and `PEXPIRE` on the key, so a reader
  never sees this deferral's fields mixed with an earlier one's, raced against `DEFER_WRITE_TIMEOUT_MS` (2 s), and
  always BEFORE the move, so the record is in place the moment the job is delayed. The bound is load-bearing: the
  worker's client queues a command during an outage rather than rejecting it (`maxRetriesPerRequest: null`), so an
  unbounded write would hold the deferral for the whole outage. The record is ADVISORY and fails open: a write that
  fails, errors in its reply or outlasts the bound changes nothing about the deferral, and the job is moved all the
  same. So the gate waits for the write at most the 2 s bound, and a deferral never fails for its reason. Nothing is
  written where the processor's client has no `multi` (a bare test wiring, which then moves exactly as it always did)
  or the job has no string id.
- **The TTL**: `deferTtlMs(until, at)`, the time until the job is due plus `DEFER_TTL_SLACK_MS` (60 s), and never
  less than 60 s, so the record outlives the job's promotion and the pickup that follows it.
- **A timed-out MULTI may still land.** The bound stops the waiting, not the command: a queued MULTI runs when the
  connection comes back. So a timed-out write still answers its nonce, and the compare-and-delete below goes out on
  the same connection after it, so it runs after the MULTI if that lands at all. A record that lands for a job that
  ran meanwhile is never read, since the job is not delayed, and expires with its TTL.
- **A move that rejects** (a lost lock, Valkey gone) leaves a record for a job that is not delayed, so `deferTo`
  removes ITS OWN record by a compare-and-delete on the nonce (`DEFER_CAD_LUA`: `DEL` only while `HGET n` is this
  write's), bounded by the same 2 s with its own failure swallowed, and rethrows the move's rejection unchanged, so it
  reaches BullMQ's failed-attempt handling exactly as a raw `moveToDelayed` rejection always did. A plain `DEL` could
  remove the record another worker wrote for a later deferral of the same job id.
- **The log, once per outage for each queue a worker drains.** The first failed write says
  `defer_reason_unwritten { why, reason }`, `reason` a fixed word (`timeout`, `threw`, `rejected`, `error-reply`) or
  an errno-shaped code, never an error's message (it can quote a URL); nothing more is said until a write succeeds,
  which says `defer_reason_restored { why }` once. One writer per processor, and a worker runs one processor per queue
  it drains (`createWorker`'s `[QUEUE, hostQueue]`: the shared queue and, on a host with one, its own), so one episode
  spans every job that processor defers, never a line per wake, and a worker with a host queue says each line once per
  queue. Every line goes through one guarded call: a logger that throws loses its line, never the deferral, and the
  episode's state is set before the line, so it holds even when the line is lost.
- **Readers start from the delayed set; the record alone proves nothing.** A record can outlive its deferral (a late
  MULTI, a delete that failed) and a job can be delayed for a reason nobody recorded, so a reader lists the delayed
  set first (`ZRANGE ... WITHSCORES`) and reads the records (`HMGET defer:job:<id>` of `DEFER_FIELDS`, in that order)
  of the ids it found there only. The job's due time is BullMQ's own score: at 5.80.4 a delayed job's score is
  `due * 4096 + counter` (`getDelayedScore.lua`; `DELAYED_SCORE_SHIFT`), so its due time is `floor(score / 4096)`
  (`dueOfScore`, null for anything but a non-negative number or a non-empty string, so a missing member never reads
  as a due time at the epoch, and null for a due time past `DEFER_TIME_MAX_MS`, since a score anything with the URL
  wrote can be any double and such an instant has no date a console can draw). Every other instant the admin's
  reader hands on from a hash is held to the same bound (`instantOf`, null past it): a job's enqueue instant and a
  scheduler run's slot (`queuedAt`), a hold's `since` and `after`, and each answer's `at`; and the console draws an
  instant only where `utcText` draws one, a whole number of milliseconds from 0 to `DEFER_TIME_MAX_MS`, the year
  9999's last, past which it says "unknown", as it does before 1970 (`drawable` is `utcText`'s own answer). So a
  console's line never says "at unknown": an instant no date can show is a missing value, and a sentence missing one
  says its bucket's title instead (`waitingLine`). `readWaiting` reads a record whose `until` disagrees with that due
  time (outside `until` minus 5 s to the later of `until` and `at` plus 5 s, `DEFER_STALE_MS`) as no reason at all,
  an earlier episode's, never as the old reason. The leaf also holds `isSchedulerNext`: a `repeat:` job is its
  scheduler's CURRENT next run only when its id is `repeat:<scheduler>:<the scheduler's score in the queue's repeat
  zset>` (BullMQ's `isJobSchedulerJob.lua`).
- **`parseDefer(values)`**, the HMGET reply in `DEFER_FIELDS` order: null when there is no `why` (absent, null or
  empty), else every field, each null when absent or failing its rule. A `why` within `DEFER_WHY_RE` that the table
  does not hold is read as unknown (`known: false`, bucket `unknown`): a newer worker's reason an older console has no
  words for, which the console says by its token (since #737 PR 3b on the overview too, to every role: the word is of
  the reason charset, and "No reason was recorded" would be false). A `why` outside the charset is no reason at all
  (`why: null`, bucket `none`), and `readWaiting` reads such a hash as no record at all, so a held job with one still
  waits on its check. The nonce is never returned.
- **Deleted** by the writer (the `DEL` that opens each write, and its compare-and-delete after a rejected move), by
  `removeQueuedJob` once the job it removed is gone, bounded and best effort, and otherwise by its TTL. Nothing else
  deletes it, and NO DECISION READS IT.
- **The falsification test**: delete every `defer:*` key while the fleet runs, and every job is deferred, moved and
  run exactly as before; a console then says "No reason was recorded" for a delayed job (one held on `run.waitFor`
  still reads as waiting on a time or a check, from its `wait:job` hash) until its next deferral writes one, and a
  job past its due by more than the grace reads "Due since ...; no worker has taken it" with or without one. It is
  not the Redis state `OQ-008` refuses: it describes delayed jobs, which Valkey already holds, expires with them, and
  instructs nobody.
- **What a record cannot promise** (`DES-WAITING-REASONS`): a failed write leaves the previous deferral's record, until
  it expires, beside a job now delayed for another reason; a job BullMQ delays by itself (a raw gate rejection the
  queue retries, a backoff `retryDelayOf` cannot know, a job added with a delay) gets no fresh record. Both show as a
  record that is missing or whose `until` is not the job's due time, which is how a reader tells a record that
  describes the wait from one that does not. Neither is shown once the job is more than the grace past its due:
  it is then `due`, whatever its record says.
- **Acceptance**: worker/test/defer-reasons.test.mjs (the closed tables, the leaf imports nothing, the four copied
  rules, `parseDefer` against hostile values, the TTL, `dueOfScore`, `isSchedulerNext`, and "INT-DEFER-REASON-KEY
  restates the leaf: its reason table is DEFER_WHYS with each bucket, its fields block DEFER_FIELDS, its bucket lists
  DEFER_BUCKETS", which reads this section's reason table, its fields block and both of its bucket lists and holds
  each two-way to the leaf), worker/test/defer-write.test.mjs (the write before the move as one transaction, a
  failed or slow write still moves, the raw rethrow after the compare-and-delete, one log episode, a logger that
  throws, `retryDelayOf`, `noteRetry`, "BY SHAPE: no module in worker/src moves a job to the delayed set except
  through defer-write.mjs", "BY SHAPE: every reason in the table is written by a site, and every site writes a reason
  from the table"), worker/test/defer-write.integration.test.mjs (a real Valkey and BullMQ: the record and the
  score's due, a failed write, a wrong token, a retry's record against BullMQ's own delay), the gate tests that record
  each site's reason (wait-gate, pause-gate, scope-mutex, host-budget-gate, podman-restart-hold, netns-keeper-young,
  processor-bundles), admin/test/read-model-waiting.test.mjs (the reader, "readWaiting: every instant it hands on is
  one a page can draw, at most DEFER_TIME_MAX_MS: ..." among them) and admin/test/read-model-waiting.valkey.test.mjs
  (the reader against a real Valkey and BullMQ).

## INT-MANAGED-FORK-CONTRACT

**Console/terminal -> queue -> worker -> runner**, issue #648 (`REQ-MANAGED-RUN-FORK`).

- **Queue input**: `fork` is a closed object with `id` (32 lowercase hex), `fromJob` (1–200 run-id characters),
  `fromEntry` (1–128 alphanumeric, underscore or hyphen), `position` (`before` or `at`), `sourceDigest` (64 lowercase
  hex), and `rootKey` (32 lowercase hex). Optional `message` is at most 16,384 UTF-8 bytes and contains no NUL.
  It carries no filesystem path or policy override. Optional top-level `thinkingLevel` is one of `off`, `minimal`,
  `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`; compatibility with the effective model is checked before spend and again
  in the runner. `forkPolicy` is the SHA-256 fingerprint of the current parsed trigger entry, re-read at pickup.
  `forkReserveMicros` is the preview's reserved micro-dollar amount (a non-negative safe integer, or null where
  no dollar reservation applies). Preview freezes provider/model and any effective positive per-job cost ceiling.
  A zero-rated preview becoming paid, or a current paid cap greater than the confirmed reservation, returns
  `fork-reservation-changed` before minting rather than silently increasing the authorized spend. A trigger with
  `run.awaitInput: true` returns `fork-await-input-unsupported` before spend: parked replies do not yet preserve
  fork namespaces. Recovery of an already admitted managed fork instead restores that fork's own durable checkpoint;
  it does not reselect the original source entry. Recovery-attempt records remain unavailable as new fork sources.
- **Session identity**: Root keys keep their existing derivation. A managed fork uses `<rootKey>.<id>`, stored at
  `<PI_SESSIONS_DIR>/<rootKey>/forks/<id>/`; a same-repository pull request on the worker-derived fork branch
  resolves that same lineage. Original and fork locks, canonical files and sidecars are separate.
- **Publication**: Sources are published only after a completed exit 0 and a confirmed-dead container. A failed
  infrastructure attempt cannot freeze the source identity of a later successful retry. Recovery attempts are not
  published as sources in this release. Only an issue job that opted into transcript retention with `run.resume`,
  or an explicitly requested managed fork, may prime a source. A configured session directory, derived root and
  final per-job transcript file are required. Opted-out jobs are never archived merely because they have a live
  transcript. A final exact quiet workspace point is captured before publication, even when `run.recover` was off. Live intermediate
  points are available only where the existing recovery checkpoint path was armed and could pause the container.
- **Private source artifacts**: `<PI_SESSIONS_DIR>/.fork-sources/<source-key>/manifest.json` and `transcript.jsonl`,
  where `source-key` is the first 32 hex characters of SHA-256 of `fork-source` + NUL + run id. Directories are 0700,
  files 0600, source opens reject symlinks and non-regular files. The manifest commit follows a durable transcript
  write and binds version, run id, original session key, base SHA, venue, pi version, attempt, host, optional host
  queue, creation time, transcript byte count/hash and a digest of that metadata. An existing source cannot be
  replaced with different bytes. Retention defaults are seven days, 8 MiB per transcript, 256 MiB total source
  transcripts, 1,024 source directories and 64 captured points per run. A separate `.workspaces` checkpointer keeps
  historical snapshots, bounded by its 20 GiB store cap and conservative base admission. Archive mutations are
  serialized within the worker; a busy optional archive is skipped by name. Unsafe base extensions leave a private
  refusal marker, so selection returns `fork-unsafe-extensions` before a job can spend.
- **Read failures and context**: Missing, expired, malformed, incompatible or digest-mismatched artifacts return
  determinate `refused` results. Temporary filesystem failures (`EIO`, `EAGAIN`, `EMFILE`, `ENFILE`, `ETIMEDOUT`,
  `EINTR`) return `unavailable` through source, point and restore reads, so pickup throws an infrastructure retry;
  archive restore's `skipped` infrastructure answer is also retryable. The base ref and its commit/tree objects are
  verified before clone. These source gates use the fork archive's own TTL/byte limits. Ordinary resume chain,
  age and context-percent behavior is unchanged; a new fork does not inherit its source's stored occupancy estimate.
  Changing models may change the context window, and this feature does not prove before spend that a selected
  transcript fits that new window. No provider context-error classification is claimed here.
- **Exact points**: Private `points/<hash>.json` files bind entry id, `at` position, archive sequence, base SHA,
  transcript byte offset and SHA-256. A selected **before** point resolves its parent's **at** artifact, except
  first-user **before**, which explicitly uses the original base. The retained prefix must end at that exact safe
  tree entry with no pending tool call. Partial workspace snapshots and snapshots that dropped ignored files are
  unavailable. Recovery's default newest-two retention is unchanged; only the fork archive enables history reads.
- **Runner environment**: An image must declare capability `fork` when `job.fork` or `job.thinkingLevel` is set,
  otherwise pickup returns `job-image-fork-unsupported`. `PI_FORK_ENTRY` and `PI_FORK_POSITION` are emitted together
  from validated job lineage, and require a staged `PI_SESSION_FILE`. Combining fork selection with command/recovery
  flags is refused. Recovery of an existing managed fork omits `PI_FORK_ENTRY` and `PI_FORK_POSITION` and uses its
  own checkpoint with the normal recovery flags instead.
  `PI_THINKING_LEVEL` is emitted only when selected. All three names are reserved and structural, never trigger-bound
  secrets. The runner branches its own staged copy using pinned pi's tree APIs and records effective model/thinking
  changes before continuing. No raw source archive is mounted.
- **Console**: Operator-only `GET /api/fork-points?id=<run-id>` returns entry id, parent id, closed type/role metadata
  and supported `positions`, never message text or an archive path. `POST /api/act/run-fork/preview` accepts `jobId`,
  `entry`, `position`, optional `provider`, `model`, `thinking`, `message`; the browser form may send `point` as
  `<entry>:<position>` instead of the separate entry/position fields. The ordinary single-use confirmation ticket,
  audit-before-write, CSRF and write-role guards apply. Confirmation and pickup revalidate current policy and source.
- **Run record**: Optional `fork` contains only `id`, `fromJob`, `fromEntry`, `position` and effective `model` (or
  null), rebuilt through the closed lineage validator. `fromEntry` in a run record is restricted to pi's generated
  eight-character lowercase-hex ids; an arbitrary custom entry id causes the optional lineage record to be omitted.
  Operator message, raw transcript, source path and policy
  payload are omitted. Optional `forkSource` records archive availability for an opted-in source attempt:
  `{saved: boolean, reason: null or closed token, pointSkipped?: closed token}`. `forkArchiveFact` rebuilds those
  fields against its closed reason vocabulary and maps arbitrary values to `unavailable`; successful source
  publication has null reason, while a primed run that did not complete records `not-completed`. A failed optional
  point capture may coexist with a successfully saved source. Archive failure is fail-open for the original job,
  with its named reason retained in the record. Jobs that never requested source retention gain no archive fact.
- **Constraint audit**: `CONST-ISOLATION-CONTAINER-PER-JOB`, `CONST-BUDGET-BEFORE-TOKENS`,
  `CONST-RETRY-INFRA-ONLY`, `CONST-TOKEN-SCOPED-PER-JOB`, `CONST-PI-VERSION-PINNED` and
  `CONST-MERGE-NEVER-AUTOMATIC` **UNCHANGED, checked**: managed forks use normal container/admission gates, determinate
  refusal results and exact pinned APIs, copy only their own transcript, log no message text, and create separate
  reviewable pull requests without any merge action.

## INT-APPROVAL-STATE-CONTRACT

- **Declaration**: `run.gates` is a nonempty distinct string array, maximum 32 entries, maximum 80 characters per
  action, matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*(?::[a-z][a-z0-9-]*)?$`. `run.gateTimeout` optionally declares integer days 1..365;
  `run.gateBudgetRaiseUsd` is an absolute one-container cap, strictly above `run.maxCostUsd`, only beside
  `budget-raise`. All three travel at job level through normalized triggers, every forge filter and the queue.
  They never become event payload fields. Gate declarations require resumable forge flows and arm `awaitInput`.
- **Container input**: internal `PI_APPROVAL_GATES` is a JSON string array; internal `PI_APPROVAL_DECISION` is JSON
  `{requestId, action, toolCallId, decision}` with no human text. `decision` is approved, declined or question. The accepted human text is staged in the existing read-only `event.json` comment body; the runner reads it once before extensions or provider calls and combines it with the decision metadata. Only the host-owned
  decision reaches this input: a queued `approvalDecision` is discarded. Both variables are reserved from secrets.
  Gate jobs require image capabilities `approvalGates` AND `exitAuth` before mint or reservation.
- **Runner output**: authenticated exit 0 / `awaiting-approval` carries `approval: {action, toolCallId}` only when
  the run ends on its own successful terminating approval tool. Unknown actions and shadowed tools cannot park.
  Runner exit-2 reasons: `approval-config-invalid`, `approval-without-session`, `approval-shadowed`,
  `approval-decision-invalid`. Summary and decision text never enter the exit metadata or public record.
- **Private state**: `run:approval:request:<requestId>` stores version 1 normalized request identity, state, and
  optional immutable decision and claimed job ID. `requestId` is SHA-256 of requesting queue job ID, NUL, tool-call ID.
  Request identity binds run ID, forge/repository/target, action, call ID, config digest, session key, exact canonical SHA-256 transcript digest, host, optional declared host queue, created
  time and optional expiry plus private original queue data. The target key is derived from forge/repository/type/
  number; `run:approval:due` is a sorted deadline index, with a hashed per-host deadline index to prevent a down host starving another host. No pending key TTL implements expiry. Terminal infrastructure failures finish their same-job claim; nonterminal retries retain it, and pending bounded terminal finalizers join worker shutdown before Redis closes. Unknown/missing versions or malformed state are determinate refusals, never authority. State transitions are
  pending to decided to claimed to finished; withdrawn live policy may retire an unanswered/decided request or the same job's claim directly to finished, preserving any accepted decision; the first decision wins, same-decision delivery and same-job claim are
  idempotent, another claim refuses. Finish removes the active target mapping and retains the immutable decision for 32 days (longer than queue retention).
  Private decision text is bounded to the existing 8 KiB answer limit and is never logged as metadata.
- **Reply binding**: the queue binds a gated comment to the active request observed at ingress; an explicitly named
  different request is rejected before enqueue. A reply that arrived before publication stays unbound until the
  held-reply path enqueues it after publication. The worker refuses an unbound decision. The console carries the
  request ID read from its original parked record; its preview and confirmation cannot approve a later request.
- **Session binding**: host preflight checks a real key directory, a bounded regular canonical transcript, age/TTL/
  lineage limits and the unanswered original call before spending. Reused provider tool-call IDs cannot transfer a decision to different transcript bytes. The normal session resolver must still stage a
  resumed session with the request's exact key; pi's projected context is independently checked in the runner.
- **Public record**: optional `approval` is rebuilt as `{requestId, action, decision?, actorKind?, actorId?, decidedAt?}`.
  Request IDs are 64 hex; actions must be declaration tokens. A decided record carries approved/declined/question,
  forge/operator/panel/system actor kind, SHA-256 actor identifier (or `expiry`/`revocation` for system), and integer milliseconds.
  Model summaries, human reasons, names and arbitrary nested fields are discarded. No approval is inferred from
  job data when building a record.
- **Expiry**: only a persisted system decline and the exact `approval-expiry-<requestId>` job, carrying the same
  request ID and `expiry-<requestId>` delivery ID, can continue an expired request. The host checks due state each
  minute, including overdue declines left by enqueue failure. A deterministic queue ID prevents repeated sweeps
  making multiple continuations. The comment marker is a private NX key retained for 32 days; failure to post remains the existing
  adapter's named failure. A later policy refusal finishes the request without granting authority to another job.
- **Traces to**: `REQ-APPROVAL-GATES`, `DES-APPROVAL-DECISION-IS-HOST-AUTHORITY`,
  `INT-TRIGGERS-FILE-CONTRACT`, `INT-CONTAINER-JOB-INPUTS`, `INT-RUNNER-EXIT-CODE-PROTOCOL`,
  `INT-SESSION-STORE-CONTRACT`, `INT-RUN-HISTORY-FILE-CONTRACT`.

## INT-MODEL-COOLDOWN-KEY

**Worker → Valkey → workers and doctor (#716).** Storage is owned by `worker/src/model-failover.mjs`.

- `dispatch:model-cooldown:<sha256(exact provider/model)>` holds JSON `{ kind, until }`. `kind` is a closed provider-failure token except `context-overflow`; `until` is a nonnegative safe-integer epoch millisecond instant no later than 253402300799999. A missing/expired key means no cooldown. Malformed state throws as infrastructure for pickup; doctor publishes an unreadable warning.
- A reset is capped to `MODEL_COOLDOWN_MAX_MS` (six hours); no reset uses six hours for quota, `MODEL_RECHECK_MS` (60 seconds) for rate limit/overload. A past reset gives a minimum one-second TTL. An atomic Lua update keeps the later existing reset rather than shortening it. The TTL expires the observation. Model identity is hashed in the key and never taken from provider error text.
- `dispatch:model-attempt:<sha256(queueName:jobId)>` holds JSON `{ ref, safe, failure, modelWhy? }` without expiry while a queued retry may still exist. `ref` is a validated exact provider/model; `modelWhy`, when present, is the closed selection token; `safe` is boolean; `failure` is null or the closed signed failure object. Retained keys are small worker-owned retry-safety state; cleanup must follow queue removal, never a run record written before the queue acknowledges completion. Written unsafe before spawn, then updated only from verified matching exit-1 metadata. Missing state on retry refuses unless a trusted previous run record proves the container never started; no transcript or queued field supplies that proof. This is worker state, not queued attacker input or a transcript inference.
- Doctor reads only candidates named in configured failover triggers, with bounded commands and an injected clock. It does not scan the keyspace. Published warning checks use `INT-DOCTOR-RESULTS-KEY`; the console displays their existing observation age.
- Temporary cooldown/window exhaustion uses `model-cooldown`/`model-window` in `INT-DEFER-REASON-KEY`; endpoint exhaustion uses its existing reason. All permanently ineligible candidates return `model-failover-no-candidate` with no container start. Store faults retry as infrastructure. No new paid attempts are added.

## INT-WATCH-EVENT-CONTRACT

**Collector to receiver to worker.** `watchSources` is reviewed hand-written configuration, never inferred from a delivery. Each source declares hmac-sha256 verification, a secret environment name, an optional project, maxBodyBytes (at most 65536) and a daily delivery cap. Watch rules have unique bounded ids, a declared source, structured fingerprint fields, optional severity/label predicates, minCount, bounded window/cooldown durations, maxPerDay and maxFingerprints. The trigger loader owns validation (`worker/src/watch-contract.mjs`); unknown fields refuse. `INT-TRIGGERS-FILE-CONTRACT` is extended by these fields and by the optional reviewed decide block, whose shadow default is true.

`POST /watch/<source>` requires JSON and `X-Watch-Timestamp` (epoch seconds), `X-Watch-Id` and `X-Watch-Signature: v1=<lowercase hex>`. The signature is HMAC-SHA256 over `v1.<timestamp>.<delivery>.` followed by the exact body bytes. The timestamp tolerance is five minutes; verification precedes JSON parsing. Unknown sources return 404, failed authentication 401, oversize 413, invalid JSON/schema 400 and unavailable source secrets/store 503. Accepted ingestion returns 202 with held, suppressed, capped or unmatched status and per-rule results. A held digest is not a claim that a paid job has started.

The finding schema is source (optional, must match route), fields (structured strings), severity, count, firstSeen, lastSeen and samples. At most eight samples of 2048 bytes each are accepted. Fingerprints hash a length-delimited source/rule/field tuple; identity alone does not bypass source/rule/cardinality caps. Replay/digest/cooldown/cap admission is atomic in Valkey. Delayed queue entries carry the finding reference only. Private evidence and histories of findings have bounded retention; ordinary run records never contain samples or structured field values. Optional `run.issue.closeAfter` enables quiet closure, disabled by default. A durable per-source issue index is capped at 4096 identities before forge calls. Suppressed matched deliveries still advance activity; a bounded sweep closes only a matching activity version and reopens if activity raced the remote close. Uncertain remote results are explicit. Issue identity excludes quiet policy and recurrence reopens the same issue.

## INT-WATCH-FINDINGS-FILE

**Worker to fresh watch container, extending `INT-CONTAINER-JOB-INPUTS`.** `/job/watch.json` is exactly `{ "version": 1, "mode": "investigate" }` on the existing read-only job mount. Malformed, linked or oversized markers refuse rather than falling back to writable ordinary behavior. `/job/event.json` contains the bounded watch metadata; `/job/findings.json` contains capped host-redacted evidence as data, never executable settings. The workspace is read-only and a watch job has no forge-mint or outbox-chain authority. `/job/board.json`, when staged, is adopted board data only.

An optional `/job/watch-decision.json` contains exactly version 1, model `{provider,id}`, bounded scalar state and typed questions, at most 32768 bytes. It selects deterministic execution: exactly one guarded classifier call, no chat agent or loader. `/outbox/decision.json` holds version 1, stopReason, answers and optional usage, at most 16384 bytes. The worker distrusts every output field and validates reviewed options/probabilities before action. Unknown/output-priced classifiers and unboundable or over-cap calls are refused. `INT-RUNNER-EXIT-CODE-PROTOCOL` metering and ordinary reservations remain authoritative.

`/job/watch-tools.json` contains version 1, an optional reviewed decisionModel and named queries, each with reviewed HTTPS endpoint/query/optional resolved headers. Only fixed named queries may be invoked; no model-supplied URL, query or header override is accepted. query_logs uses a ten-second timeout, refuses redirects and caps response bytes at 65536 and rows at 100. Credentials never enter its trace. Trusted decide calls dispatch through the process-metered runtime. The primary and reviewed classifier providers are both credential-probed before admission spends; only their derived provider credential variables are forwarded. Secondary credential names are reserved against trigger and bundle overrides, with a final env-construction guard. No ordinary extension factories load in watch mode.

## INT-WATCH-TRACE-STREAM

**Runner file to worker to private Valkey evidence store.** The runner appends `/outbox/watch-trace.jsonl`, capped at 128 entries and 262144 bytes. Entries have bounded id, timestamp, kind, callId and status. Query starts retain reviewed query text and finishes retain row counts; decision starts retain state/questions and finishes retain probabilities/usage; board entries identify proposals. Started/failed entries preserve partial operations without exception bodies or header values. Containers never receive Valkey access. The worker validates/redacts/caps every imported entry. The watch store retains at most 1000 trace entries per finding for seven days; a bounded trimming count names missing entries. Expiry or store failure is unavailable, never an empty successful trace. Known job credentials are redacted before private trace or board persistence, as for the operator transcript.

Operators may inspect private state/query/sample evidence through the dedicated authorized endpoint. Viewers receive only the explicit public projection of identifiers, counts, stages, choices, probabilities and cost. This projection applies before JSON serialization and server rendering; hiding a browser element is not authorization. The run record's optional decision summary contains no state values. Reason tokens include watch-cooldown, watch-cap, watch-unmatched, watch-ignored, decide-refused and decide-unanswered; `INT-DEFER-REASON-KEY` remains the authority for their catalog registration and buckets.

## INT-WATCH-BOARD-FILE

**Job proposal to worker validation to operator adoption, extending `INT-OUTBOX-CONTRACT`.** `/outbox/board.json` is a version-1 document containing blocks, at most 16384 UTF-8 bytes. Each block has a unique bounded id, a fixed type and a traceId provenance reference. Types are number, line, table, note, hypotheses and timeline; `worker/src/watch-board.mjs` owns their bounded field schemas. Unknown fields and executable markup schemas refuse. Strings are inert data and are escaped by the renderer. Invalid or oversize proposals never replace the existing adopted board.

Board audit `beforeDigest` hashes the read snapshot. The request-backed `afterDigest` binds the reviewed change and, for adoption, the proposed blocks; it is not a claim to hash Valkey's future JSON serialization. Expected board version and proposal identity are rechecked atomically at mutation. Viewer board projections contain version, freeze state and structural counts, never agent-authored block values. Doctor adds `watch.sources` and bounded hashed per-source credential check ids under the existing `INT-DOCTOR-RESULTS-KEY` schema.
