Proposals are retained separately from adopted blocks. Board updates compare expectedVersion atomically, retain at most twenty versions/proposals and expire after seven days without a store refresh. A frozen board refuses adoption. Audited operator actions board-freeze, board-unfreeze, board-adopt, board-revert and board-clear use the existing preview/confirm mechanism; freeze, revert and clear are destructive. `INT-CONSOLE-AUDIT-LOG` is extended by these action kinds with the same audit-before-write and failed-write correlation semantics. A stale preview refuses rather than adopting onto changed state. Viewer board projections exclude private text/query/proposal data.

## INT-TOUCH-INDEX

**Worker, CLI and admin → fleet readers**, issue #770 (`REQ-ZERO-TOUCH-RATE`).

- `touch:index` is a bounded sorted set of event ids scored by the trusted human-event time; `touch:event:<id>` is
  its rebuilt JSON body. `touch:meta` holds `since`, `indexed` and a monotonic loss `horizon`. `touch:pending` holds
  unresolved intent ids and times. The source is `worker/src/touch-state.mjs`.
- A touch body contains `v:1`, a lowercase SHA-256 `id`, `type:"touch"`, validated `runId`, `at` (nonnegative integer
  milliseconds), and one closed `cause`:
  ```json
  ["question-answer", "approval-decision", "rerun", "config-fix", "steer", "cancel"]
  ```
  Optional rebuilt fields are opaque SHA-256 `scopeId`, validated project id and safe target, millisecond `endedAt`,
  `parkedAt`, `receivedAt`, closed `answerSource` (`forge`, `console`, `panel`, `draft`) and validated `draftRunId`.
  Nonces determine ids but are not retained. A pre-start stop uses `type:"stop"` and no cause. A non-human
  approval closure uses `type:"wait-end"`, no cause, and the closed reason `approval-expired` or
  `approval-policy-changed` (`WAIT_END_REASONS`). It ends only an approval wait, never adds a touched run,
  cause count, stop or human-answer median. Expiry uses the trusted deadline; withdrawal uses its first accepted
  terminal time. Publication uses durable intent/repair and cannot replay a transition. No body carries a
  question, answer, instruction, identity credential or payload. Unsupported properties are dropped.
- Events are idempotent by id, and one run contributes once to the numerator. Primary-cause charts use earliest
  successful event, breaking ties by vocabulary order; all causes remain available. Stops have their own distinct
  job count and never enter the denominator. Internal grouping jobs do not enter workload stops either.
- Scope identity distinguishes local host/folder pairs without publishing paths. An unbound shared-queue local
  cancellation has no invented host identity. Scoped stop counts report unassignable evidence separately.
- Retention follows the writer's history setting, bounded to 365 days and 30,000 indexed events; zero history
  retention still means this finite bound. Trim, missing bodies, lost index/start and unresolved intents are named
  coverage gaps. An indexed-but-missing set is already unknown before a later write can reset its epoch.
- Pending uncertainty conservatively makes the covered rate unavailable until repaired. A zero denominator has
  `rate:null`. Reads never interpret missing events or an older client as proof that no person intervened.
- Waiting evidence is separately bounded: a park older than known touch history, without a retained terminal
  answer, cannot prove it is still open. `totals.waitingPartial` and `waitingUnknown` expose that uncertainty;
  waiting hours, median and pending count are null, while valid current-rate counts remain available. Affected
  project/repository streaks are unknown and cannot earn a zero-touch badge. Retained terminal answer facts can
  close that old wait without guessing from an expired index event.
- `touch-outbox/<event-id>.json` below the private logs root holds `{state,event}` with `pending` or `applied` state.
  Publication repairs applied entries idempotently and never re-executes an action. An interrupted pending entry
  remains unknown until its owner can prove the outcome. Every successful action whose metric could not finish
  returns a fixed warning; CLI, panel and console preserve it without turning success into a retry.
- **Run-record extension** (`INT-RUN-HISTORY-FILE-CONTRACT`): wired writers stamp optional `touchTrackingVersion:1`
  and `touchScopeId`; at most 16 rebuilt `touches` carry source facts. The optional fixed
  `touchLineageSkipped:"source-unavailable"` records an admitted answer whose exact parked source could not be proved.
  These facts survive a same-id retry's record replacement while its fresh outcome and usage remain authoritative.
  `purpose:"zero-touch-grouping"` identifies internal analysis, including pre-container refusals; it remains ordinary
  history/spend but is excluded from workload rates and activity. Missing legacy fields are unknown, never false.
- **Session extension** (`INT-SESSION-STORE-CONTRACT`): new parked sidecars use
  `{v:2,runId,at,transcriptIdentity}`. The identity is the store's private canonical-file identity, not a path. Staging
  attaches `parkedSource:{runId,at}` only when that sidecar matches the exact canonical descriptor already checked
  and copied. Timestamp-only and v1 sidecars still establish a parked session but cannot prove answer lineage.
  A proven runner resume uses its staged source, never an earlier lookup that a concurrent promotion could replace.
- **Held-reply receipt extension** (`INT-STEER-INBOX-CONTRACT`): a released held comment carries optional host-authored
  `replyReceivedAt` at job level, copied only from its validated held entry time for a resumable comment. Pickup uses
  it before the new queue timestamp, so queueing or park delays never extend the wait after an answer arrived. It
  never enters the forge event payload. Phrase-prefixed and phrase-free replies both need exact staged source proof.
- **Acceptance**: real Valkey duplicate/loss/retention tests and production producer tests recount two hosts, retain
  uncertainty across repair/retry, distinguish stops and scopes, and reject false source attribution and false zero.

## INT-QUESTION-GROUPS

**Operator configuration → worker → classifier container → safe assignment readers**, issue #770.

- Optional top-level `zeroTouch` in `INT-TRIGGERS-FILE-CONTRACT` contains `capture` (boolean), explicit classifier
  `model`, dollar-string `maxCostUsd`, optional `confidence` (default 0.9, above 0.5 and at most 1), and `names` mapping
  opaque 32-hex group ids to human names of 1 to 120 Unicode characters without control/bidi formatting characters.
  It is strictly validated; unknown keys are refused. Names are operator configuration, never model output.
- The text-bearing `zero-touch:questions:private:*` corpus is separate from safe `meta:*`, `index`, `corpus` and
  repository `groups:*` state. Queue jobs contain only `questionGrouping:{runId,digest,configDigest}`. Neither public
  snapshots nor ordinary configuration/state/tool results fetch the private bodies.
- Opt-in capture reads a bounded contiguous final context from the parked transcript because `await_human_input`
  has no question argument. It uses the actual job's complete credential redactor before storing anything. Missing
  redactor, unreadable source or an oversized last entry becomes a named status, not guessed earlier text.
- Limits come from `QUESTION_GROUP_LIMITS`: 16,384 excerpt bytes, 262,144 total input bytes, 1,000 private entries,
  5,000 safe metadata entries, 14 existing candidate groups plus `new`/`unassigned`, and at most 90 private days
  (the shorter of positive history retention and 90; zero is still 90). Loss or expiry never establishes a new group.
- Safe statuses are closed:
  ```json
  ["unassigned", "pending", "assigned", "source-expired", "source-unavailable", "source-oversize", "candidates-expired", "group-limit", "stale", "refused", "failed"]
  ```
  Safe metadata carries validated source id/scope/project/repository/time/digest, optional trigger index and bounded
  context-truncation fact. Assigned groups hold opaque ids, counts and source links. The private exemplar is read
  only by workers constructing an explicitly confirmed classification, including unnamed exemplars across hosts.
- Each paid request has one queue attempt. On every pickup, including after deferral JSON serialization, the worker
  re-resolves the narrow reference against current reviewed configuration and private evidence; queued execution
  settings are not authority. Source project billing remains in force, and a removed source project refuses.
- The free gate checks classifier type, input-only finite pricing and a conservative full-context cost bound before
  ordinary admission/reservation. Primary text-model and secondary classifier credentials must pass the same free
  probe as container environment construction. There is no provider call on GET.
- `questionGrouping` in the image capability label gates this mode before reserve. The worker stages private
  `question-grouping.json` in read-only `/job`, with a read-only empty workspace and writable per-job `/outbox`.
  No Valkey, forge or unrelated forwarded credential, package or global extension is admitted. The guarded runner
  branches before extension loading or an agent session; the normal model/cost meter is already installed.
- `question-group.json` is exactly `{version:1,slot,confidence}` with a reviewed candidate slot, `new` or `unassigned`.
  It has no names, answers or summaries. The collector validates bounds, confidence, config/source digest and group
  revision before atomic assignment; concurrent stale imports and malformed output never buy another call. A person
  may explicitly confirm another paid request for an uncertain pending result, with that cost stated in its preview.
- **Acceptance**: actual queue/store/runtime/admission/executor/collector tests plus the image's authenticated
  network-free zero-cap probe prove guards, no extension/tool execution, privacy, idempotence and stale-source refusal.

## INT-ZERO-TOUCH-FIXES

**Confirmed operator write → fleet telemetry and on-demand console**, issue #770.

- `zero-touch:fixes:meta:*` stores safe typed fix facts: opaque id, `instructions` or `config` kind, time, source run,
  scope/project, one refusal reason or group id, optional trigger index, state and optional undone time. Bounded
  private Undo/proof state is separate. Index entries expire with history retention, with a finite 365-day/5,000-row
  ceiling when history is unlimited.
- Stage a pending fix before a nonurgent write, then commit or refuse its metadata. Exact file/trigger proof can
  repair an applied write without executing it again. Arbitrary paths outside the configured file allowlist are
  never read for repair; uncertain conflicting state remains partial. Safe public reads omit instruction text and actors.
- Instruction planning is console-only, uses retained source-job identity plus the current loader's trigger match,
  and binds the raw trigger digest and file comparison to the ticket. Kind/index alone is insufficient. A stale or
  expired source refuses. Append obeys the existing 2,000-character limit and cron restriction. Undo requires the
  exact confirmed trigger/instructions and preserves later edits rather than overwriting them.
- Ordinary configuration previews may carry validated `becauseRun` context from a retained refusal. The parsed
  configuration page says which source it carries; its script preserves the source across configuration navigation
  and adds it only to the derived configuration-action set. Confirm uses the normal action funnel and records a fix
  only if that write actually succeeds. An unrelated write has no attribution.
- Counts measure occurrences of a typed refusal reason or question group, including untouched refusals and
  unanswered questions. Before and after spans are equal actual elapsed spans, with subsequent workload exposure.
  Undo ends the observation at the reversal time and never establishes current effectiveness. A later identical
  instruction append has a new confirmation identity and its own fix, rather than reviving the reverted metadata.
  A group comparison with unclassified sources is partial; no later runs or missing coverage establishes no success.
- Console reads are `/runs/zero-touch?days=7|30|90` with optional project and opaque scope. The page is on-demand,
  viewer-readable, and operator groups/actions are projected away before rendering for viewers. Project/scope filters
  constrain fix observations and pending/unassigned source counts as well as rates and groups. Read-only operators
  keep reads. `/runs?touched=1&days=...` preserves its window/scope through pagination and live canonical queries.
  The reserved analytics-only `project=~` selects missing project attribution without colliding with a real
  project named `unassigned`. It is accepted only here and on touched Runs, not in ordinary project-id fields.
  Neither feature changes the version or payload of `/api/state` or the existing event stream.
- Actions are `zero-touch-group` (paid), `zero-touch-name`, `zero-touch-instruction` and `zero-touch-undo`. They use
  existing same-origin/session/role/read-only guards, single-use preview tickets, exact comparison and audit-before-write.
  No model-callable instruction tool is introduced. Native reads work without script; writes stay disabled.
- **Acceptance**: HTTP persistence and real-browser tests exercise diff/Confirm/Undo, stale writes, source binding,
  linked configuration, roles, no JavaScript, CSP, live filters and >50 touched-run pagination.


## INT-SANDBOX-OPENER-CONTRACT

- `pi-dispatch-open://<open-or-attach>/<encoded-id>?host=<worker-name>` carries only the fixed verb, checked ID and host. Parsing decodes once and refuses noncanonical encodings, duplicate/extra fields, fragments, userinfo and unknown verbs/hosts before any terminal is opened.
- `sandbox-hosts.json` is a versioned operator-only configuration mapping worker names to a trusted SSH target or explicit local mode, deployment directory and absolute Node/CLI paths. Fleet edits have expected-file guards. An exported mapping is credential-free; it becomes opener authority only through an explicit local import. Links never update it.
- Current-user registration is LaunchServices on macOS, an x-scheme-handler desktop entry on Linux and HKCU protocol registration followed by a shell association-change notification on Windows. Linux's measured URL dispatcher is GNOME/GIO, which implements standard desktop-entry quoting; xdg-utils 1.1.3's generic fallback does not. The terminal helper shows the full constructed command and requires Enter; Cancel/EOF performs no SSH or sandbox action. An unsupported terminal integration refuses with the copy route.
- Deployment loading uses the shared descriptor/trusted-chain and loader-faithful environment reader. It rejects unreadable/untrusted settings and contradictory ambient capabilities. Only sandbox, validated runtime identity and host-control connection settings enter the re-executed host process; container environment remains its original credential-free allowlist.

## INT-SANDBOX-CONTROL-CONTRACT

- Host-bound `pi-sandbox-prepare@<host>` is a dedicated control queue, never a `pi-jobs` queue. It is consumed at concurrency one without run slots, dollar/job-count reservations, agent calls, ordinary history or status comments.
- Confirmed prepare requests bind a generated `sb-` ID, host, repository, reference, trigger index/digest, effective-plan digest and optional pin. The host revalidates all determinate configuration before mint/clone. Expired requests refuse; infrastructure alone retries within the queue's finite attempts.
- Pending claims, payloads, clone calls and retained result counts/ages are bounded by the exported control constants. Pending, preparing, ready, refused, failed and unknown are distinct. A matching final manifest reconciles a retry; a foreign ID collision never overwrites. Staging uses worker-owned job temporary directories. The per-ID lock lives in the jobs root, outside retained-workspace sweeps; dead-owner takeover reclaims its recorded stage before retry. Jobs and retention roots must share a filesystem for atomic publication, checked before mint/clone. An abandoned standalone CLI stage whose ID is never retried follows the existing worker boot orphan sweep.
- Pin requests bind the existing workspace generation and observed deadline/pin. They call the same pin writer on the owning host. Preparation and pin results contain checked IDs, host, deadline and fixed status fields, never credentials or forge payloads.

## INT-SANDBOX-SESSIONS-CONTRACT

- The sandbox CLI starts a detached private monitor. `sandbox:shell:<host>:<id-digest>` holds a versioned, expiring session: checked host/ID, random 32-hex nonce, immutable 64-hex container ID, venue, terminal-reported account, since and heartbeat instants. It contains no input or idle-time claim. These records are operator-private, never run records.
- The lease lasts 45 seconds and is renewed while the runtime confirms this incarnation. The renew's Lua script uses Valkey TIME for index expiry/pruning; key TTL is authority and host/console clocks are display only. A sorted index expires crashed observations by score. Reads are bounded to 256 entries and distinguish unreachable/malformed/truncated information. An expired observation says tracking was lost, not that the runtime container disappeared.
- `sandbox:end:<nonce>` is a short-lived request bound to host, ID, nonce, immutable container ID and a random per-request ID. Acknowledgements include that request ID so an earlier failed End cannot answer a later one. The monitor checks that exact incarnation, removes only that container and acknowledges only confirmed disappearance. A failed stop has an explicit response. Renew/release compare ownership atomically so an old process cannot erase a replacement lease. A timed-out requester removes its own pending request and reports ambiguity.
- The monitor survives terminal detach/closure and keeps the workspace. Its persistent client rejects disconnected commands without buffering and reconnects after an outage. Cleanup refusals/failures become bounded operator-private notices, with the admitted runtime evidence preserved. It cleans the session network only after the runtime confirms the container is absent, using existing guarded egress teardown. Unknown runtime answers never authorize stopping a replacement or cleaning its network.

## INT-SANDBOX-INVENTORY-CONTRACT

- Each worker publishes `sandbox:inventory:h:<host>` with version, publication time, bounded retained rows, overflow count, retention window and validated credential-free image/venue/size/egress preview settings. `sandbox:inventory:hosts` discovers publishers.
- The writer uses the existing cached telemetry projection rather than another filesystem scan, publishes every 60 seconds and retains the last record for seven days. Reads bound host count to 64 and keep missing, malformed, stale, truncated and empty distinct. Shutdown retains the last publication; its age is always visible. Published configuration is preview evidence, never worker execution authority.
- The console's own host still checks the actual manifest; the worker revalidates requests and the CLI revalidates before opening. No credential, absolute workspace path, repository payload or ref is published in inventory.

## INT-ANSWER-DRAFT-STORE

- The host’s `answerer:` keyspace holds per-source-run bounded metadata and private input/draft bodies, addressed by
  SHA256 of validated run IDs. `answerer:index` is a bounded expiring sorted index, not authority to answer a run.
  Queue entries are refs only: job name/purpose `answer-draft`, `answerDraft: {runId,ruleId}`. The worker reconstructs
  the forge job only from the host’s private captured source and current reviewed configuration.
- Metadata version 1 holds validated source/draft/rule IDs, closed status/passReason/category, confidence and normalized
  probability evidence, validated revision-bound source descriptors, optional cost, draft digest, send time/name and
  `as-drafted` or `edited` disposition. Public to operators means metadata only; question and draft bodies require
  an operator’s exact run-page request. Viewer/agent projections contain only existence and answering identity/time.
- Status transitions use compare-and-set on serialized metadata and keep the original TTL. Passed, failed, sent
  and dropped rows are terminal; an already offered drafted result cannot be replaced. Claiming/scheduling is idempotent per source run/rule. Pending infrastructure can be retried; deterministic
  missing sources/configuration record named passes. A late collector cannot replace a dropped/sent draft.
- Retention is the deployment’s positive retention capped at 90 days; keep-forever uses 90 days. Inputs are bounded
  16 KiB, draft text 8192 bytes, at most 32 validated citations, metadata at most 16 KiB serialized, private output at most 64 KiB serialized,
  and a 5000-row index/read bound. Writers enforce the same byte limits before CAS as readers. Oversized inputs
  refuse instead of truncating. The private input includes captured project/source identity and config digest;
  each offer/send checks current project membership, configured forge root and the rule/standing-answer digest
  again. Worker pickup independently checks current root and account identity before any token mint, approval
  processing, comment/status update or paid admission; a changed identity refuses and an unreadable authority
  remains an infrastructure retry. Hostcase/trailing slashes normalize, base paths remain distinct.
- `/outbox/answer-draft.json` is trusted-tool structured output only. Host import checks exact shape, admissible
  categories/probabilities/coverage, real source IDs and scope/revisions against captured inputs and prepared SHA,
  plus its authenticated exit digest. Private bodies never enter logs, queue data, ordinary records, audit or state.
- A sent-draft mark follows a successful existing parked-answer enqueue, with exact source draft ID/digest and the
  edited/as-drafted disposition. Losing this mark reports incomplete accounting, never requeues the answer. Standing
  adoption is a separate person-confirmed atomic file edit and audit event, never an automatic send side effect.

## INT-AUTH-CONNECTIONS-FILE-CONTRACT

**Operator to owning worker and terminal CLI (#781).** `PI_AUTH_CONNECTIONS_FILE` is opt-in. Its owned regular
file is at most 65536 bytes and not group/other writable. Shape is version 1, `connections` (at most 32) and
`bindings` (supported provider to a declared connection id). Each row has validated `id`, `provider`, `adapter`
and `ownerHost`; community rows additionally name an absolute prepared `root` and lowercase SHA-256 `digest`.
Optional `quotaWindows` selects the displayed five-hour/seven-day account-window monitoring focus, default both.
Known exhausted windows remain visible and mandatory outside that focus; scoped and other windows remain
visible because they are not independently selectable. Optional positive safe-integer `extraUsageCreditMicros` authorizes a per-job conservative dollar
ceiling, and requires the job's normal dollar cap to fit. It is not a vendor credit balance. Supported adapters
are `openai-chatgpt`, `pi-anthropic-oauth@0.3.6` and `@gotgenes/pi-anthropic-auth@3.4.3`; source/dependency hashes and
audited transformations are held by `community-auth-pins.mjs` and `community-auth-patches.mjs`. Changing exact
source, dependency tree, root, profile or binding invalidates the old capability rather than widening it.

Competing reviewed Claude adapter packages visible in the staged manifest refuse as `auth-adapter-conflicting`
before quota claims, renewal or token mint. Arbitrary trusted factory registration conflicts are checked inside
the runner before provider dispatch. Final snapshot validation rechecks the stage root, digest and known
conflicts. A racing stage change prevents container start and retries as infrastructure with the ordinary
reservation refund.

The file selects authentication independently of analytics-only `subscriptions.json`. Unbound providers retain
legacy behavior. A bound provider never silently spends an environment key, another account or proxy after an
authentication, quota or availability failure. The first implementation accepts direct official OpenAI Responses
and Anthropic Messages endpoints, finite physical model lists and supported container-custody venues only;
unsupported classifier, OpenShell and canary routes refuse before spend. Auth management is terminal-only on
the owner, never a model-callable tool or browser credential form.

Version 1 rejects a finite set of executable routes that mixes bound subscription and unbound API billing
as `auth-mixed-billing`, including decision roles. A subscription primary cannot select an unbound API fallback.
Cross-provider fallback may use another explicitly bound subscription provider after all ordinary checks;
there is still one active connection per provider and no account rotation within an attempt. Claude's admitted
root runtime and children sharing that runtime are supported. Independent legacy Anthropic compatibility calls
and fresh runtimes without the admitted adapter refuse; only the root runtime's own internal reentry is allowed.
Separate pi CLI and Node child processes do not inherit attested subscription admission; subscription dispatch
from them refuses in the initial release, while child sessions sharing the root runtime retain its policy.

The safe host-status key is `dispatch:subscription-status:<host>` with a 90-second lifetime. Its writer and
reader share the connection and quota payload bounds: at most 32 connections, with 65,536 quota-record bytes
plus 16,384 projection bytes per connection (2,621,440 bytes total). Every supported window is retained;
excess or malformed publication is reported partial/unavailable rather than silently dropping exhaustion.
Private binding digests and generations are removed before publication. Browser presentation may bound the
combined host rows with an explicit partial/truncated indication.

## INT-SUBSCRIPTION-CREDENTIAL-STORE

**Owning host to access-only container (#781).** `PI_AUTH_STORE_DIR` defaults to `subscription-auth` beside the
settings file. The directory is owned mode 0700; credential rows are owned regular mode-0600 files, never links,
and the store is outside overlays, job roots and sandbox roots. Every local job also refuses a folder containing
the store as `local-folder-holds-subscription-auth`, independently of its model provider or authentication mode.
The worker checks before token minting and again at final local preparation against the resolved mount source;
future store paths resolve through existing or dangling symlink parents. Directory identity catches alternate
spellings. The private path is held only in host closures, never job data, environment or history. A connection row includes version, id, adapter,
provider, generation, local opaque account group, state, private credential and registration, and refresh time.
Refresh grants and access values are absent from queued data, history, telemetry, logs and command arguments.

A per-connection lock serializes login, renewal and logout. Atomic replacement and file/directory synchronization
persist a replacement before the transaction completes. A durable uncertain marker precedes token rotation;
an ambiguous remote or persistence result must not repeat that rotation blindly. Authentication/refresh failure
returns a closed actionable reason. Only named transient transport/store faults retry as infrastructure.

Host policy, credential-store and adapter-validation reads use the shared determinate-filesystem-error
allowlist. Missing or malformed policy/adapter metadata and determinate path faults return closed policy
refusals; credential-store absence still reads as disconnected. Permission/ownership validation remains a
policy refusal, while an unanswered read such as EACCES, EIO or an unknown errno is retryable infrastructure.
Dependency existence checks must propagate unanswered stat errors rather than certify a missing package.
The complete read boundary includes directory/file lstat, open, fstat, read and close; private paths and
credential text are removed from its diagnostics. These refusals never fall through to another credential.
If the default adapter's read-only validation fails after the durable refresh marker, its internal
`beforeRefresh` proof restores the exact pre-marker row before returning that refusal. No provider request
has begun in this branch. A provider error code alone supplies no such proof; terminal remote rejection and
ambiguous network rotation keep their existing disconnect or uncertain-marker outcomes.

An insufficient access lifetime with a known future earliest refresh instant defers as `subscription-auth`
before the uncertain marker or refresh network request. It spends no queue attempt. A quota/owner change found
during selected preparation uses the same closed free-delay path. The host releases all slot/endpoint holds
before moving the job, and checks cancellation before handing it back; no terminal run is recorded for a wait.

The prepared snapshot is host-private: provider, connection id, adapter, account group, generation, expiry,
deadline and the access-only environment map. Expiry must exceed deadline plus six minutes. Its provider binding
and generation are rechecked before use. The job's reserved `PI_SUBSCRIPTION_AUTH` contains profile/binding/expiry
metadata and prepared package root/digest, never refresh grants; access values use only the selected provider's
derived credential variables. Other credential sources cannot shadow that selection. A host-only
`subscriptionAuthRequired` image gate requires the `subscriptionAuth` capability before access preparation,
mint, clone or reservations; queued data cannot arm or disable it. An older image refuses as
`job-image-subscription-auth-unsupported`. The image proof exercises real receipt rejection, deadline/endpoint
checks and final shaped-body cost refusal under no network. Each supported profile also runs through the normal
entrypoint with a valid binding: its initial cost refusal must precede dispatch, and an offline synthetic 429
proves authoritative auth, final request shaping, bounded retry and signed subscription attribution. The runner validates
metadata and the exact package before provider calls, then holds the credential snapshot immutable. No auth
file or host credential directory is mounted. Ordinary subprocess, transcript and checkpoint redaction includes
every admitted access credential. A sandbox receives none.

Published host status is ephemeral, bounded and explicitly projected: configured connection id, provider,
profile, owner, active/state, expiry, last refresh, compatibility and quota evidence. It excludes private account
groups, credential generations, access/refresh values, raw profile/account data, headers and arbitrary diagnostics.
Missing or expired host telemetry stays unknown. Connections and Models consume this projection, not private files.

OpenAI and Claude access-token formats are validated at login, renewal and stored-row reads, before paid
admission. An API-key-shaped or malformed Claude bearer cannot be deferred to an in-container refusal.
Logout reports local disconnection and a separate `remoteRevocationConfirmed` boolean. Discarding a grant
whose adapter no longer matches cannot confirm remote revocation. Lifecycle diagnostics stay precise on
the terminal; job admission maps them to the closed actionable reason catalog.

## INT-SUBSCRIPTION-QUOTA-KEY

**Owning workers and terminal CLI to Valkey (#781).** `worker/src/subscription-quota.mjs` owns the parser and
store. `dispatch:subscription-quota:<sha256([connectionId, accountDigest, bucket])>` holds a closed JSON state
with monotonic version, owner/generation binding, source, observation time, normalized windows, extra-usage
facts and an optional one-attempt trial. Access tokens, email, profile names and provider prose are never stored.
The local account digest is an opaque account group, stable across renewal; no vendor-account deduplication of
separate connections is inferred. Physical model cooldown keys and their six-hour cap are UNCHANGED, checked.

- Observations have version 1, a closed source (`claude-community`, `openai`, `provider-error`), injected epoch-ms
  observation time, a completeness flag, normalized windows and typed extra usage. Each window has an opaque
  id, five-hour/seven-day/other kind, account/scoped scope, nullable measured percent and reset instant, and
  unknown/available/exhausted state. Community model display names are not silently mapped to physical models.
  Exhausted unmapped scoped limits conservatively block their application bucket. Null is unknown, never zero.
- Claude parses legacy five-hour/seven-day fields, modern `limits`, scoped legacy windows and `extra_usage`.
  OpenAI parses typed primary/secondary rate limits. Only closed authoritative transport codes establish an
  error observation; authentication, arbitrary error prose and overload do not. Percent and reset values are
  validated; resets beyond the 32-day evidence bound become unknown rather than an invented shorter reset.
- A payload/state is bounded to 65536 bytes, a community limits array to 32 and retained normalized windows to
  64. Reads use named keys, never keyspace scans. Observation freshness is five minutes; stale availability is
  unknown. Exhaustion remains authoritative through its full known reset, including a week. Without a reset it
  has no TTL and persists until newer sufficient evidence or a person's explicit trial. Missing/partial evidence
  does not erase it. A complete newer snapshot may clear generic unknown-reset error exhaustion.
- A measured Claude HTTP 429 invalidates cached availability and paid-overage facts before a bounded usage
  refresh; it does not alone prove plan exhaustion. The persistent probe-required flag permits read-only
  candidate inspection but refuses selected paid admission until new usage is recorded. The fetch binds its
  pre-network state version, so another worker's invalidation cannot be cleared by its old in-flight response.
  Known exhaustion survives invalidation. Missing/failed usage leaves the probe required without a guessed reset.
- Exact-byte Lua CAS serializes changes and one-trial claims, with at most eight bounded retries. Older
  observations, changed expected versions and stale owner/generation cannot overwrite newer evidence. Equal-time
  ties may only strengthen exhaustion, never clear it. A higher
  generation carries prior exhaustion forward. Candidate preview writes nothing; selected admission publishes
  the newer binding atomically. Store corruption, capacity and unavailable state fail loudly as infrastructure.
- Initial unknown quota permits ordinary admission only after the separate authentication and billing gates.
  Monitoring selections never disregard an observed exhausted applicable window. With several resets, all must
  clear. Enabled or unknown Claude paid extra usage requires explicit positive authorization and the compatible
  job dollar ceiling; missing vendor currency/scale is not assumed USD. Provider counters and API-equivalent
  conservative dollar accounting remain distinct.
- A person may grant one trial only against the observed version of unknown-reset exhaustion. Known resets,
  stale previews and model/agent requests cannot obtain it. Candidate checks do not consume it. Selected
  admission atomically binds it to a hash of the durable attempt id; repeating that same attempt is idempotent,
  another attempt refuses. Newer evidence revokes an outstanding trial. It starts no job and bypasses no other
  gate. `subscription-quota`/`subscription-owner` extend `INT-DEFER-REASON-KEY` without changing its fields/buckets.

The runner's signed provider-failure gains closed optional subscription-code and provider tokens; replay fields remain closed. The final shaped request may
increase its existing cost ticket only before dispatch; a larger/unboundable payload writes the closed
`final-payload` cost refusal. `INT-RUNNER-EXIT-CODE-PROTOCOL` and `INT-RUN-HISTORY-FILE-CONTRACT` add that one
`why` token; provider text, account identity, credentials and quota snapshots never become public run facts.
